topic: Diarrhoea and ORS
source_name: WHO - Diarrhoeal disease (fact sheet)
content: Diarrhoea makes the body lose water and salts. Oral rehydration solution (ORS) replaces them and is the main home treatment. Keep giving fluids and keep feeding, including breastfeeding for babies. Get medical help quickly if there is blood in the stool, high fever, signs of dehydration such as a very dry mouth, sunken eyes, very little urine or unusual sleepiness, or if the person cannot drink.

topic: Dengue prevention
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue (fact sheet)
content: Dengue spreads through bites of Aedes mosquitoes, which bite mainly in the daytime and breed in clean standing water in containers, coolers, tyres and water tanks. Prevent it by emptying and scrubbing water containers every week, covering water storage, using mosquito repellent, wearing full-sleeve clothes and using mosquito nets.

topic: Dengue warning signs
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue (fact sheet)
content: There is no specific medicine for dengue. Rest and drinking plenty of fluids help. Go to a hospital immediately if there is severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from the nose or gums, blood in vomit or stool, fast breathing, or unusual restlessness or weakness. Do not take medicines on your own; ask a doctor.

topic: Malaria
source_name: WHO - Malaria (fact sheet)
content: Malaria is spread by the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes. Common signs are fever, chills, headache and sweating, and the fever may come and go. A simple blood test at a health centre can confirm malaria, so get tested if you have fever. Sleep under a mosquito net, remove standing water near your home and cover your skin at dusk and night. Confusion, seizures or severe weakness with fever need emergency care.

topic: Myth: vaccines and autism
source_name: WHO - Vaccine safety (myths and facts)
content: Vaccines do not cause autism. Many large studies in different countries have found no link. Vaccines are tested for safety and protect children from serious diseases. Mild side effects such as a sore arm or a low fever can happen and usually go away quickly.

topic: Myth: antibiotics and viral fever
source_name: WHO - Antimicrobial resistance (fact sheet)
content: Antibiotics work only against bacteria. They do not work on viral illnesses such as the common cold, flu or most coughs. Using antibiotics when they are not needed can make germs resistant, so that the medicines stop working when they are really needed. Take antibiotics only when a doctor prescribes them.

topic: Handwashing
source_name: WHO - Hand hygiene guidance
content: Washing hands with soap and clean water helps prevent diarrhoea and many infections. Wash for at least 20 seconds: before eating or feeding a child, before cooking, after using the toilet, and after cleaning a child. Rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers and under the nails.

topic: Pregnancy danger signs
source_name: WHO - Maternal health (danger signs in pregnancy)
content: Go to a hospital immediately if a pregnant woman has vaginal bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, convulsions, severe stomach pain, high fever, trouble breathing, or if the baby moves much less than usual. Register the pregnancy early with your ASHA or ANM worker at the nearest health centre and attend regular antenatal check-ups.

topic: Childhood vaccination
source_name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare - Universal Immunisation Programme
content: Childhood vaccines protect against serious diseases such as measles, polio, tuberculosis, diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus and hepatitis B. Under the Universal Immunisation Programme, these vaccines are given free at government health facilities and immunisation sessions. Follow the schedule written on the child's Mother and Child Protection card and ask your ASHA or ANM worker for the dates.

topic: Tuberculosis
source_name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare - National TB Elimination Programme
content: A cough that lasts more than two weeks, with fever, night sweats, weight loss or blood in the sputum, can be a sign of tuberculosis (TB). TB is curable. Testing and treatment are free at government health facilities. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment and never stop it early, even if you feel better.

topic: Diabetes
source_name: WHO - Diabetes (fact sheet)
content: Common signs of diabetes are extreme thirst, passing urine often, tiredness, blurred vision and wounds that heal slowly. A blood test is needed to know for sure. Healthy eating, being active (about 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week for adults), avoiding tobacco and regular check-ups help. People with diabetes should keep taking their medicines as the doctor advised. Confusion, vomiting or fast breathing in a person with diabetes is an emergency.

topic: High blood pressure
source_name: WHO - Hypertension (fact sheet)
content: High blood pressure often has no signs, so have your blood pressure checked regularly. Eating less salt (under 5 grams a day), being active, avoiding tobacco and alcohol, and keeping a healthy weight help control it. If a doctor has prescribed medicine, keep taking it as advised. Severe headache, chest pain, weakness on one side of the body or trouble speaking need emergency care.

topic: Safe water in monsoon
source_name: WHO - Drinking-water (fact sheet)
content: During the rainy season, drink water that has been boiled or treated and store it in a clean, covered container. Wash hands before handling food, eat freshly cooked food, wash fruits and vegetables, and avoid walking or playing in flood water. These steps help prevent diarrhoea, typhoid and other water-borne diseases.

topic: Dengue fever symptoms and home care
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue
content: Dengue causes sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pain, and mild rash. Most recover with rest and plenty of oral fluids like coconut water, soups, and ORS. Paracetamol may be taken for fever under a doctor's advice, but avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, or pain medications as they increase bleeding risk. Seek hospital care immediately if warning signs appear.

topic: Dengue warning signs and critical phase
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue
content: The critical phase of dengue begins 3 to 7 days after fever onset, often when fever subsides. Warning signs of severe dengue include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding from gums or nose, vomiting blood, extreme fatigue, rapid breathing, and fluid accumulation. Severe dengue is a medical emergency requiring immediate hospitalization for intravenous fluids.

topic: Dengue mosquito breeding and prevention
source_name: National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC) India
content: Aedes mosquitoes that spread dengue bite primarily during daytime and breed in stagnant clean water. Prevent breeding by emptying, scrubbing, and drying water coolers, drums, flower vases, and discarded tires at least once every week. Keep all domestic water storage containers tightly covered, wear light-colored full-length clothing, and apply mosquito repellent.

topic: Malaria signs and diagnosis
source_name: WHO - Malaria fact sheet
content: Malaria symptoms include cyclical high fever, shaking chills, profuse sweating, headache, nausea, and body aches. In malaria-endemic areas like Odisha, every fever should be tested immediately using a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) or blood smear at the nearest government health center or by an ASHA worker. Early diagnosis prevents severe complications such as cerebral malaria.

topic: Malaria mosquito protection and bed nets
source_name: WHO - Malaria prevention guidelines
content: Anopheles mosquitoes that transmit malaria bite from dusk to dawn. Sleeping under Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) distributed through government health centers is the most effective prevention method. Use window meshes, eliminate open water pools around homes, and cooperate with public health indoor residual spraying (IRS) programs.

topic: Chikungunya symptoms and joint care
source_name: WHO - Chikungunya fact sheet
content: Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and causes acute fever accompanied by severe, debilitating joint pain, joint swelling, muscle pain, and headache. While joint pain usually subsides in weeks, it can persist for months in older adults. Care involves adequate rest, drinking plenty of liquids, and gentle joint mobilization once acute fever resolves.

topic: Japanese Encephalitis awareness
source_name: NCVBDC India - Japanese Encephalitis
content: Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is a viral brain infection spread by Culex mosquitoes breeding in rice paddies and waterlogged areas, often involving pigs and birds as hosts. Symptoms include high fever, severe headache, stiff neck, confusion, and seizures. Prevention includes routine child vaccination under the Universal Immunization Programme, using mosquito nets, and segregating pig shelters from dwellings.

topic: Filariasis and elephantiasis prevention
source_name: WHO - Lymphatic filariasis
content: Lymphatic filariasis, or elephantiasis, is spread by mosquito bites and causes painful, abnormal swelling of limbs and genitals. It is completely preventable by taking the annual Mass Drug Administration (MDA) preventative tablets distributed free by health workers during government campaigns. Practicing good limb hygiene and skin care prevents secondary infections in affected individuals.

topic: Diarrhoea and dehydration management
source_name: WHO - Diarrhoeal disease fact sheet
content: Diarrhoea causes dangerous rapid loss of water and electrolytes. The primary home intervention is Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) solution combined with continued feeding and breastfeeding. Immediate medical consultation is required if stool contains blood, fever is high, the person cannot drink, has sunken eyes, dry tongue, or stops producing urine.

topic: ORS preparation and correct usage
source_name: UNICEF - Managing diarrhoea with ORS and Zinc
content: To prepare standard ORS: mix the entire contents of one WHO-approved ORS packet into exactly 1 litre of clean boiled and cooled drinking water. Stir thoroughly until fully dissolved. Do not add sugar, salt, milk, or fruit juice to the mixture. Use the prepared solution within 24 hours; discard any remaining fluid after 24 hours and prepare a fresh batch.

topic: Zinc supplementation in childhood diarrhoea
source_name: WHO - Clinical management of acute diarrhoea
content: Zinc supplementation for children with acute diarrhoea reduces the duration and severity of the episode and protects against recurrent episodes for up to 2 to 3 months. As per national guidelines, give 20 mg of zinc daily (10 mg for infants under 6 months) for 14 full days along with ORS, even if the diarrhoea stops before 14 days.

topic: Cholera warning signs and rapid rehydration
source_name: WHO - Cholera fact sheet
content: Cholera is an acute intestinal infection caused by consuming food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae bacteria. It causes profuse, painless watery diarrhoea resembling rice-water and rapid vomiting. Extreme dehydration can cause shock within hours. Start oral rehydration immediately and transport the patient to a hospital without delay for intravenous fluids.

topic: Typhoid fever causes and prevention
source_name: WHO - Typhoid fact sheet
content: Typhoid is a bacterial infection spread through food and water handled by infected individuals or contaminated with sewage. Symptoms include prolonged high fever, headache, stomach pain, loss of appetite, and constipation or diarrhoea. Prevention requires drinking boiled or filtered water, eating hot thoroughly cooked foods, washing hands before eating, and typhoid conjugate vaccination.

topic: Jaundice and viral hepatitis A and E care
source_name: WHO - Hepatitis A and E guidance
content: Viral hepatitis A and E cause acute liver inflammation transmitted through fecal-contaminated water and food, especially during monsoons. Symptoms include yellowing of eyes and skin (jaundice), dark urine, pale stools, fatigue, nausea, and right-upper abdominal discomfort. Management includes complete rest, hydration, avoiding oily foods and alcohol, and strict water purification.

topic: Safe water purification in monsoon and flood seasons
source_name: WHO - Drinking water quality guidelines
content: During floods or monsoons, groundwater and piped sources often get contaminated. Boil drinking water at a rolling boil for at least 1 minute before cooling. Alternatively, treat with chlorine (halazone) water purification tablets distributed by health workers. Store drinking water in clean, covered vessels with a narrow mouth or a tap to prevent hand contact.

topic: Food poisoning and prevention
source_name: WHO - Food safety fact sheet
content: Food poisoning occurs after eating food spoiled by bacteria, toxins, or parasites. Symptoms include vomiting, crampy abdominal pain, fever, and diarrhoea. Prevent it by practicing the 5 keys to safer food: keep clean, separate raw meat from cooked foods, cook thoroughly above 70°C, keep food at safe temperatures, and use safe water and fresh raw ingredients.

topic: Antenatal check-up (ANC) schedule and MCP card
source_name: MoHFW India - Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)
content: Every pregnant woman should register her pregnancy early at the nearest Anganwadi or Sub-Center and obtain a Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card. She must attend at least 4 comprehensive Antenatal Care (ANC) visits for blood pressure, blood glucose, weight monitoring, tetanus toxoid (Td) immunization, and ultrasound screening to detect high-risk pregnancy early.

topic: Pregnancy danger signs requiring emergency care
source_name: WHO - Maternal health: danger signs in pregnancy
content: Seek immediate emergency hospital care (call 108) if a pregnant woman experiences: vaginal bleeding, severe headache with blurred vision, convulsions (fits), high fever, severe persistent abdominal pain, reduced or absent fetal movements in the third trimester, swelling of face and hands, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge.

topic: Anemia in pregnancy and iron folic acid tablets
source_name: MoHFW India - Anemia Mukt Bharat Guidelines
content: Anemia during pregnancy increases risk of maternal exhaustion, hemorrhage, and low birth weight. Pregnant women must take 1 Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) red tablet daily for at least 180 days starting from the second trimester (after 12 weeks), followed by 180 days postpartum. Take IFA with water or citrus fruit after meals; avoid tea or milk immediately after as they hinder iron absorption.

topic: Maternal nutrition and weight gain
source_name: National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) India - Dietary Guidelines
content: A pregnant woman needs an additional 350 calories and extra protein daily. Her diet should feature green leafy vegetables, lentils, pulses, milk, eggs, nuts, and seasonal fruits. Adequate weight gain (typically 10 to 12 kg during full term) indicates healthy fetal development. Rest for at least 2 hours in the afternoon and sleep on the left side to optimize blood flow to the placenta.

topic: Postpartum care and warning signs after delivery
source_name: WHO - Postnatal care for mothers and newborns
content: The first 42 days after childbirth require close monitoring. Seek urgent emergency care if the new mother has heavy vaginal bleeding (soaking more than one pad per hour), large clots, fever with foul discharge, severe calf pain, high blood pressure, or extreme sadness and detachment from the baby (postpartum depression).

topic: Exclusive breastfeeding in the first 6 months
source_name: WHO - Infant and young child feeding
content: Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of birth. The first milk, colostrum, is rich in antibodies and acts as the baby's first natural vaccine. Practice exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 full months—do not give water, gripe water, honey, or animal milk. Exclusive breastfeeding provides all nutrients, water, and immune defense an infant needs.

topic: Complementary feeding after 6 months
source_name: UNICEF - Feeding your baby: 6-12 months
content: At 6 completed months, breast milk alone is no longer sufficient. Introduce soft, clean, nutrient-dense complementary foods while continuing breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond. Begin with mashed khichdi with vegetables, mashed dal, pureed fruits, and boiled eggs. Increase consistency, variety, and frequency as the child grows.

topic: National immunization schedule: Birth to 1 year
source_name: MoHFW India - Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)
content: Under India's Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), vaccines given free at government centers are: At birth: BCG, OPV-0, Hepatitis B birth dose. At 6, 10, and 14 weeks: Pentavalent (DPT+HepB+Hib), Rotavirus, bOPV, fIPV, and PCV. At 9-12 months: MR (Measles-Rubella) 1st dose, JE-1 (in endemic districts), PCV booster, and Vitamin A dose 1.

topic: Child immunization booster schedule
source_name: MoHFW India - Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)
content: Booster vaccinations ensure lifelong protection against infectious killers: At 16-24 months: MR 2nd dose, DPT booster-1, bOPV booster, and JE-2. At 5-6 years: DPT booster-2. At 10 years and 16 years: Tetanus and adult Diphtheria (Td) vaccine. Keep your child's immunization card safe and present it at every health visit.

topic: Childhood pneumonia recognition and fast breathing
source_name: WHO - Pneumonia in children
content: Pneumonia is a leading infectious killer of children under 5. Danger signs include cough accompanied by fast breathing and chest indrawing (the lower chest pulls inward when inhaling). In infants 2 to 11 months, 50 or more breaths per minute is fast breathing; in children 12 to 59 months, 40 or more breaths per minute. Take the child to a hospital immediately.

topic: Childhood malnutrition and SAM warning signs
source_name: WHO - Malnutrition fact sheet
content: Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) occurs when a child is very thin for their height or has bilateral pitting edema (swelling of both feet). Children with SAM have compromised immunity and high mortality risk. Anganwadi centers screen children using Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tapes. Children with red MUAC (<115 mm) need admission to a Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC).

topic: Heatstroke symptoms and first aid during summers
source_name: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) India - Heat Wave Guidelines
content: Heatstroke (Loo) is life-threatening when body temperature rises above 40°C (104°F) during summer heatwaves. Symptoms include hot dry skin, absence of sweating, confusion, dizziness, seizures, and loss of consciousness. Immediate first aid: move person to shade or cool room, loosen clothing, spray cool water on body, place ice packs on armpits and groin, fan vigorously, and call 108 ambulance.

topic: Heat exhaustion prevention in hot weather
source_name: NDMA India - Beat the Heat Guidelines
content: To prevent heat illness during Odisha summer peaks: drink water frequently even when not feeling thirsty, carry water when traveling, consume homemade cooling drinks like ORS, lemon water, buttermilk, and torani (rice water). Avoid direct sunlight between 11 AM and 3:30 PM, wear loose light cotton clothing, use umbrellas or hats, and never leave children or pets in parked vehicles.

topic: Snakebite emergency protocol: Dos and Don'ts
source_name: WHO - Snakebite envenoming guidelines
content: DO: Keep patient calm, completely immobilize the bitten limb using a splint or sling (like a fracture), remove rings and tight jewelry, and transport immediately to a government hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV). DONT: Do NOT cut, suck venom, apply tourniquets or tight bands, apply ice, herbal pastes, or visit faith healers. Anti-Snake Venom is the only proven cure.

topic: Dog bite first aid and rabies post-exposure prophylaxis
source_name: WHO - Rabies fact sheet
content: Rabies is 100% fatal once clinical symptoms develop, but 100% preventable with prompt post-exposure care. Immediate action after any dog, cat, or monkey bite/scratch: wash the wound vigorously under running water with soap for at least 15 continuous minutes. Apply povidone-iodine antiseptic. Do not apply chili, lime, or bandage tightly. Visit a hospital immediately for Anti-Rabies Vaccine (ARV) and Immunoglobulin.

topic: Burn first aid: Thermal and scald burns
source_name: WHO - Burns fact sheet
content: Immediate burn first aid: cool the burn wound under clean, gentle running tap water for at least 10 to 20 minutes. Remove non-adherent clothing and jewelry before swelling begins. Do NOT use ice, ice water, toothpaste, butter, mud, or oil on burns. Do not burst blisters. Cover loosely with a clean, dry cloth and seek medical evaluation.

topic: Electric shock emergency first aid
source_name: Red Cross & National Safety Council
content: In case of electric shock: do NOT touch the victim directly with bare hands while they are in contact with the electrical source. Turn off the main switch immediately, or separate the victim using a dry wooden stick or dry plastic. Check breathing once safe; if unconscious and not breathing, begin CPR chest compressions immediately and call 108 ambulance.

topic: Tuberculosis symptoms and free government treatment
source_name: MoHFW India - National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP)
content: Any cough persisting for more than 2 weeks, accompanied by fever (especially in evening), night sweats, weight loss, or blood in sputum, is suspected tuberculosis (TB). Sputum microscopy, CBNAAT/TrueNat testing, and anti-TB medications are provided 100% free at all government primary health centres. TB is completely curable if the full treatment course is completed without skipping doses.

topic: Asthma triggers, management, and inhalers
source_name: WHO - Asthma fact sheet
content: Asthma is a chronic lung disease causing episodes of wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing. Common triggers include smoke, dust mites, biomass fuel smoke from cooking, pollen, cold air, and respiratory viral infections. Inhaler medications are safe, deliver medicine directly to lungs with minimal body side effects, and are not addictive.

topic: Common cold versus influenza (flu) signs
source_name: WHO - Influenza (seasonal)
content: A common cold develops gradually with runny nose, sneezing, and mild sore throat. Influenza (flu) hits suddenly with high fever, severe body aches, fatigue, dry cough, and headache. Antibiotics do not cure either cold or flu. Most flu cases resolve with bed rest, hydration, and paracetamol. High-risk individuals (elderly, pregnant, diabetics) should consult a doctor if breathing difficulties arise.

topic: Type 2 diabetes warning signs and screening
source_name: WHO - Diabetes fact sheet
content: Common signs of type 2 diabetes include excessive thirst (polydipsia), frequent urination especially at night (polyuria), unexplainable weight loss, constant hunger, blurred vision, and slow-healing cuts or sores. Many people have no symptoms early on. Everyone over age 30 should have a fasting blood glucose test annually at their nearest health and wellness centre.

topic: Diabetes lifestyle management and foot care
source_name: International Diabetes Federation (IDF) - Guidelines
content: Managing diabetes requires balanced eating with whole grains and legumes, avoiding sugary drinks and refined sweets, maintaining 30 minutes of daily physical exercise, and taking prescribed medicines consistently. Inspect feet daily for cuts, blisters, or redness, as diabetes impairs nerve sensation and wound healing. Never walk barefoot.

topic: Hypertension (high blood pressure) silent symptoms
source_name: WHO - Hypertension fact sheet
content: Hypertension is called a silent killer because it often has no warning symptoms until severe damage occurs. Left uncontrolled, it leads to heart attacks, stroke, and kidney failure. Normal blood pressure is under 120/80 mmHg. Have blood pressure measured at least twice a year. If diagnosed, take prescribed antihypertensive tablets every day without skipping.

topic: Dietary salt reduction for cardiovascular health
source_name: WHO - Salt reduction guidelines
content: Excess dietary salt raises blood pressure and increases cardiovascular disease risk. WHO recommends consuming less than 5 grams of salt (about 1 level teaspoon) per day for adults. Reduce salt by avoiding processed snacks, papads, pickles, and salty chips, not adding table salt at meals, and seasoning foods with lemon, herbs, and spices instead.

topic: Recognizing stroke symptoms: FAST protocol
source_name: American Stroke Association & WHO
content: A stroke occurs when blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted. Remember FAST: F - Face drooping on one side. A - Arm weakness or numbness when raised. S - Speech difficulty, slurred words, or trouble repeating a simple sentence. T - Time to call 108 ambulance immediately. Getting to a hospital within 3 to 4.5 hours of symptom onset saves brain tissue and prevents permanent paralysis.

topic: Heart attack warning signs and emergency response
source_name: WHO - Cardiovascular diseases fact sheet
content: Common heart attack symptoms include intense chest pain, tightness, or pressure in the center of the chest that may spread to the jaw, neck, back, or left arm, accompanied by cold sweating, shortness of breath, nausea, and lightheadedness. In women and diabetics, it can present atypical symptoms like burning in upper stomach and fatigue. Call 108 immediately and do not drive yourself.

topic: Iron deficiency anemia signs and iron-rich foods
source_name: MoHFW India - Anemia Mukt Bharat
content: Anemia symptoms include pale conjunctiva, brittle nails, chronic fatigue, shortness of breath during exertion, dizziness, and poor concentration in children. Combat anemia by eating iron-rich foods: drumstick leaves (moringa), spinach, jaggery (gud), chana (chickpeas), lentils, liver, and eggs. Consume vitamin C-rich foods (amla, lemon, guava) alongside meals to double iron absorption.

topic: Correct handwashing technique and critical times
source_name: WHO - Hand hygiene guidelines
content: Washing hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds reduces diarrhoea risk by nearly 50% and respiratory infections by 25%. Wash at 5 critical times: before cooking or handling food, before eating or feeding a child, after using the toilet, after cleaning a child's bottom, and after touching sick individuals or waste.

topic: Deworming tablets and National Deworming Day
source_name: MoHFW India - National Deworming Day
content: Intestinal parasitic worms (helminths) cause chronic malnutrition, anemia, and stunted physical and cognitive development in children. Under the National Deworming Day (NDD), chewable Albendazole tablets (400 mg) are distributed free twice a year at schools and Anganwadis to all children aged 1 to 19 years. Good sanitation and wearing footwear prevent re-infection.

topic: Myth: Antibiotics cure common cold and flu
source_name: WHO - Antimicrobial resistance (AMR)
content: Antibiotics kill bacteria, but have zero effect against viruses. Colds, runny noses, viral fevers, and the flu are caused by viruses. Taking antibiotics for viral illnesses does not make you recover faster, can cause side effects like diarrhoea, and accelerates antibiotic resistance, making medicines ineffective when needed for severe bacterial infections. Use antibiotics only when prescribed by a doctor.

topic: Myth: Vaccines cause autism or infertility
source_name: WHO - Vaccine safety: Myths and facts
content: Extensive scientific studies involving millions of children worldwide have conclusively disproven any link between vaccines and autism or infertility. Vaccines are among the most rigorously tested medical interventions in human history and save over 4 million lives globally each year from deadly diseases like measles, polio, and tetanus. Mild fever or local soreness after vaccination is normal.

topic: Myth: Starving a fever or withholding food during illness
source_name: WHO - Integrated Management of Childhood Illness
content: The belief that sick or febrile patients should be denied food is harmful. The immune system requires more energy, protein, and fluids when fighting off infections. Continue feeding soft, digestible, nourishing foods (khichdi, curd, soups) in frequent small portions throughout illnesses, and never withhold water or breast milk.

topic: Tele-MANAS free mental health helpline India
source_name: MoHFW India - National Tele Mental Health Programme
content: Tele-MANAS is the Government of India's toll-free, 24/7 mental health helpline available at 14416 or 1800-891-4416. It provides free, confidential psychological counseling in Odia, Hindi, English, and regional languages for stress, anxiety, depression, exam stress, and emotional crises with trained mental health professionals.

topic: Recognizing common depression and anxiety signs
source_name: WHO - Depressive disorder fact sheet
content: Depression involves persistent sadness, emptiness, loss of interest in activities, sleep disruption, extreme fatigue, changes in appetite, feelings of worthlessness, and difficulty concentrating lasting more than 2 weeks. Depression is a medical condition, not a personal weakness. Professional counseling, lifestyle modifications, and medical support provide effective recovery.

topic: Common headache types and home relief
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Tension-type headaches and dehydration headaches are very common. They feel like a constant dull ache or tight band around the forehead or back of the head. Relief includes drinking 2-3 glasses of water, resting in a quiet dark room, applying a cool or warm cloth to forehead or neck, and avoiding prolonged phone or computer screen exposure. Consult a doctor if headaches become frequent or severe.

topic: Headache red flags and danger signs
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Seek immediate medical care for a headache if it is sudden and severe (thunderclap headache), accompanied by high fever and stiff neck (suspected meningitis), confusion, speech difficulty, weakness or numbness on one side of face or body, vision loss, or following a recent head injury.

topic: Migraine symptoms and triggers
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Migraine is a recurrent headache disorder causing moderate-to-severe throbbing or pulsating pain, usually on one side of the head, worsened by routine physical activity. It is often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light and sound. Common triggers include lack of sleep, skipping meals, stress, bright lights, and loud noises. Resting in a quiet, dark room and staying hydrated helps.

topic: Red spot on skin, irritation, and insect bites
source_name: WHO - Managing common skin conditions
content: A red, irritating spot on the neck or skin is often caused by an insect or ant bite, localized contact dermatitis from soap or jewelry, or mild heat irritation. Home care: wash gently with clean water and mild soap, apply a cold compress or ice pack wrapped in a cloth to soothe itching, and avoid scratching to prevent bacterial infection. If the spot spreads, develops pus, causes fever, or does not improve in 3-4 days, see a doctor.

topic: Prickly heat and heat rash (Ghamori)
source_name: National Health Portal (NHP) India - Heat rash guidelines
content: Heat rash (prickly heat or miliaria) occurs during hot, humid weather when sweat ducts become blocked. It presents as tiny red bumps or blisters causing intense itching and prickling sensations, common on the neck, chest, back, and skin folds. Care: stay in cool, well-ventilated areas, take cool baths, wear loose lightweight cotton clothing, and avoid heavy oils or greasy creams that clog sweat pores.

topic: Fungal skin infection and ringworm (Daad)
source_name: WHO - Control of fungal and parasitic skin infections
content: Ringworm (tinea) is a fungal infection appearing as an itchy, red, circular ring with raised scaly borders on the neck, groin, underarms, or body. Fungi thrive in warm, sweaty skin folds. Keep skin clean and dry, change sweaty clothes daily, do not share towels or soap, and use antifungal cream prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist for the full duration. Avoid topical steroid creams as they worsen fungal spread.

topic: Scabies symptoms and household treatment
source_name: WHO - Scabies fact sheet
content: Scabies is a contagious skin infestation caused by microscopic mites that burrow into the skin. It causes severe, intense itching that is noticeably worse at night, with small red bumps or tracks between fingers, wrists, armpits, and waist. Because it spreads through close contact, all household members and sexual partners must be treated simultaneously. Wash bedding and clothes in hot water.

topic: Skin boils and bacterial infections (Furruncle / Pus boils)
source_name: WHO - Managing skin infections
content: Boils are painful, pus-filled bumps caused by bacterial infection of hair follicles. Apply a warm, moist washcloth for 10-15 minutes 3-4 times a day to encourage natural drainage and relieve pain. Never squeeze, pop, or pierce a boil with needles, as this spreads bacteria into deeper tissues or the bloodstream. If boils are on the face, multiply, cause fever, or fail to heal, consult a doctor.

topic: Eczema and dry itchy skin care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dermatitis guidance
content: Eczema (atopic dermatitis) causes dry, cracked, inflamed, and intensely itchy patches of skin, often behind knees, elbows, neck, and face. Protect the skin barrier by taking short lukewarm baths with mild non-perfumed soap, applying coconut oil or gentle moisturizer immediately after bathing while skin is still damp, wearing soft cotton clothes, and avoiding scratching.

topic: Acidity, acid reflux and heartburn (GERD)
source_name: National Health Portal India - Acidity management
content: Acidity and heartburn cause a burning sensation in the chest and upper stomach, sour burps, and acid taste in the mouth. Relieve acidity by drinking cool water or cold milk, eating smaller frequent meals, avoiding spicy, deep-fried, oily foods and caffeine, avoiding lying down immediately after meals (wait at least 2 hours), and elevating the head of the bed slightly.

topic: Stomach pain and abdominal cramp triage
source_name: WHO - Clinical guidelines on acute abdominal pain
content: Mild stomach cramps from gas or indigestion often ease with sips of warm water, ginger tea, and resting. Warning signs of serious abdominal emergencies include sudden severe sharp pain (especially in lower right abdomen indicating appendicitis), vomiting blood, high fever, rigid hard belly, yellowing eyes, or pain so severe one cannot stand. Seek immediate hospital care.

topic: Constipation relief and high-fiber diet
source_name: National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) India - Dietary fiber
content: Constipation causes hard, dry, infrequent stools and straining. Promote bowel regularity naturally by drinking at least 8-10 glasses of water daily, eating high-fiber foods such as whole wheat roti, green vegetables, dal with skin, oats, papaya, and guavas, and engaging in 30 minutes of daily brisk walking. Avoid excessive tea, coffee, and refined flour (maida).

topic: Gas, bloating, and indigestion (Flatulence)
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive wellness
content: Excessive intestinal gas and bloating occur from swallowing air, eating too quickly, carbonated drinks, or hard-to-digest legumes and raw foods. Helpful measures include chewing food thoroughly and unhurriedly, taking a gentle 15-minute walk after eating, drinking warm carom seed (ajwain) or cumin (jeera) water, and limiting chewing gum and fizzy drinks.

topic: Nausea and vomiting home care
source_name: WHO - Managing acute gastroenteritis and dehydration
content: When experiencing vomiting, do not drink large amounts of water at once, as this triggers further vomiting. Rest the stomach for 30 minutes, then take tiny sips (1-2 teaspoons) of cold water, ORS, or clear broth every 5 minutes. If fluids are tolerated, progress to bland foods like toast, plain rice, and banana. Seek urgent medical care if unable to keep fluids down for over 24 hours, vomiting blood, or experiencing severe dizziness.

topic: Sore throat and tonsillitis home care
source_name: WHO - Acute respiratory infections guidance
content: A sore, scratchy, painful throat is usually caused by common viral respiratory infections. Soothe it by gargling with warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in warm water) 3-4 times daily, sipping warm water with honey and ginger, staying well-hydrated, and resting the voice. Consult a doctor if you have high fever, severe difficulty swallowing saliva, or swollen white patches on tonsils.

topic: Dry cough versus wet chesty cough care
source_name: WHO - Respiratory illness home management
content: A dry cough is tickly and unproductive; soothe it with warm herbal teas, honey (for children over 1 year), and steam inhalation. A wet cough brings up mucus; drink plenty of warm liquids to thin the secretions and help clear the chest. Any cough lasting longer than 2 weeks, or coughing with blood or night sweats, requires sputum testing for tuberculosis at a government health center.

topic: Nasal congestion and sinus headache relief
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sinusitis and congestion
content: Blocked nose, facial pressure, and forehead heaviness from sinusitis or cold can be managed with plain steam inhalation for 10 minutes twice a day, using saline nasal drops, drinking warm fluids, and sleeping with the head elevated. Avoid sudden exposure to cold air and dust. If sinus pain is severe with high fever or swelling around eyes, consult a doctor.

topic: Conjunctivitis (Eye Flu / Red Eye) care and prevention
source_name: WHO - Prevention of blindness and eye infections
content: Conjunctivitis causes red, bloodshot eyes, sticky discharge, tearing, itching, and crusting of eyelids upon waking. Highly contagious: wash hands frequently with soap, do not touch or rub eyes, avoid sharing towels, pillows, or handkerchiefs. Clean eyelids gently with a clean cotton ball soaked in boiled and cooled water. Consult an eye doctor or health worker for appropriate medicated eye drops; never use leftover drops.

topic: Earache and ear discharge precautions (Kan Pakiba)
source_name: WHO - Deafness and hearing loss: Ear care
content: Earache or pus discharge from the ear is often due to middle ear infection (otitis media) or water entering the ear canal. Crucial rule: NEVER insert hairpins, matchsticks, safety pins, or mustard oil into the ear, as this can tear the eardrum and cause permanent hearing loss. Keep the ear strictly dry while bathing. See a doctor for examination and medical treatment.

topic: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) and burning sensation
source_name: WHO - Urinary tract infections management
content: UTI causes burning or stinging during urination, frequent urge to pass small amounts of urine, lower abdominal cramping, and cloudy or strong-smelling urine. Home care: drink plenty of clean water (at least 3-4 liters daily) to flush bacteria out of the urinary tract. Women should wipe from front to back after using the toilet. Consult a doctor for a urine test and prescription antibiotics if burning persists or fever develops.

topic: Kidney stones warning signs and hydration
source_name: National Health Portal India - Renal calculi
content: Kidney stones cause sharp, severe cramping pain in the back and flank, radiating down to the groin, often with nausea and blood in urine. Prevention: drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily to keep urine clear or pale yellow, reduce salt intake, and avoid excessive animal protein. Severe intractable pain, inability to pass urine, or fever with chills requires immediate emergency care.

topic: Mouth ulcers and canker sores home care (Gha)
source_name: WHO - Oral health fact sheet
content: Mouth ulcers are small, painful white or yellow sores on the inside of lips, cheeks, or tongue. They often arise from accidental biting, stress, nutritional deficiency (vitamin B12, iron), or sharp teeth. Soothe with warm salt water rinses, applying honey or coconut oil, drinking cool fluids, and avoiding spicy, acidic, or rough foods. Most heal within 7-10 days. Any mouth ulcer lasting over 2-3 weeks must be examined by a doctor to rule out oral lesions.

topic: Toothache and gum swelling first aid
source_name: WHO - Oral health fact sheet
content: A toothache is usually caused by dental caries (cavities), plaque buildup, or gum infection. First aid: gently rinse the mouth with warm salt water, floss to dislodge trapped food particles, and apply a drop of clove oil on a small cotton swab directly to the sore tooth. Do not place aspirin directly on the gums as it causes chemical burns. Visit a dentist for cavity filling or root treatment.

topic: Lower back pain and posture care
source_name: WHO - Low back pain fact sheet
content: Non-specific low back pain is usually caused by muscle strain from heavy lifting, poor sitting posture, or prolonged standing. Care: stay gently active rather than bed-bound, apply warm compress to tight muscles, avoid heavy lifting or sudden bending, and maintain an upright spine when sitting. Warning signs requiring urgent medical attention: back pain accompanied by leg numbness, loss of bladder control, or high fever.

topic: Sprains, ankle twists, and RICE first aid
source_name: Red Cross & National Safety Council - Musculoskeletal injuries
content: For acute sprains and joint twists, use the R.I.C.E protocol: Rest the injured joint, Ice with a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15-20 minutes at a time, Compress with an elastic crepe bandage to control swelling, and Elevate the limb above heart level when resting. Do not apply hot balm or massage vigorously in the first 48 hours. If the person cannot bear any weight on the foot, get an X-ray to rule out fracture.

topic: General fever home care and sponging (Jwara)
source_name: WHO - Integrated management of fever
content: Fever is the body's natural immune defense fighting an infection. Home care: rest in a well-ventilated room, wear lightweight clothes, drink plenty of fluids (water, dal water, tender coconut water, ORS), and do not wrap in heavy blankets. If body temperature is high, sponge with normal tap water (not cold or ice water) on forehead, neck, and limbs. If fever persists over 48-72 hours or is accompanied by rash, seizures, or breathing difficulty, see a doctor.

topic: Weakness, fatigue, and low energy causes
source_name: National Health Portal India - Fatigue and nutritional deficiency
content: Persistent fatigue and tiredness commonly stem from inadequate sleep, dehydration, nutritional deficiencies (anemia/low hemoglobin, vitamin D, vitamin B12), stress, or recovering from recent viral illness. Boost recovery with 7-8 hours of sleep, drinking 2-3 liters of water, eating balanced meals with green vegetables, sprouts, milk, and eggs, and spending 20 minutes in morning sunlight. Have blood tested if exhaustion persists for weeks.

topic: Dizziness, lightheadedness and orthostatic hypotension
source_name: WHO - Clinical guidelines on cardiovascular and neurological signs
content: Feeling dizzy or lightheaded upon standing quickly often happens when blood pressure drops temporarily (orthostatic hypotension) or from mild dehydration, skipped meals, or low blood sugar. When feeling dizzy: sit or lie down immediately with legs elevated, take slow deep breaths, and drink water or sweet electrolyte fluid. Stand up gradually from sitting or lying positions. If dizziness causes fainting, chest pain, or slurred speech, seek emergency care.

topic: Red spot on skin, neck irritation, and insect or ant bites
source_name: WHO - Managing common skin conditions
content: A single red, irritating spot on the neck or skin is often caused by an insect bite, localized contact dermatitis from soap, laundry detergent, perfume, or jewelry, or mild heat friction. Home Care: Clean the area gently with water and mild soap. Apply a cool compress or an ice cube wrapped in cloth for 10 minutes to reduce inflammation and itching. Calamine lotion or aloe vera gel can soothe irritation. Avoid scratching to prevent secondary bacterial infection. Warning Signs: If the spot spreads rapidly, develops a bullseye ring, oozes yellow pus, causes fever, or does not improve in 3 to 4 days, consult a doctor.

topic: Prickly heat, heat rash (Miliaria / Ghamori)
source_name: National Health Portal India - Heat rash guidelines
content: Prickly heat happens during hot and humid weather when sweat ducts become clogged, trapping perspiration beneath the skin. Symptoms include tiny itchy red bumps or clear blisters, prickling or stinging sensations, most common on the neck, chest, back, and skin folds. Home Care: Stay in well-ventilated, shaded, or cool rooms. Take cool water baths. Wear loose-fitting, breathable cotton clothes. Keep skin dry. Avoid thick oil massages or heavy greasy creams that further block pores. Seek medical advice if rashes show signs of bacterial infection such as pus or warmth.

topic: Ringworm, fungal skin infections (Tinea / Daad)
source_name: WHO - Fungal skin disease management
content: Ringworm is a contagious fungal infection that appears as an itchy, circular red rash with slightly raised, scaly borders and clearer skin in the middle. Commonly affects the neck, groin (jock itch), armpits, feet (athlete's foot), and scalp. Home Care: Keep the affected skin clean and completely dry, especially after bathing. Wear fresh cotton underwear and loose clothing. Do not share personal towels, bedsheets, combs, or clothes. Apply doctor-recommended antifungal creams for the full prescribed duration. Avoid steroid creams like Betnovate without prescription as steroids cause fungi to spread aggressively.

topic: Scabies intense nocturnal itching and household spread
source_name: WHO - Scabies fact sheet
content: Scabies is an infestation of the skin by microscopic mites that burrow into the upper layer of the skin. Symptoms include intense, severe itching that worsens significantly at night, with tiny pimple-like rashes or thin wavy burrow lines between fingers, inner wrists, elbows, armpits, and waistline. Care: Scabies is highly contagious through direct skin contact. All members of the household must be treated simultaneously with anti-parasitic lotion prescribed by a health worker. Wash all bedding, towels, and clothing used in the last 4 days in hot water and sun-dry thoroughly.

topic: Skin boils, furuncles, and bacterial pus bumps
source_name: WHO - Management of bacterial skin infections
content: A boil is a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump under the skin caused by bacterial infection of hair follicles (usually Staphylococcus). Home Care: Apply a warm, moist cloth or compress for 10-15 minutes 3-4 times a day to increase circulation and encourage natural drainage. Wash hands before and after touching the area. NEVER squeeze, pierce, or cut a boil yourself, as this can force the infection into deeper tissue or the bloodstream. Seek urgent medical care if boils appear on the face, multiply into a cluster (carbuncle), cause fever, or fail to drain after 10 days.

topic: Eczema, atopic dermatitis and chronic dry skin
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eczema care
content: Eczema is a non-contagious inflammatory skin condition causing dry, red, cracked, and intensely itchy skin patches, frequently on the inner elbows, back of knees, neck, and hands. Home Care: Take short lukewarm baths using mild, fragrance-free soaps. Apply pure coconut oil, petroleum jelly, or prescribed emollient moisturizer immediately after bathing while the skin is still damp. Avoid known triggers such as harsh detergents, wool fabrics, and stress. Keep fingernails trimmed short to avoid skin damage from scratching.

topic: Hives, urticaria and acute allergic skin flare-ups
source_name: WHO - Management of allergic emergencies
content: Hives (urticaria) are raised, red or skin-colored, itchy welts that appear suddenly on the skin, often triggered by food allergies, insect stings, viral infections, or medication reactions. Home Care: Apply cool damp cloths to soothe the itch, take a cool bath, and wear loose clothing. Avoid hot water, scratching, and tight belts. Danger Signs: If hives occur with facial or lip swelling, difficulty breathing, throat tightness, or dizziness (anaphylaxis), seek emergency hospital care immediately as this is life-threatening.

topic: Dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis scalp care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Scalp health
content: Dandruff involves flaking of dead skin cells from the scalp, often accompanied by mild itching. Seborrheic dermatitis is a more severe form with greasy yellowish scales and redness on the scalp, eyebrows, and sides of the nose. Care: Wash hair regularly with anti-dandruff shampoo containing zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole, or selenium sulfide. Leave medicated shampoo on the scalp for 5 minutes before rinsing. Avoid excessive heavy hair oils that feed the Malassezia yeast.

topic: Acne, facial pimples and adolescent breakout care
source_name: WHO - Adolescent health guidelines
content: Acne develops when oil glands and dead skin cells clog pores, allowing bacteria to multiply. Causes include hormonal fluctuations, stress, and pore-clogging cosmetics. Care: Wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and lukewarm water. Do not pop, pick, or scrub pimples roughly, as this leads to permanent scarring and infection spread. Use non-comedogenic (water-based) moisturizers and sunscreen. Consult a doctor for stubborn cystic acne.

topic: Sunburn protection and UV damage first aid
source_name: WHO - Ultraviolet radiation and sun protection
content: Sunburn occurs from excessive ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure, causing red, warm, painful, and tender skin that may peel after a few days. First Aid: Get out of the sun immediately. Cool the skin with cold water compresses or take a cool bath. Apply aloe vera gel or calamine. Drink plenty of water to prevent dehydration. Do not pop blisters. Protect skin outdoors with wide-brimmed hats, sunglasses, and umbrellas.

topic: Warts (HPV) skin growth care and precautions
source_name: National Health Portal India - Viral skin lesions
content: Common warts are harmless, rough, grainy skin growths caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in the top skin layer. They are common on fingers, hands, and feet (plantar warts). Care: Avoid picking, scratching, or shaving over warts to prevent spreading them to other body areas. Keep feet dry and wear slippers in public bathrooms and pools. Consult a health worker or dermatologist for topical treatments or cryotherapy if painful.

topic: Corns and calluses foot friction management
source_name: International Diabetes Federation - Diabetic foot care
content: Corns and calluses are thick, hardened layers of skin that develop when your skin tries to protect itself against repeated friction and pressure, usually from ill-fitting shoes or prolonged standing. Care: Wear properly fitting, cushioned shoes with wide toe boxes. Soak feet in warm water for 15 minutes, then gently rub calluses with a pumice stone. Never cut corns with razor blades or sharp knives at home. People with diabetes must never treat foot corns themselves due to ulcer risks.

topic: Tension headache and dehydration headache home relief
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Tension-type headaches and dehydration headaches feel like a steady, dull ache or tight vise-like band gripping the forehead, temples, or base of the neck. Common causes include mental stress, eye fatigue from screens, skipped meals, lack of sleep, or inadequate water intake. Home Relief: Drink 2 to 3 large glasses of clean water immediately. Rest in a dark, quiet, cool room. Apply a cool or warm cloth across the forehead and back of the neck. Gently massage temple and shoulder muscles. Take regular screen breaks.

topic: Migraine symptoms, visual aura and trigger prevention
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Migraine causes moderate to severe throbbing, pulsating pain typically on one side of the head, exacerbated by movement, climbing stairs, or bright light. May be preceded by visual auras (flashing lights, zigzag lines). Often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and extreme sound sensitivity. Prevention & Care: Identify triggers (strong smells, skipping meals, caffeine withdrawal, lack of sleep). Lie down in a dark, silent room with a cold forehead pack. Consult a physician for preventive therapy if migraines happen weekly.

topic: Headache red flags requiring immediate emergency hospital care
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders emergency triage
content: Seek urgent emergency medical care (call 108) for a headache if it strikes suddenly with maximal intensity in seconds (thunderclap headache), is accompanied by high fever and stiff neck with chin unable to touch chest (meningitis), or comes with confusion, slurred speech, facial drooping, one-sided body weakness, sudden vision loss, or follows head trauma.

topic: Sinus headache and facial pressure relief
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sinusitis
content: Sinus headaches cause a dull, throbbing pressure and aching around the forehead, cheekbones, bridge of the nose, and behind the eyes, which worsens when bending forward. Usually accompanies a cold or sinus infection with nasal discharge. Care: Inhale plain steam twice daily. Use warm compresses over the sinuses. Drink warm liquids and stay hydrated. Consult a doctor if facial swelling, high fever, or vision changes occur.

topic: Dizziness, lightheadedness and postural hypotension
source_name: WHO - Clinical management of cardiovascular and neurological signs
content: Dizziness upon standing up quickly occurs when blood pressure drops momentarily (orthostatic hypotension), or from mild dehydration, hunger, or heat fatigue. Care: Sit or lie down immediately with legs slightly raised. Take slow deep breaths. Sip water or oral rehydration fluids. Avoid jumping out of bed suddenly; sit on the edge for 1 minute before standing. Seek medical checkup if fainting, heart palpitations, or blackouts occur.

topic: Vertigo, spinning sensation and inner ear balance
source_name: WHO - Deafness and hearing care: Balance disorders
content: Vertigo creates a false sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning or tilting, often accompanied by nausea, loss of balance, and vomiting. It is frequently caused by inner ear balance issues (like BPPV or labyrinthitis). Care: Sit still immediately during a spinning episode in good lighting. Avoid sudden head turns, bending down, or looking upward. Sleep with head slightly elevated. Consult an ENT specialist or neurologist for diagnosis and vestibular exercises.

topic: Stroke emergency warning signs: FAST protocol
source_name: American Stroke Association & WHO
content: A stroke happens when blood flow to the brain is blocked or a brain vessel ruptures. Immediate recognition saves lives using the FAST test: F - Face drooping on one side. A - Arm weakness or inability to keep both arms raised. S - Speech difficulty, slurred words, or inability to repeat a simple sentence. T - Time to call 108 ambulance immediately. Do not wait for symptoms to improve; clot-busting treatment must be given within 4.5 hours.

topic: Tremors, shaky hands and neurological awareness
source_name: WHO - Neurological disorders public health challenges
content: Hand tremors can be temporary and harmless due to excess caffeine, anxiety, physical exhaustion, low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), or fever chills. Persistent tremors that occur at rest, during handwriting, or progress over months warrant medical evaluation to rule out essential tremor, thyroid abnormalities, or Parkinson's disease.

topic: Acidity, acid reflux and heartburn relief (GERD)
source_name: National Health Portal India - Acidity management
content: Acidity occurs when stomach acid flows back into the food pipe (esophagus), causing a burning sensation behind the breastbone, sour burping, and upper stomach burning. Causes include eating heavy spicy meals, sleeping right after dinner, smoking, and excess tea or coffee. Home Relief: Drink a glass of cold water or cold milk. Eat smaller, frequent meals. Avoid lying down for at least 2 hours after eating. Elevate the head end of your bed. Limit oily fried snacks, pickles, and carbonated sodas.

topic: Acute stomach pain, abdominal cramps and emergency red flags
source_name: WHO - Clinical management of acute abdominal emergencies
content: Mild stomach cramps from gas or indigestion often subside with warm sips of water, ginger tea, and rest. Red Flags: Seek emergency hospital care immediately if abdominal pain is sudden, excruciating, localized to the lower right abdomen (suspected appendicitis), accompanied by vomiting blood, black tarry stools, high fever, rigid board-like belly, or severe dizziness.

topic: Constipation relief, bowel regularity and high-fiber nutrition
source_name: National Institute of Nutrition India - Dietary fiber guidelines
content: Constipation involves infrequent, hard, dry bowel movements with painful straining. Relief: Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of water daily. Increase dietary fiber by eating whole-wheat roti, oats, dal with skin, green vegetables, papaya, and guavas. Engage in 30 minutes of physical walking daily. Do not suppress the natural urge to defecate. Avoid dependency on chemical laxatives without medical advice.

topic: Intestinal gas, flatulence and abdominal bloating
source_name: National Health Portal India - Gastrointestinal wellness
content: Abdominal bloating and gas build-up occur from swallowing air while eating too quickly, drinking fizzy sodas, or bacterial fermentation of undigested carbohydrates in the gut. Care: Chew food slowly with closed mouth. Take a gentle 15-minute walk after meals. Drink warm carom seed (ajwain) or cumin (jeera) water. Limit chewing gum and carbonated drinks. Seek evaluation if bloating is accompanied by unexplained weight loss.

topic: Nausea and vomiting rehydration protocol
source_name: WHO - Diarrhoeal disease and vomiting management
content: Vomiting causes rapid loss of fluids and stomach electrolytes. Home Care: Rest the stomach for 30 minutes after vomiting. Then take small sips (1-2 teaspoons) of cold water, ORS solution, or clear broth every 5 minutes. Do not drink large volumes at once. Once fluids are tolerated, progress to bland foods like rice, toast, and bananas. Seek urgent medical care if vomiting blood, unable to keep water down for 24 hours, or having signs of severe dehydration.

topic: Diarrhoea treatment with Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and fluids
source_name: WHO - Diarrhoeal disease fact sheet
content: Diarrhoea is the passage of 3 or more loose or watery stools per day, causing dehydration. The cornerstone of treatment is Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) combined with continued feeding and breastfeeding. Do not starve the patient. Consult a doctor immediately if there is blood in the stool, high fever, sunken eyes, dry mouth, skin that does not bounce back when pinched, or inability to drink.

topic: Proper ORS preparation steps and volume guidelines
source_name: UNICEF - Managing diarrhoea with ORS
content: To prepare standard WHO-ORS: wash hands thoroughly, pour the entire contents of 1 packet of ORS into exactly 1 litre of clean drinking water (boiled and cooled). Stir well until completely dissolved. Do not add sugar, salt, milk, or fruit juice. Drink small sips frequently throughout the day. Discard any leftover solution after 24 hours and prepare a fresh batch.

topic: Food poisoning signs, contaminated food, and recovery
source_name: WHO - Food safety fact sheet
content: Food poisoning occurs from consuming food contaminated with infectious bacteria, viruses, or toxins. Symptoms start within hours and include nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, and mild fever. Care: Rest, drink ORS and coconut water to prevent dehydration, and eat simple khichdi or bananas when ready. Seek immediate hospital care if high fever, severe bloody stool, or extreme weakness occurs.

topic: Hemorrhoids, piles symptoms and bowel strain prevention
source_name: National Health Portal India - Hemorrhoids
content: Piles (hemorrhoids) are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus, causing painless bright red bleeding during bowel movements, anal itching, or painful lumps around the anus. Care: Prevent hard stools by eating high-fiber foods and drinking plenty of water. Take a warm sitz bath (sit in warm plain water for 15 minutes twice daily). Avoid straining on the toilet. Seek medical examination to rule out other causes of rectal bleeding.

topic: Jaundice, viral hepatitis and liver inflammation care
source_name: WHO - Hepatitis A and E fact sheets
content: Jaundice presents with yellowing of the white of the eyes and skin, dark mustard-colored urine, pale stools, fatigue, and loss of appetite, often from viral Hepatitis A or E spread through contaminated food and water. Care: Complete physical rest, drink boiled water, eat light non-oily carbohydrates (rice, glucose, fruit juices), and strictly avoid alcohol and heavy oils. Visit a doctor for liver function tests (LFT).

topic: Sore throat, tonsil pain and warm saline gargling
source_name: WHO - Acute respiratory infections
content: A sore, scratchy throat is usually caused by viral infections like the common cold. Care: Gargle with warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in warm water) 3 to 4 times a day to reduce throat swelling. Sip warm water with honey and ginger. Avoid cold drinks and smoking. See a doctor if there is high fever, difficulty swallowing saliva, or white patches on the tonsils.

topic: Dry cough vs wet productive cough home management
source_name: WHO - Respiratory health guidance
content: A dry cough is hacking and produces no phlegm; soothe it with steam inhalation and warm honey drinks. A wet cough produces mucus; drink plenty of warm water and broths to thin secretions so they can be cleared easily. Crucial Rule: Any cough persisting for more than 2 weeks must be evaluated for tuberculosis at a government health center.

topic: Common cold vs influenza (Flu) differentiation
source_name: WHO - Influenza (seasonal)
content: A cold develops gradually with a runny nose, sneezing, and mild throat irritation. Influenza (flu) hits abruptly with high fever, severe body and muscle aches, chills, fatigue, and dry cough. Antibiotics do not work against cold or flu viruses. Care: Bed rest, plenty of warm fluids, and paracetamol for body aches. Seek medical care if breathing becomes labored.

topic: Asthma wheezing, breathlessness and inhaler usage
source_name: WHO - Asthma fact sheet
content: Asthma is a chronic condition causing inflammation and narrowing of the airways, with symptoms of wheezing (whistling sound when breathing), chest tightness, and shortness of breath. Triggers include dust mites, smoke, pollen, cold air, and exercise. Care: Inhaler medications deliver tiny doses directly to the lungs, are safe, and do not cause addiction. Keep your prescribed reliever inhaler accessible at all times.

topic: Childhood pneumonia danger signs: Fast breathing and chest indrawing
source_name: WHO - Pneumonia in children
content: Pneumonia is a serious lung infection. In young children, warning signs include cough with fast breathing and chest indrawing (the lower chest pulls inward when the child breathes in). In infants 2 to 11 months, fast breathing is 50+ breaths/minute; in children 1 to 5 years, it is 40+ breaths/minute. Take the child to a hospital immediately.

topic: Tuberculosis symptoms and free government treatment (NTEP)
source_name: MoHFW India - National TB Elimination Programme
content: Tuberculosis (TB) is an airborne bacterial infection. Symptoms: cough lasting more than 2 weeks, evening fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, and blood in sputum. Sputum testing and complete multi-drug anti-TB treatment are provided 100% free under India's National TB Elimination Programme. TB is completely curable if medicines are taken consistently without stopping early.

topic: Conjunctivitis, red eye, eye flu care and prevention
source_name: WHO - Prevention of blindness and eye infections
content: Conjunctivitis causes red, bloodshot eyes, sticky yellowish discharge, gritty feeling, tearing, and crusted eyelids in the morning. It spreads rapidly through contact with eye discharge. Care: Wash hands frequently with soap. Do not touch or rub eyes. Clean eyelids gently with a clean cotton ball soaked in boiled and cooled water. Do not share towels, pillows, or eye cosmetics. Consult an eye doctor for antibiotic or anti-allergic eye drops.

topic: Eye strain, computer vision fatigue and 20-20-20 rule
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye care
content: Staring at mobile phones or computer screens for hours causes dry eyes, blurred vision, eye fatigue, and headaches. Protect vision with the 20-20-20 rule: Every 20 minutes, look at an object at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Blink frequently, adjust screen brightness, and ensure good room lighting. If blurred vision persists, have eyes checked by an optometrist.

topic: Earache, ear discharge precautions (Kan Pakiba)
source_name: WHO - Deafness and hearing loss: Ear care
content: Ear pain or pus discharge typically results from middle ear infection or fungal growth from moisture. Crucial Warning: NEVER insert matchsticks, hairpins, safety pins, or mustard oil into the ear. These can perforate the eardrum and cause permanent hearing loss. Keep the ear dry during bathing. Consult a doctor for an otoscopic examination and medicated ear drops.

topic: Mouth ulcers, canker sores home care (Mukha Gha)
source_name: WHO - Oral health fact sheet
content: Mouth ulcers are painful small white or red sores on the inner lips, cheeks, or tongue, triggered by stress, accidental biting, hot/spicy foods, or vitamin B12 and iron deficiency. Care: Rinse with warm salt water. Apply honey or coconut oil to soothe the sore. Eat cool, non-spicy, soft foods. Most ulcers heal within 7 to 10 days. Warning: Any ulcer that persists beyond 3 weeks must be examined by a doctor to rule out oral lesions.

topic: Toothache and cavity first aid care
source_name: WHO - Oral health fact sheet
content: Toothache is usually caused by tooth decay (cavities), plaque buildup, or pulp infection. First Aid: Rinse gently with warm salt water. Floss carefully to remove trapped food debris. Place a drop of clove oil on a cotton swab and apply directly to the painful tooth for natural numbing. Do not put aspirin directly on gums. Visit a dentist promptly for cavity filling or root canal care.

topic: Nosebleed (Epistaxis) emergency first aid: Lean forward
source_name: Red Cross First Aid Guidelines
content: To stop a nosebleed: Sit upright and lean slightly forward (do NOT tilt head back, as blood flows down the throat and causes choking or vomiting). Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly with thumb and index finger for 10 full minutes without releasing. Breathe through the mouth. Apply a cold ice pack to the bridge of the nose. If bleeding continues past 20 minutes, seek emergency medical care.

topic: Urinary tract infection (UTI) burning urination care
source_name: WHO - Urinary tract infections management
content: UTI causes burning or stinging pain during urination, frequent urgent need to pass small amounts of urine, and lower abdominal discomfort. Common in women due to a shorter urethra. Care: Drink 3 to 4 liters of clean water daily to flush bacteria out. Urinate frequently without holding. Wipe from front to back after using the toilet. See a doctor for a urine test and prescription antibiotics if burning persists or fever develops.

topic: Kidney stones prevention and hydration
source_name: National Health Portal India - Renal calculi
content: Kidney stones cause severe, sharp cramping pain in the back and side, radiating downward to the lower abdomen and groin, often with nausea and blood in urine. Prevention: Drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily to keep urine pale and clear, reduce excessive dietary salt, and eat a balanced diet. Severe uncontrollable pain, fever with chills, or inability to pass urine requires urgent hospital care.

topic: Type 2 diabetes warning signs and screening
source_name: WHO - Diabetes fact sheet
content: Diabetes causes high blood sugar. Warning signs: frequent urination (especially at night), excessive thirst, constant hunger, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision, and slow-healing cuts. Many have no symptoms early on. Everyone over age 30 should have a fasting blood sugar test annually at a primary health centre. Maintain 30 minutes of daily exercise and a whole-grain diet.

topic: Hypertension (High blood pressure) silent symptoms
source_name: WHO - Hypertension fact sheet
content: Hypertension is called a silent killer because it often produces no symptoms until severe damage to the heart, brain, or kidneys occurs. Normal blood pressure is under 120/80 mmHg. Have blood pressure measured at least twice a year. Keep blood pressure controlled by reducing salt intake to under 5g/day, staying physically active, managing weight, and taking prescribed medicines daily without skipping.

topic: Lower back pain and posture care
source_name: WHO - Low back pain fact sheet
content: Back pain is commonly caused by muscle strain from heavy lifting, poor sitting posture, or prolonged standing. Care: Stay gently active rather than bed-bound. Apply a warm compress to tight muscles. Avoid sudden bending or twisting. Sit with proper lower back support. Warning Signs: Seek urgent medical care if back pain is accompanied by leg numbness, loss of bladder control, or fever.

topic: Ankle sprain and joint injury RICE first aid
source_name: Red Cross First Aid Guidelines
content: For sudden joint twists or sprains, follow the R.I.C.E protocol: Rest the injured joint, Ice with a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15-20 minutes, Compress with an elastic crepe bandage to support the joint, and Elevate the limb above heart level when resting. Do not apply hot balm or massage vigorously during the first 48 hours. If the foot cannot bear any weight, get an X-ray to check for fractures.

topic: Joint pain, arthritis and knee stiffness in older adults
source_name: WHO - Musculoskeletal health fact sheet
content: Osteoarthritis causes joint stiffness (especially in the morning), swelling, and aching in the knees and hips, worsening with prolonged walking. Care: Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce knee strain. Engage in low-impact exercises like walking, swimming, or cycling. Apply warm compresses for stiffness and cold packs for swelling. Consult a doctor for physiotherapy and pain management.

topic: Dengue fever symptoms and home hydration care
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue
content: Dengue causes sudden high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital eye pain, severe joint and muscle pain, and mild rash. Transmitted by daytime Aedes mosquitoes. Care: Bed rest and abundant fluid intake (ORS, tender coconut water, dal soup). Paracetamol can be taken for fever under medical advice, but avoid aspirin and ibuprofen as they increase bleeding risks. Monitor closely for warning signs.

topic: Dengue critical phase warning signs and hospitalization
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue
content: The critical phase of dengue occurs when the fever starts subsiding (days 3-7). Danger signs of severe dengue: severe continuous abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding from gums or nose, vomiting blood, extreme restlessness, cold clammy skin, or difficulty breathing. Severe dengue is a medical emergency requiring immediate hospitalization for intravenous fluids.

topic: Malaria fever chills and blood smear testing
source_name: WHO - Malaria fact sheet
content: Malaria causes cyclical high fever with violent shivering chills, profuse sweating, and body aches. Transmitted by night-biting Anopheles mosquitoes. In endemic areas like Odisha, every fever should be tested immediately using a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) or blood smear by an ASHA worker or at a primary health centre. Sleep under Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs).

topic: Chikungunya joint swelling and mosquito protection
source_name: WHO - Chikungunya fact sheet
content: Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and causes acute fever accompanied by severe, debilitating joint pain and swelling, headache, and fatigue. While fever lasts a few days, joint pain can linger for weeks. Care: Rest, hydration, and gentle joint mobilization once fever subsides. Prevent mosquito breeding by emptying standing water in coolers and flower pots weekly.

topic: Heatstroke (Loo) emergency first aid in Odisha summers
source_name: National Disaster Management Authority India - Heat wave guidelines
content: Heatstroke is a life-threatening medical emergency when body temperature rises above 40°C (104°F) during summer heatwaves. Symptoms: hot dry skin, absence of sweating, confusion, dizziness, seizures, and loss of consciousness. First Aid: Move person to shade or cool room immediately, loosen clothing, spray cool water on body, place ice packs on armpits and groin, fan vigorously, and call 108 ambulance without delay.

topic: Snakebite emergency protocol: DOs and DON'Ts
source_name: WHO - Snakebite envenoming guidelines
content: DO: Keep patient calm, completely immobilize the bitten limb using a splint or sling (like a fracture), remove rings and tight jewelry, and transport immediately to a hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV). DONT: Do NOT cut, suck venom, apply tourniquets or tight bands, apply ice, herbal pastes, or visit faith healers. Anti-Snake Venom is the only proven cure.

topic: Dog bite first aid and rabies post-exposure prophylaxis
source_name: WHO - Rabies fact sheet
content: Rabies is 100% fatal once symptoms appear, but 100% preventable with prompt post-exposure care. Immediate action after any dog, cat, or monkey bite/scratch: wash the wound vigorously under running water with soap for at least 15 continuous minutes. Apply povidone-iodine antiseptic. Do not apply chili, lime, or bandage tightly. Visit a hospital immediately for Anti-Rabies Vaccine (ARV) and Immunoglobulin.

topic: Burn first aid: Thermal and scald burns
source_name: WHO - Burns fact sheet
content: First Aid for burns: Cool the burn wound under clean, gentle running tap water for at least 10 to 20 minutes. Remove non-adherent clothing and jewelry before swelling begins. Do NOT use ice, toothpaste, butter, mud, or oil on burns. Do not burst blisters. Cover loosely with a clean, dry cloth and seek medical evaluation.

topic: Anemia in pregnancy and Iron Folic Acid (IFA) tablets
source_name: MoHFW India - Anemia Mukt Bharat Guidelines
content: Anemia during pregnancy increases risk of maternal exhaustion, hemorrhage, and low birth weight. Pregnant women must take 1 Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) red tablet daily for at least 180 days starting from the second trimester, followed by 180 days postpartum. Take IFA with water or citrus fruit after meals; avoid tea or milk immediately after as they hinder iron absorption.

topic: Red spot on neck, insect bite, ant bite, friction rash, collar irritation
source_name: WHO - Managing common skin conditions
content: A single red spot or irritating bump on the neck, face, or skin is commonly caused by an insect bite, ant sting, localized contact dermatitis from perfumes, laundry soap, or friction from tight clothing. Home Care: Clean the area gently with cool water and mild soap. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth or cold towel for 10 minutes to soothe itching and reduce swelling. Apply calamine lotion or pure aloe vera gel. Do not scratch or pinch the spot to avoid secondary bacterial infection. Warning Signs: If redness spreads quickly, develops a circular bullseye ring, oozes yellow pus, causes facial swelling, or if you develop fever, seek medical evaluation at a Community Health Centre.

topic: Prickly heat, heat rash, miliaria, ghamori, sweat bumps
source_name: National Health Portal India - Heat rash guidelines
content: Prickly heat happens during hot and humid weather when sweat ducts become clogged, trapping perspiration beneath the skin. Symptoms include tiny itchy red bumps, stinging sensation, and clear superficial vesicles on the neck, chest, back, and skin folds. Home Care: Stay in well-ventilated, shaded, or cool rooms. Take cool water baths without harsh scrubbing. Wear loose, lightweight cotton clothing. Keep skin dry. Avoid thick oil massages, heavy petroleum jelly, or greasy ointments that further block pores. Warning Signs: If bumps become swollen, drain yellow pus, or remain painful after 5 days, consult a health worker.

topic: Ringworm, fungal rash, tinea corporis, tinea cruris, daad, circular itchy patch
source_name: WHO - Fungal skin disease management
content: Ringworm is a contagious fungal skin infection presenting as a ring-shaped, itchy red rash with slightly raised, scaly borders and clearer skin in the center. Commonly found on the neck, arms, groin (jock itch), and thighs. Home Care: Wash and dry the area completely with a dedicated clean towel. Wear loose, dry, breathable cotton underwear and clothes. Do not share towels, bedsheets, or clothing. Apply prescribed topical antifungal cream consistently for 2 weeks. Never apply steroid creams like Betnovate, as steroids make fungal infections grow uncontrollably. Warning Signs: Seek a clinic doctor if the rash spreads over large body areas or develops open sores.

topic: Scabies, night itching, skin mites, burrows between fingers, khujli
source_name: WHO - Scabies fact sheet
content: Scabies is an intensely itchy parasitic skin infestation caused by microscopic Sarcoptes scabiei mites burrowing into the skin. Hallmark symptoms include severe itching that becomes unbearable at night, tiny pimple-like bumps, and thin grayish burrow lines between fingers, wrists, elbows, armpits, and waist. Home Care: Scabies is highly contagious; all members of the household must receive simultaneous anti-parasitic treatment prescribed by an ASHA worker or doctor. Wash all clothes, bedsheets, and towels in hot water and sun-dry thoroughly. Keep nails clipped short. Warning Signs: Extensive crusted skin or secondary bacterial infection requires immediate clinic attention.

topic: Skin boil, furuncle, carbuncle, pus-filled lump, baltoad
source_name: WHO - Management of bacterial skin infections
content: A skin boil is a painful, warm, swollen lump filled with pus caused by bacterial infection of a hair follicle, usually from Staphylococcus bacteria. Home Care: Apply a warm, moist cloth compress for 10-15 minutes 3 to 4 times daily to boost blood flow and encourage gentle natural drainage. Wash hands before and after touching the area. NEVER squeeze, press, or puncture a boil at home, as this pushes bacteria into deep tissues and the bloodstream.
