Warning Signs: Seek medical care immediately if boils appear on the central face or nose, cluster together into a carbuncle, or cause fever and red streaks.

topic: Eczema, atopic dermatitis, dry itchy patches, skin peeling
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eczema care
content: Atopic dermatitis or eczema is a chronic, non-contagious inflammatory skin condition causing dry, itchy, red, and cracked skin patches, often on inner elbows, behind knees, hands, and face. Home Care: Take short lukewarm baths using mild soap-free cleansers. Within 3 minutes of bathing, gently pat skin and apply a liberal layer of plain coconut oil or petroleum jelly to lock in moisture. Wear smooth 100% cotton clothes. Avoid harsh detergents, wool, and strong fragrances. Warning Signs: If cracked skin starts oozing yellow liquid, forms golden crusts, or becomes hot and tender, visit a clinic for antibiotic evaluation.

topic: Hives, urticaria, sudden allergic itchy welts, skin wheals
source_name: WHO - Guidelines on allergic emergencies
content: Hives (urticaria) are raised, itchy, reddish or skin-colored welts that appear suddenly, often triggered by allergic reactions to food, viral infections, insect bites, or medications. Home Care: Apply cool damp cloths to relieve itching. Take a cool shower and wear loose clothing. Avoid hot water, rubbing, alcohol, and known allergy triggers. Warning Signs: If hives are accompanied by swelling of the lips, tongue, or eyelids, difficulty breathing, throat tightness, or lightheadedness, call 108 or go to emergency immediately for anaphylaxis.

topic: Dandruff, flaky itchy scalp, seborrheic dermatitis
source_name: National Health Portal India - Scalp health
content: Dandruff is characterized by flaking of dead scalp skin cells, often with mild to moderate itching, linked to the Malassezia yeast. Seborrheic dermatitis causes greasy, yellowish flakes with redness along the scalp, eyebrows, and nose creases. Home Care: Wash hair regularly with anti-dandruff shampoo containing zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole, or selenium sulfide. Leave the lather on the scalp for 5 minutes before rinsing. Avoid applying heavy mustard or mineral oils which feed yeast. Warning Signs: Consult a doctor if the scalp develops bleeding sores, severe swelling, or hair loss.

topic: Acne vulgaris, pimples, blackheads, whiteheads, facial breakouts
source_name: WHO - Adolescent health guidelines
content: Acne develops when oil glands and dead skin cells clog pores, allowing bacteria (Cutibacterium acnes) to multiply and cause inflammation. Home Care: Wash the face twice daily with lukewarm water and a gentle cleanser. Do not pick, pop, or scrub pimples roughly, which causes scarring and deep cysts. Use non-comedogenic, oil-free moisturizers and water-based sunscreen. Keep hair clean and away from the face. Warning Signs: Severe cystic painful nodules under the skin require prescription topical retinoids or oral therapy from a dermatologist.

topic: Athlete's foot, tinea pedis, peeling itchy skin between toes
source_name: WHO - Fungal infections
content: Athlete's foot is a fungal infection between the toes causing macerated white peeling skin, intense itching, burning, and unpleasant odor. Home Care: Wash feet daily with soap and dry thoroughly, especially between every toe. Wear clean, dry cotton socks and change them if feet sweat. Alternate footwear so shoes dry completely. Apply prescribed antifungal powder or cream. Avoid walking barefoot in public communal showers. Warning Signs: If feet develop redness that spreads up the leg, fever, or pus, seek clinic evaluation.

topic: Cracked heels, heel fissures, painful dry feet
source_name: National Health Portal India - Foot health
content: Cracked heels (heel fissures) happen when dry, thickened skin around the heel rim splits under body weight pressure. Common with barefoot walking or open sandals. Home Care: Soak feet in warm water for 15 minutes, gently rub dead skin with a pumice stone, dry thoroughly, and apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly or urea cream, then wear clean cotton socks overnight. Drink adequate water throughout the day. Warning Signs: If you have diabetes or if cracks bleed, become red, warm, or infected, see a doctor promptly.

topic: Contact dermatitis, soap allergy, watch strap rash, nickel allergy
source_name: WHO - Occupational and environmental skin diseases
content: Contact dermatitis is an itchy, red rash caused by direct skin contact with an irritant or allergen, such as nickel jewelry, wrist watch straps, detergents, poison ivy, or hair dyes. Home Care: Immediately wash the skin with mild soap and cool water to remove residual substances. Stop using the suspected cosmetic, detergent, or metal item. Apply cold wet compresses and calamine lotion. Warning Signs: If the rash affects the eyes, face, or genital area, or if blisters burst with severe oozing, visit a health centre.

topic: Psoriasis, silvery scaly skin plaques, thick red patches
source_name: WHO - Global report on psoriasis
content: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition where skin cells multiply rapidly, causing thick, red patches covered with silvery-white scales, commonly on elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back. Home Care: Keep skin constantly moisturized with heavy fragrance-free creams or petroleum jelly. Take short lukewarm baths and avoid harsh scrubbing. Moderate gentle sunlight exposure can help under medical guidance. Avoid skin injuries, stress, and smoking. Warning Signs: If plaques become generalized, painful, or accompanied by swollen, painful joints (psoriatic arthritis), consult a physician.

topic: Vitiligo, white patches on skin, loss of skin pigment, safed daag
source_name: National Health Portal India - Vitiligo guidelines
content: Vitiligo is an autoimmune disorder where the immune system destroys melanocytes (pigment-producing cells), leading to smooth, pale white patches on the skin, face, hands, or lips. It is completely non-contagious. Home Care: Protect white skin patches from sun exposure by wearing protective clothing and applying sunscreen, as depigmented skin burns easily. Eat a balanced nutritious diet. Avoid self-medicating with unproven caustic chemical pastes. Consult a dermatologist for safe medical repigmentation therapies.

topic: Sunburn, peeling red skin, UV damage, sun exposure pain
source_name: WHO - Ultraviolet radiation health risks
content: Sunburn occurs from excessive exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, leading to red, hot, painful skin that may develop small blisters and peel after several days. Home Care: Get out of direct sun immediately. Take cool showers or place cold wet compresses on burned areas. Apply pure aloe vera gel or calamine lotion. Drink extra water to avoid dehydration. Never peel loose skin or pop blisters. Warning Signs: Severe blistering over large areas, high fever, chills, dizziness, or confusion indicates severe heat illness requiring hospital care.

topic: Common warts, plantar warts, HPV skin bumps, verruca
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin warts
content: Warts are rough, non-cancerous skin growths caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in the top skin layer, commonly occurring on hands, fingers, and soles of feet (plantar warts). Home Care: Do not pick, bite, scratch, or cut warts with razor blades, as this spreads the virus to other areas and causes severe infections. Keep feet dry. Wear sandals in shared showers. Over-the-counter salicylic acid patches can be used under pharmacy guidance. Warning Signs: Seek clinic evaluation if warts become painful, bleed, change appearance, or occur on genitals.

topic: Corns and calluses, hardened friction pads on toes and soles
source_name: International Diabetes Federation - Diabetic foot care
content: Corns and calluses are thickened layers of dead skin developed in response to repeated friction and pressure, usually from ill-fitting footwear or prolonged walking. Home Care: Wear comfortable shoes with adequate toe room and soft cushioning. Soak feet in warm water for 10-15 minutes, then gently buff with a pumice stone. Apply moisturizing cream. Never slice or cut corns with knives or blades at home. Warning Signs: People with diabetes must never treat foot corns themselves due to severe ulcer and gangrene risks; consult a foot clinic.

topic: Ingrown toenail, painful red swelling beside big toe, onychocryptosis
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail disorders
content: An ingrown toenail occurs when the edge of the toenail curves into the surrounding skin fold, causing throbbing pain, redness, and swelling, often on the big toe. Home Care: Soak the toe in warm salt water for 15 minutes twice daily. Gently dry the area. Always trim toenails straight across—never round the edges deeply into the corners. Wear open-toed sandals or wide shoes. Warning Signs: If the toe discharges pus, smells bad, or redness spreads up the toe, visit a Community Health Centre for minor surgical relief.

topic: Fungal nail infection, onychomycosis, thick yellowish brittle nails
source_name: WHO - Fungal infections guidance
content: Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail bed and plate, causing the nail to become thickened, discolored (yellow, brown, or white), brittle, and crumbly at the edges. Home Care: Keep nails short, clean, and filed straight across. Dry feet completely after bathing. Wear breathable footwear and clean cotton socks. Do not share nail clippers. Disinfect clippers after use. Consult a physician for oral or topical antifungal treatment, as nail fungus takes several months to clear.

topic: Dry skin, xerosis, itchy rough skin, winter itch
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dry skin management
content: Xerosis or dry skin is common during winter, dry winds, or from excessive harsh soap usage, causing skin roughness, fine cracks, flaking, and itching. Home Care: Limit showers to 5-10 minutes with lukewarm water. Use mild glycerin-based or soap-free cleansers. Apply moisturizers like pure coconut oil or heavy moisturizing cream within 3 minutes of stepping out of the bath. Use indoor humidification if air is dry. Drink adequate water. Warning Signs: Severe cracking with deep bleeding or signs of infection requires medical care.

topic: Bed bug bites, clustered itchy red welts, mattress bug marks
source_name: WHO - Vector biology and control
content: Bed bug bites present as small, red, itchy bumps often arranged in a line or zigzag cluster ('breakfast, lunch, and dinner' pattern) on exposed skin like arms, neck, and shoulders. Home Care: Wash bite sites with soap and water. Apply cool compresses and calamine lotion to soothe itching. Avoid scratching to prevent secondary skin infections. Wash bedding, pillows, and curtains in hot water and expose mattresses to direct hot sunlight for several hours. Warning Signs: If bite marks become warm, swollen, and ooze pus, seek clinic care.

topic: Head lice infestation, pediculosis capitis, scalp crawling sensation, joon
source_name: National Health Portal India - Head lice guidelines
content: Head lice are tiny parasitic insects living on the scalp and feeding on human blood, causing persistent scalp itching, crawling sensations, and tiny white nits (eggs) cemented to hair shafts. Home Care: Use a fine-toothed metal nit comb on wet hair coated with hair conditioner to remove lice and eggs mechanically. Use anti-lice medicated wash recommended by a health worker. Wash hairbrushes, pillowcases, and caps in hot water. Avoid head-to-head contact with others. Warning Signs: Severe bacterial skin sores from vigorous scratching need medical attention.

topic: Shingles, herpes zoster, painful blistering rash along one side of torso
source_name: WHO - Varicella and herpes zoster
content: Shingles is caused by reactivation of the dormant varicella-zoster virus (chickenpox), causing tingling, burning, or sharp pain followed by a localized band or cluster of fluid-filled blisters strictly on one side of the body or face. Home Care: Keep the rash clean, dry, and loosely covered with a non-stick sterile dressing. Apply cool, moist compresses. Wear loose cotton clothing. Avoid contact with pregnant women and infants. Warning Signs: See a doctor within 72 hours for antiviral treatment; if shingles appears near the eye, seek emergency ophthalmic care to protect vision.

topic: Impetigo, honey-colored crusted skin sores in children
source_name: WHO - Bacterial skin infections in children
content: Impetigo is a highly contagious bacterial skin infection, common in young children, presenting with red sores that quickly burst, ooze clear fluid, and form characteristic honey-colored or golden crusts, usually around the nose and mouth. Home Care: Gently wash crusted areas with warm water and mild antibacterial soap. Wash the child's clothes, towels, and toys separately in warm water. Keep the child's fingernails clipped short and discourage touching sores. Keep home from school until sores heal. Warning Signs: Seek medical care promptly for prescription antibiotic ointment or syrup.

topic: Cellulitis, red hot swollen tender spreading skin infection
source_name: WHO - Management of bacterial skin infections
content: Cellulitis is a serious, deep bacterial skin infection causing an area of skin to suddenly become bright red, swollen, intensely hot to touch, and tender, most often on the lower legs or face. Home Care: Rest the affected limb elevated on pillows to reduce swelling. Mark the red border with a pen to monitor whether redness expands. Do not compress or massage the area. Warning Signs: Cellulitis requires immediate medical evaluation and prescription antibiotics; seek urgent care if redness spreads rapidly, or if accompanied by chills, fever, or confusion.

topic: Folliculitis, razor bumps, small whitehead pimples around hair roots
source_name: National Health Portal India - Folliculitis
content: Folliculitis is inflammation or superficial infection of hair follicles, appearing as clusters of tiny red bumps or whiteheads around hair bases, frequently after shaving, waxing, or friction. Home Care: Apply a warm damp compress for 10 minutes 3 times daily. Pause shaving the area for several days. When resuming shaving, use a fresh sharp razor, shave in the direction of hair growth, and never shave dry. Wear loose breathable fabrics. Warning Signs: If bumps enlarge into deep painful boils or fail to improve after 5 days, consult a health worker.

topic: Skin tags, acrochordons, small flesh-colored skin growths
source_name: National Health Portal India - Common skin lesions
content: Skin tags are completely harmless, small, soft, flesh-colored or brown balloon-like growths attached to the skin by a thin stalk, frequently found on the neck, armpits, eyelids, and under breasts. Home Care: Skin tags are benign and do not require treatment unless irritated by clothing or jewelry. Do not attempt to cut, tie off with thread, or burn skin tags at home, as this causes severe bleeding and infection. If removal is desired for comfort or appearance, have a doctor or dermatologist remove it safely.

topic: Lip sores, chapped dry cracked lips, cheilitis
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral and lip care
content: Chapped lips (cheilitis) involve dryness, flaking, peeling, and painful stinging splits on the lips, caused by cold dry winds, sun exposure, dehydration, or habitual lip-licking. Home Care: Apply plain petroleum jelly, coconut oil, or beeswax lip balm frequently throughout the day. Drink plenty of water. Resist licking your lips, as evaporating saliva strips away natural oils and worsens dryness. Protect lips with a scarf in dusty or dry wind. Warning Signs: Persistent cracking at lip corners that does not heal (angular cheilitis) may need antifungal ointment from a clinic.

topic: Mouth fever blisters, cold sores, herpes simplex labialis, oral blisters
source_name: WHO - Herpes simplex virus fact sheet
content: Cold sores are small, fluid-filled blisters that erupt on or around the lips, caused by the contagious Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1). They often tingle or burn before breaking out and forming a crust. Home Care: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth to soothe tingling and swelling. Dab petroleum jelly to keep crusts soft. Wash hands frequently and avoid touching your eyes. Do not kiss anyone or share drinking glasses, towels, or utensils while blisters are present. Warning Signs: Seek medical attention if blisters spread close to the eyes or if you have a weakened immune system.

topic: Friction blisters, foot water blisters from new shoes
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid for blisters
content: Friction blisters are fluid-filled pockets that form between upper skin layers caused by repeated rubbing and friction from tight shoes or repetitive tool use. Home Care: Leave the blister intact; the bubble roof protects against bacterial infection. Clean gently with soap and water, and cover loosely with a sterile adhesive bandage. If a blister bursts naturally, wash gently, leave the flap of skin in place, apply antibacterial ointment, and dress cleanly. Change dressings daily. Warning Signs: If the blister fills with yellow pus, red streaks appear, or pain worsens, see a doctor.

topic: Intertrigo, raw red chafing rash in skin folds, groin and under breasts
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin fold hygiene
content: Intertrigo is an inflammatory condition of skin folds (groin, armpits, under breasts, abdominal folds) caused by skin-on-skin friction, warmth, and trapped sweat, frequently complicated by Candida yeast. Symptoms include red, raw, stinging, or itchy patches. Home Care: Keep skin folds thoroughly clean and dry. Wash with mild soap and gently pat completely dry with a soft towel (do not rub). Use a fan or hairdryer on a cool setting. Wear loose, moisture-wicking cotton clothing. Place a dry cotton washcloth between skin folds to absorb moisture. Warning Signs: If cracks bleed or ooze white fluid with foul odor, visit a clinic for antifungal treatment.

topic: Paronychia, infected nail fold, swollen red painful cuticle, eponychia
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail fold infections
content: Paronychia is an infection of the skin immediately surrounding a fingernail or toenail, usually entering via hangnails, nail-biting, thumb-sucking, or aggressive manicures, causing localized redness, throbbing pain, and swelling. Home Care: Soak the affected finger or toe in warm water for 15-20 minutes 3 to 4 times daily to reduce swelling and promote circulation. Dry gently. Avoid biting nails or picking at cuticles. Never squeeze or lance the nail fold at home. Warning Signs: If a yellow pocket of pus forms under the nail, redness spreads up the finger, or fever develops, visit a health centre for drainage.

topic: Melasma, dark brown facial pigmentation patches, chloasma
source_name: WHO - Ultraviolet radiation and pigmentation
content: Melasma is a harmless skin condition characterized by symmetric brown or grayish-brown patches on sun-exposed facial areas, particularly cheeks, bridge of nose, forehead, and upper lip, commonly triggered by sunlight exposure, hormonal fluctuations during pregnancy, or oral contraceptives. Home Care: Melasma is benign. The single most important step is rigorous sun protection: apply broad-spectrum sunscreen daily, wear wide-brimmed hats, and seek shade. Avoid harsh skin bleaching chemicals and bleaching creams containing mercury or unregulated steroids. Consult a certified dermatologist for safe topical care.

topic: Rosacea, facial flushing, persistent central facial redness, visible capillaries
source_name: National Health Portal India - Rosacea
content: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin condition primarily affecting the face, causing frequent flushing, persistent redness across the nose and cheeks, visible tiny spider blood vessels, and sometimes small red bumps. Home Care: Identify and avoid individual triggers: spicy foods, hot beverages, alcohol, extreme heat/cold, and emotional stress. Cleanse face gently with lukewarm water and a soap-free cleanser. Use gentle fragrance-free moisturizers and daily mineral sunscreen. Do not scrub or exfoliate facial skin. Warning Signs: If eyes become red, gritty, or dry (ocular rosacea), see an eye specialist.

topic: Hyperhidrosis, excessive sweating of palms, soles, and armpits
source_name: National Health Portal India - Hyperhidrosis
content: Primary hyperhidrosis is excessive sweating beyond physiological thermoregulatory needs, most commonly affecting the palms of the hands, soles of the feet, and armpits. Home Care: Wash sweat-prone areas daily and dry completely. Apply aluminum chloride antiperspirants at night onto completely dry skin. Wear natural breathable cotton or linen clothes and leather or canvas shoes. Change socks twice daily. Carry a clean absorbent cotton handkerchief. Warning Signs: Sudden generalized sweating, particularly night sweats accompanied by fever and weight loss, requires urgent medical testing for tuberculosis.

topic: Bromhidrosis, strong body odor, foul-smelling sweat, perspiration odor
source_name: National Health Portal India - Personal hygiene
content: Body odor occurs when harmless natural bacteria on the skin surface break down odorless apocrine sweat into volatile, pungent fatty acids and thioalcohols, predominantly in armpits and groin. Home Care: Bathe daily using antibacterial soap, washing armpits and groin thoroughly. Dry completely after bathing. Wear clean cotton clothes and wash garments after every use. Apply antiperspirants or deodorant. Shaving or trimming armpit hair helps keep the area dry and reduces bacterial colonization. Limit strong pungent foods like raw garlic and onions if odor is persistent.

topic: Alopecia areata, sudden patchy circular hair loss, balding coins
source_name: National Health Portal India - Hair loss guidelines
content: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, causing sudden, well-defined circular or oval smooth bald patches on the scalp or beard area, without skin redness or scaling. Home Care: The condition does not cause physical pain and hair often regrows over several months. Protect bare scalp patches from sun exposure with hats or sunscreen. Avoid harsh hair pulling, tight braiding, chemical straightening, and hot blow dryers. Manage stress through exercise and rest. Consult a dermatologist for safe medical therapies if patches enlarge.

topic: Keloid scars and hypertrophic scars, raised thick overgrown scars
source_name: National Health Portal India - Scar care
content: A keloid is an overgrowth of dense fibrous scar tissue that extends beyond the original wound boundaries following skin trauma, piercings, vaccinations, or acne, appearing as a raised, firm, smooth, shiny pink or dark nodule. Home Care: Keloids are non-cancerous. Do not attempt to burn, cut, or squeeze keloids at home, as surgical trauma without medical supervision causes them to grow back much larger. Apply silicone gel sheets under physician guidance. Keep the skin moisturized. Avoid elective piercings or cosmetic tattoos if you have a family or personal tendency to keloids.

topic: Molluscum contagiosum, small pearly dome-shaped skin bumps with central dimple
source_name: WHO - Common pediatric skin infections
content: Molluscum contagiosum is a benign viral skin infection caused by a poxvirus, producing small, firm, dome-shaped, pearl-like bumps with a tiny central dimple (umbilication), common in young children and spreading by skin contact. Home Care: The bumps are harmless and typically resolve on their own over 6 to 18 months. Do not squeeze, scratch, or pop the bumps, as the cheesy white center contains infectious virus that spreads to adjacent skin. Keep bumps covered with clothing or a light bandage. Do not share towels or bath sponges.

topic: Chickenpox rash, varicella fluid-filled itchy blisters, fever in children
source_name: WHO - Varicella and herpes zoster fact sheet
content: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral illness caused by the varicella-zoster virus, causing fever followed by intensely itchy red spots that turn into fluid-filled blisters ('dewdrops on a rose petal'), which eventually burst and scab over. Home Care: Keep fingernails cut short and put cotton mittens on young children to prevent scratching and bacterial scarring. Apply calamine lotion to blisters. Give cool water baths with colloidal oatmeal or neem leaves. Maintain good hydration. NEVER give aspirin to children or teenagers with chickenpox due to the life-threatening risk of Reye's syndrome. Warning Signs: Breathing difficulty, extreme drowsiness, or red hot swollen infected blisters requires hospital care.

topic: Conjunctivitis, pink eye, red eyes, eye discharge, eye itching
source_name: WHO - Vision and eye care
content: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by viral or bacterial infection or allergies, causing pink/red eyes, gritty burning sensation, watery or sticky yellow discharge, and crusting of eyelids overnight. Home Care: Clean crusts gently from inner to outer eye corner using cotton soaked in boiled and cooled water (use a separate piece for each eye). Apply cool compresses. Wash hands frequently with soap. Do not rub eyes. Avoid sharing towels, eye drops, or pillowcases. Stop wearing contact lenses. Warning Signs: Seek immediate medical care if you experience severe eye pain, extreme light sensitivity, or loss of vision.

topic: Eye stye, hordeolum, painful red bump on eyelid, eyelid pimple
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye care
content: A stye is a painful, tender red bump on the edge of the eyelid caused by bacterial infection of an eyelash follicle or oil gland. Home Care: Apply a warm, moist, clean cloth compress to the closed eyelid for 10-15 minutes 3 to 4 times a day to promote blood flow and drainage. Wash hands before touching the eyes. NEVER squeeze, press, or pop a stye. Avoid wearing eye makeup or contact lenses until fully resolved. Warning Signs: Seek a clinic doctor if the entire eyelid swells shut, the stye does not improve after 48 hours, or vision is impaired.

topic: Dry eyes, gritty eye feeling, screen eye strain, computer vision syndrome
source_name: WHO - Blindness and visual impairment
content: Dry eyes occur when tear production decreases or tears evaporate too quickly, caused by prolonged screen viewing, air conditioning, wind, or dust, causing burning, stinging, and gritty sensations. Home Care: Practice the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Consciously blink more frequently while reading screens. Use preservative-free artificial tear drops. Adjust screen brightness and keep screens slightly below eye level. Wear protective eyewear in dusty wind. Warning Signs: Persistent eye redness, corneal pain, or changes in vision require an eye doctor's evaluation.

topic: Chalazion, painless eyelid lump, blocked meibomian gland
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eyelid conditions
content: A chalazion is a painless, firm lump inside the eyelid caused by an inflammatory blockage of an oil (meibomian) gland, unlike a stye which is an acute painful bacterial infection. Home Care: Apply warm damp compresses to the eyelid for 10-15 minutes 4 times daily to soften hardened oils. After warming, gently massage the eyelid toward the eyelashes with clean fingertips. Never pop or lance a chalazion. Maintain good eyelid hygiene. Warning Signs: If the chalazion enlarges, presses on the cornea causing blurred vision, or does not resolve in 4 weeks, consult an ophthalmologist for minor clinic drainage.

topic: Blepharitis, inflamed crusty red eyelid edges, dandruff on eyelashes
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye conditions
content: Blepharitis is chronic inflammation of the eyelid margins where eyelashes grow, causing red, swollen, itchy eyelids with greasy flakes or dandruff-like scales clinging to eyelash roots. Home Care: Place a warm wet cloth over closed eyelids for 5 minutes to loosen crusts. Dilute a few drops of mild baby shampoo in warm water and gently scrub the eyelash margins with a clean cotton swab or washcloth. Rinse thoroughly with clean water. Do this twice daily. Avoid eye makeup until inflammation clears. Warning Signs: If you develop severe pain, deep corneal redness, or blurred vision, visit an eye clinic.

topic: Subconjunctival hemorrhage, red blood patch on white of eye
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye health
content: A subconjunctival hemorrhage occurs when a tiny, fragile capillary under the clear conjunctiva breaks, creating a bright red, painless patch on the sclera (white of the eye), often triggered by heavy coughing, sneezing, straining, or rubbing eyes. Home Care: The condition looks alarming but is harmless and does not affect vision. No medical drops are required; the pooled blood naturally absorbs into the body over 10 to 14 days, like a skin bruise changing from red to yellow-green. Avoid rubbing the eye. Warning Signs: Seek immediate medical care if accompanied by eye pain, changes in vision, discharge, or following severe blunt trauma to the eye.

topic: Foreign object in eye, dust in eye, eyelash in eye first aid
source_name: WHO - Emergency eye care
content: Dust, sand, or an eyelash getting trapped in the eye causes immediate discomfort, reflex tearing, and sharp gritty sensations. First Aid: DO NOT rub the eye, as rubbing grinds particles into the delicate cornea, causing painful scratches (corneal abrasions). Wash your hands. Pull the upper eyelid down over the lower lid and blink repeatedly to flush the particle with tears. Flush the eye gently with clean, sterile water or saline. If visible on the white part, dab gently with a wet cotton swab. Warning Signs: If the object is embedded, metal, or pain and vision impairment persist after flushing, go immediately to an eye clinic.

topic: Corneal abrasion, scratched cornea, severe gritty eye pain, light sensitivity
source_name: WHO - Vision and eye care
content: A corneal abrasion is a superficial scratch on the clear surface of the cornea caused by fingernails, tree branches, foreign bodies, or contact lenses, producing sharp pain, excessive tearing, redness, and extreme light sensitivity (photophobia). Home Care: Rinse the eye gently with clean saline solution. Rest the eye and wear dark sunglasses in bright light. DO NOT rub the eye. Remove and stop wearing contact lenses immediately. Do not patch the eye without a doctor's order. Warning Signs: Corneal abrasions risk serious fungal or bacterial ulcers; visit an eye specialist promptly for antibiotic drops to prevent permanent scarring.

topic: Earwax buildup, blocked ear, muffled hearing, ear fullness, wax plug
source_name: WHO - Deafness and hearing loss
content: Earwax (cerumen) protects the ear canal, but excess accumulation can cause a plugged feeling, partial hearing reduction, mild itching, or ringing. Home Care: Put 2-3 drops of clean olive oil, mineral oil, or medical wax-softening drops into the ear canal twice daily for 3 days to soften wax naturally. NEVER insert cotton buds, matchsticks, bobby pins, or keys into the ear canal; doing so rams wax deeper and can puncture the eardrum. Warning Signs: If you experience sharp ear pain, fluid or blood drainage, or dizziness, visit an ENT doctor for safe irrigation.

topic: Swimmer's ear, otitis externa, ear canal itch and pain when pulling earlobe
source_name: National Health Portal India - Ear infections
content: Swimmer's ear is an infection of the outer ear canal lining caused by water remaining in the ear after swimming or bathing, allowing bacteria or fungi to grow. Symptoms include itching, redness, clear odorless fluid, and sharp pain when pulling the earlobe. Home Care: Keep the ear canal completely dry. Tilt head sideways after bathing to drain water. Avoid swimming until healed. Use a hairdryer on the lowest cool setting held 30 cm away to dry outer ear. Never scratch inside with objects. Warning Signs: Severe pain, fever, swollen lymph nodes, or thick pus requires prescription ear drops from a doctor.

topic: Otitis media, middle ear infection, throbbing earache after cold in children
source_name: WHO - Ear and hearing care guidelines
content: Acute otitis media is inflammation and fluid accumulation in the middle ear space behind the eardrum, commonly occurring following a cold when the Eustachian tube swells shut. Symptoms: Throbbing ear pain, irritability, sleep disturbances, temporary hearing reduction, and fever in children. Home Care: Hold a warm (not hot) damp compress against the outer ear for 15 minutes to soothe pain. Keep head elevated while resting. Keep child well-hydrated. Never put oil or liquids into the ear if the eardrum might be perforated. Warning Signs: Fluid, yellow pus, or blood draining from the ear canal, high fever, or swelling behind the ear requires prompt clinic care.

topic: Tinnitus, ringing in ears, buzzing sound in ears, ear whistling
source_name: WHO - Deafness and hearing loss
content: Tinnitus is the perception of sound (ringing, buzzing, hissing, or whistling) in one or both ears without an external acoustic source, often caused by loud noise exposure, earwax plugs, stress, or age-related hearing changes. Home Care: Avoid exposure to loud sounds; wear ear protection near machinery or loudspeakers. Avoid complete silence by playing soft, soothing background sounds (white noise, fan, or calm music). Limit caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine which aggravate tinnitus. Practice relaxation techniques. Warning Signs: Tinnitus occurring in only one ear, pulsing in rhythm with heartbeat, or accompanied by dizziness or sudden hearing loss requires prompt ENT evaluation.

topic: Ear barotrauma, airplane ear, popping ears during flight or diving
source_name: National Health Portal India - Ear disorders
content: Airplane ear occurs when altitude changes create an air pressure imbalance between the environment and the middle ear across the Eustachian tube during flight ascent or descent. Symptoms include fullness, muffled hearing, and popping discomfort. Home Care: Swallowing, chewing gum, or yawning frequently during descent opens the Eustachian tube. Perform the gentle Valsalva maneuver: pinch nostrils shut, close mouth, and gently blow through the nose as if blowing nose lightly. Avoid sleeping during landing so you can swallow actively. Warning Signs: Severe persistent sharp ear pain, hearing loss, or bleeding from ear requires medical evaluation.

topic: Sore throat, pharyngitis, scratchy throat, painful swallowing
source_name: WHO - Management of respiratory infections
content: A sore throat is irritation or inflammation of the pharynx, commonly caused by viral upper respiratory infections (common cold), dry indoor air, or smoking. Home Care: Gargle with warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in a glass of warm water) 3 to 4 times a day to reduce swelling and clear mucus. Drink warm fluids like water, ginger tea, or clear soups. Suck on throat lozenges. Rest voice and stay hydrated. Avoid smoking and second-hand smoke. Warning Signs: High fever, difficulty breathing, inability to swallow saliva (drooling), or white pus patches on tonsils requires clinic evaluation for bacterial strep.

topic: Common cold, runny nose, sneezing, nasal congestion, seasonal sniffles
source_name: WHO - Common viral respiratory illnesses
content: The common cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract causing a runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, scratchy throat, mild cough, and slight tiredness. Antibiotics do not kill cold viruses and are ineffective. Home Care: Rest adequately. Inhale warm steam to clear blocked nasal passages. Drink plenty of warm fluids (water, soups, herbal tea). Use saline nasal spray or drops to loosen thick mucus. Wash hands frequently to protect family members. Warning Signs: If symptoms persist beyond 10 days, fever exceeds 38.5C (101.3F), or breathing becomes difficult, visit a doctor.

topic: Allergic rhinitis, hay fever, seasonal sneezing, itchy watery eyes, nasal itching
source_name: WHO - Allergic rhinitis and its impact on asthma
content: Allergic rhinitis occurs when the immune system overreacts to airborne allergens like plant pollen, dust mites, mold spores, or pet dander, causing bouts of rapid sneezing, clear watery nasal discharge, itchy nose, palate itching, and watery red eyes. Home Care: Identify and limit exposure to known triggers. Wash face and hair after being outdoors in dusty or pollen-heavy weather. Use saline nasal rinses (neti pot or saline spray) to physically flush trapped allergens from nasal passages. Keep windows closed during high dust/pollen periods. Avoid sweeping dry dust; use damp mopping. Warning Signs: If chronic nasal blockage causes persistent sinus pain, ear infections, or sleep apnea, consult an ENT doctor.

topic: Sinusitis, sinus pressure, facial fullness behind cheekbones, post-nasal drip
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sinusitis
content: Sinusitis is inflammation of the air-filled cavities within the facial bones (paranasal sinuses), usually following a viral cold, causing thick discolored nasal mucus, facial pain and pressure over cheeks and forehead, reduced smell, and post-nasal drip. Home Care: Inhale warm steam from a bowl of hot water 2 to 3 times daily. Apply a warm moist compress over forehead and cheeks. Stay well-hydrated with warm water and herbal teas. Flush nasal passages with warm sterile saline solution. Sleep with head slightly elevated. Warning Signs: Severe pain around the eyes, high fever, double vision, or swelling of the forehead or eyelids requires urgent clinic evaluation.

topic: Nosebleed, epistaxis, bleeding from nose, first aid for bloody nose
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid epistaxis
content: Nosebleeds occur when fragile blood vessels in the anterior nasal septum break due to dry air, vigorous nose-picking, allergies, or minor trauma. First Aid: Sit upright and lean slightly FORWARD (never tilt the head backward, which causes blood to run down the throat and trigger vomiting or choking). Firmly pinch the soft part of the nose just below the nasal bridge with thumb and index finger for 10 continuous minutes without letting go. Breathe through the mouth. Place an ice pack on the bridge of the nose. Warning Signs: If bleeding does not stop after 20 minutes of firm pressure, or follows heavy head injury, seek emergency hospital care immediately.

topic: Laryngitis, lost voice, hoarse raspy voice, vocal cord irritation
source_name: National Health Portal India - Voice disorders
content: Laryngitis is inflammation of the vocal cords (larynx) caused by viral respiratory infections, vocal strain (shouting, loud singing, prolonged speaking), or acid reflux, resulting in a hoarse, raspy voice or complete voice loss. Home Care: Rest your voice completely: speak as little as possible. DO NOT whisper, as whispering puts more mechanical strain on the vocal cords than normal quiet speech. Drink plenty of warm water and caffeine-free teas. Inhale warm steam. Avoid smoking and alcohol. Use lozenges to soothe throat tickles. Warning Signs: Voice hoarseness lasting more than 2 weeks, difficulty breathing, or coughing up blood requires an ENT evaluation.

topic: Canker sores, aphthous mouth ulcers, painful sores inside cheek and lips
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral health
content: Canker sores are small, painful, non-contagious ulcers that appear inside the lips, inner cheeks, or gums, with a white/yellow center and red border, triggered by stress, minor accidental biting, or spicy foods. Home Care: Rinse mouth with warm salt water or diluted baking soda solution. Avoid spicy, acidic, crunchy, or salty foods that sting. Apply an ice chip to the sore to numb pain. Maintain good oral hygiene with a soft-bristled toothbrush. Sores heal naturally in 7 to 10 days. Warning Signs: If an ulcer lasts longer than 3 weeks, grows unusually large, or makes eating impossible, see a dentist or doctor.

topic: Toothache, dental decay, cavity pain, sensitive tooth
source_name: WHO - Oral health fact sheet
content: Toothache is usually caused by dental caries (cavities) reaching the sensitive inner tooth nerve, cracked enamel, or gum inflammation. Home Care: Rinse mouth thoroughly with warm salt water. Gently floss between teeth to dislodge trapped food particles. Apply an ice pack to the outside of the cheek for 15 minutes. Dab a small drop of clove oil on a clean cotton ball and place lightly near the aching tooth for temporary numbing. Avoid very hot, cold, or sugary drinks. Warning Signs: Facial swelling, swollen jaw, fever, or difficulty swallowing indicates a serious dental abscess requiring urgent dental or clinic care.

topic: Gingivitis, bleeding gums when brushing, red swollen tender gums
source_name: WHO - Oral health
content: Gingivitis is the early, reversible stage of gum disease caused by bacterial dental plaque accumulating along the gumline, leading to red, swollen gums that bleed easily during toothbrushing or flossing. Home Care: Brush teeth thoroughly twice daily for 2 full minutes using a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Floss daily between all teeth to remove plaque bacteria. Rinse with warm salt water. Replace toothbrush every 3 months. Avoid tobacco, gutka, and bidi, which accelerate gum disease. Warning Signs: Gums receding from teeth, persistent loose teeth, or pus oozing from gums indicates advanced periodontitis requiring professional dental cleaning.

topic: Halitosis, chronic bad breath, foul mouth odor, tongue coating
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dental hygiene
content: Halitosis or chronic bad breath is predominantly caused by anaerobic bacteria breaking down food debris and protein on the tongue, between teeth, and along inflamed gums, producing foul sulfur compounds. Home Care: Brush teeth twice daily and floss between every tooth once daily. Gently scrape or clean the back of the tongue using a tongue scraper or soft toothbrush to remove the white bacterial coating. Drink plenty of water to prevent dry mouth (saliva naturally neutralizes odor). Rinse mouth with water after eating. Avoid tobacco. Warning Signs: Bad breath accompanied by chronic tonsil stones, sinus pain, or sweet fruity odor (diabetic ketoacidosis) requires medical assessment.

topic: Oral thrush, candidiasis in mouth, white curd patches on tongue and cheeks
source_name: WHO - Fungal infections in oral health
content: Oral thrush is a fungal infection caused by Candida yeast overgrowth inside the mouth, producing creamy white, slightly raised curd-like patches on the tongue, inner cheeks, and roof of mouth that reveal red, bleeding tissue when wiped. Common in infants, denture wearers, or after antibiotic/steroid inhaler use. Home Care: Maintain meticulous oral hygiene. Clean and sterilize dentures daily. After using steroid asthma inhalers, always rinse mouth thoroughly with water and spit it out. In infants, sterilize bottle nipples and pacifiers. Consult a doctor for prescription antifungal oral drops (such as nystatin). Warning Signs: Difficulty swallowing or burning pain in the chest requires medical evaluation.

topic: Geographic tongue, benign migratory glossitis, map-like smooth red patches on tongue
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral conditions
content: Geographic tongue is a completely benign, non-contagious condition where smooth, red, irregularly shaped patches with slightly raised white borders appear on the tongue surface, shifting location over days like a map. Home Care: The condition is harmless and does not lead to cancer or infection. Most people experience no symptoms, though some have mild sensitivity to spicy, acidic, salty, or very hot foods. Avoid irritating foods and acidic drinks when patches are sensitive. Maintain regular gentle oral hygiene with a soft toothbrush. No medical intervention is necessary.

topic: Dry cough, tickly throat, non-productive cough, cough without phlegm
source_name: WHO - Clinical management of respiratory illness
content: A dry cough is a ticklish, irritating cough that does not produce mucus or phlegm, frequently following viral colds, respiratory allergies, air pollution, or acid reflux. Home Care: Drink warm water frequently throughout the day. Sip warm water with honey and lemon (never give honey to infants under 1 year due to infant botulism risk). Inhale warm steam. Use a humidifier or bowl of warm water in the room. Avoid smoke, incense, and sudden temperature shifts. Warning Signs: Seek immediate medical care if cough lasts over 2 weeks, produces blood, causes shortness of breath, or is accompanied by chest pain or night sweats.

topic: Wet cough, productive cough with mucus, chest congestion, phlegm
source_name: WHO - Pneumonia fact sheet
content: A wet (productive) cough helps clear excess mucus and fluid from the airways and lungs, commonly associated with bronchitis, post-cold congestion, or respiratory infections. Home Care: Stay well-hydrated: drink plenty of warm water, broths, and herbal teas, which thin mucus so it can be cleared easily. Inhale steam 2 to 3 times daily. Keep your head elevated with an extra pillow while sleeping. Avoid cough suppressants that prevent clearing mucus unless advised by a doctor. Warning Signs: Coughing up rusty, green, or blood-streaked phlegm, high fever, or rapid breathing requires urgent clinic evaluation for pneumonia.

topic: Tuberculosis, TB symptoms, persistent cough over 2 weeks, Odisha NTEP
source_name: MoHFW India - National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme
content: Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious infectious bacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, spreading through air droplets. Symptoms: Persistent cough lasting more than 2 weeks, low-grade evening fever, drenching night sweats, unexplained weight loss, loss of appetite, and coughing up blood (hemoptysis). Protocol: All testing (sputum microscopy, CBNAAT/Truenat) and complete 6-month DOTS treatment are provided completely FREE by the Government of Odisha under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP). Visit your nearest Community Health Centre (CHC) or Primary Health Centre (PHC) immediately. Take the full medicine course without skipping.

topic: Bronchitis, acute bronchial inflammation, chest rattle, cough
source_name: WHO - Respiratory disease management
content: Acute bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchial airway tubes, usually triggered by a viral infection following a cold or flu, causing a persistent cough with clear or colored phlegm, mild chest soreness, and fatigue. Home Care: Get plenty of rest. Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of warm water daily. Inhale warm steam to loosen chest tightness. Antibiotics are generally ineffective because over 90% of acute bronchitis cases are viral. Avoid exposure to cigarette smoke, kitchen chulha smoke, and dust. Warning Signs: Wheezing, breathlessness, fever above 38.5C, or symptoms lasting over 3 weeks require medical evaluation.

topic: Asthma triggers, wheezing prevention, dust and smoke allergy, inhaler care
source_name: WHO - Asthma fact sheet
content: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways causing recurring episodes of wheezing, chest tightness, coughing, and shortness of breath when exposed to triggers like cold air, dust mites, pollen, pet dander, or smoke. Home Care: Identify and avoid personal triggers. Keep bedding washed and sun-dried. Avoid wood smoke and mosquito coils indoors. Always carry prescribed reliever inhalers. Take long slow breaths during mild tightness and sit upright. Warning Signs: If severe breathlessness prevents speaking in full sentences, chest pulls inward (retractions), or lips turn blue, call 108 or go to the emergency room immediately.

topic: Pneumonia warning signs, chest infection, rapid breathing, lung crackles
source_name: WHO - Pneumonia in children and adults
content: Pneumonia is an acute infection of the lung alveoli (caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi) where air sacs fill with pus and fluid. Symptoms include high fever, chills, rapid shallow breathing, chest pain when inhaling or coughing, and severe fatigue. Home Care: Pneumonia is a serious illness requiring professional medical assessment and prescription antibiotics or antivirals. Rest in bed with upper body propped up on pillows. Drink warm fluids to prevent dehydration. Warning Signs: Seek emergency hospital care (call 108) if an adult or child develops severe breathlessness, bluish lips or nails (cyanosis), confusion, or chest indrawing.

topic: Post-nasal drip, throat clearing, mucus dripping down back of throat
source_name: National Health Portal India - Respiratory health
content: Post-nasal drip occurs when excess or thickened mucus from the nose and sinuses drips down the back of the throat, triggering constant throat clearing, a ticklish chronic cough (often worse when lying flat), and hoarseness. Home Care: Drink plenty of warm water throughout the day to thin mucus. Perform nasal saline irrigation (saline nasal spray or neti pot) to rinse out trapped mucus and allergens. Sleep with head slightly elevated on an extra pillow. Inhale warm steam before bedtime. Avoid dusty environments and smoke. Warning Signs: If mucus is thick yellow-green with facial pain, fever, or bloody streaks, consult a clinic.

topic: Seasonal influenza, flu vs common cold, high fever and body ache
source_name: WHO - Influenza (seasonal) fact sheet
content: Seasonal flu (influenza) is an acute viral infection that begins abruptly with high fever (often 38.5C to 40C), severe body aches, head pain, extreme fatigue, chills, dry cough, and sore throat, whereas a common cold starts gradually with mainly runny nose. Home Care: Complete bed rest. Drink plenty of warm liquids (water, lemon honey tea, kanji, clear soups). Use paracetamol under medical guidance for fever and aches; do not give aspirin to children. Stay home from school/work to prevent spreading infection. Wash hands frequently. Warning Signs: Difficulty breathing, chest pain, confusion, or bluish lips requires emergency medical care.

topic: Chulha smoke, indoor air pollution, wood smoke respiratory irritation
source_name: WHO - Household air pollution and health
content: Burning biomass fuels (firewood, cow dung, crop residue) in traditional unvented kitchen chulhas releases high levels of hazardous carbon monoxide, particulate matter, and toxic smoke, causing burning eyes, chronic bronchitis, asthma flare-ups, and childhood respiratory infections. Home Care: Cook in well-ventilated spaces with open windows, chimneys, or outdoor shaded cooking areas. Switch to clean cooking gas (Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana LPG) whenever possible. Keep infants, young children, and elderly family members away from cooking smoke. Wash face and eyes with clean water if exposed to heavy smoke.

topic: Shortness of breath, dyspnea, difficulty catching breath, breathlessness triage
source_name: WHO - Emergency clinical guidelines
content: Dyspnea is the uncomfortable sensation of being unable to get enough air into the lungs. Causes range from physical exertion, anxiety, and asthma to serious heart or lung conditions. Triage: If breathlessness is sudden, occurs while resting, or is accompanied by chest tightness, pressure, radiating pain, blue lips, or dizziness, treat as a MEDICAL EMERGENCY and call 108 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. For mild breathlessness due to known mild asthma or exertion, sit upright, lean slightly forward with hands on knees (tripod position), and practice pursed-lip breathing (inhale through nose for 2 seconds, exhale through pursed lips for 4 seconds).

topic: Acid reflux, GERD, heartburn, burning chest sensation, acid burps
source_name: National Health Portal India - Gastroesophageal reflux disease
content: Heartburn is a burning pain behind the breastbone caused by stomach acid regurgitating into the esophagus, often triggered by heavy, oily, or spicy meals, lying down after eating, or excess tea/coffee. Home Care: Eat smaller, more frequent meals. Avoid lying down for at least 2 to 3 hours after eating. Elevate the head of the bed by 6 inches. Avoid triggers like fried foods, citrus, onions, mint, and alcohol. Maintain a healthy body weight. Wear loose clothing around the abdomen. Warning Signs: Difficulty swallowing, food feeling stuck in the chest, vomiting blood, or black stools requires immediate medical evaluation; chest pain radiating to arm or jaw must be treated as an emergency.

topic: Indigestion, dyspepsia, stomach fullness, bloating after food
source_name: WHO - Noncommunicable diseases and digestive health
content: Indigestion (dyspepsia) involves discomfort or a painful, heavy feeling in the upper stomach, early fullness during meals, bloating, and mild nausea, often due to eating too fast, overeating, or stress. Home Care: Chew food thoroughly and eat at a relaxed pace. Drink warm water between meals rather than large gulps during meals. Sip ginger or mint tea. Avoid chewing gum or drinking carbonated sodas which swallow extra air. Take a gentle 15-minute walk after meals. Warning Signs: Unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting, or difficulty swallowing requires medical attention.

topic: Acute diarrhea, loose watery motions, gastroenteritis, dehydration prevention
source_name: WHO - Diarrhoeal disease fact sheet
content: Acute diarrhea is the passage of 3 or more loose or watery stools per day, commonly caused by viral or bacterial contamination of food or water, leading to rapid loss of water and essential electrolytes. Home Care: Prevent dehydration immediately with Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). Mix 1 full packet of WHO-formula ORS in 1 liter of clean drinking water; drink after every loose stool. Consume rice water (kanji), thin dal soup, tender coconut water, and plain salted buttermilk. Continue eating light digestible foods (khichdi, bananas, curd). Warning Signs: If stools contain blood, high fever develops, persistent vomiting prevents drinking, or eyes look sunken, visit a clinic immediately.

topic: ORS preparation and dehydration signs, zinc supplementation
source_name: WHO / UNICEF - Clinical management of acute diarrhoea
content: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) is a life-saving mixture of clean water, salts, and glucose that restores lost fluids during diarrhea. Preparation: Dissolve one complete packet of WHO-standard ORS in exactly 1 liter of boiled and cooled water. Stir well. Discard any unused prepared solution after 24 hours and make fresh. Children with diarrhea should also receive dispersible Zinc tablets (20 mg daily for 14 days, 10 mg for infants under 6 months) under ASHA guidance to shorten diarrhea duration and protect against future episodes for 3 months. Warning Signs: Extreme lethargy, no urination for 6 hours, or rapid breathing requires hospital IV fluid therapy.

topic: Constipation, hard stools, difficulty passing motion, kabz
source_name: National Health Portal India - Constipation
content: Constipation involves having fewer than 3 bowel movements per week, accompanied by hard, dry, lumpy stools and straining during defecation, usually linked to low dietary fiber, inadequate hydration, or physical inactivity. Home Care: Increase dietary fiber by eating whole grains, oats, papayas, green leafy vegetables, lentils, and prunes. Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of water daily. Engage in 30 minutes of physical exercise like brisk walking. Establish a regular toilet routine, particularly after breakfast when colonic reflexes are strongest. Do not ignore the urge to defecate. Warning Signs: Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, inability to pass gas, or blood in stool requires medical evaluation.

topic: Hemorrhoids, piles, bleeding during bowel movement, swollen anal veins, bawaseer
source_name: National Health Portal India - Piles management
content: Piles (hemorrhoids) are swollen, inflamed veins in the lower rectum and anus, causing painless bright red bleeding during bowel movements, anal itching, and tender lumps around the anus, exacerbated by straining. Home Care: Take a warm sitz bath (sit in a tub of warm plain water for 15 minutes twice daily) to soothe inflammation. Prevent constipation by eating high-fiber foods and drinking plenty of water. Avoid straining or sitting on the toilet for prolonged periods. Use soft moist wipes instead of dry paper. Warning Signs: Heavy rectal bleeding, persistent dizziness, or a hard, intensely painful purple lump (thrombosed external hemorrhoid) requires clinic evaluation.

topic: Gas, flatulence, abdominal bloating, excessive burping
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive health
content: Excess gas and bloating occur from swallowed air or the breakdown of undigested foods by gut bacteria in the colon, producing hydrogen, carbon dioxide, and methane. Home Care: Eat and drink slowly; avoid gulping food or talking while chewing. Avoid carbonated fizzy drinks, chewing gum, and drinking through straws. Limit notorious gas-forming foods temporarily (raw cabbage, cauliflower, beans, artificial sweeteners). Light walking after meals stimulates intestinal motility. Warning Signs: Bloating accompanied by severe persistent abdominal pain, unexplained weight loss, or persistent diarrhea requires medical investigation.

topic: Nausea and vomiting, upset stomach, emesis home relief
source_name: WHO - Clinical guidelines for emergency care
content: Nausea and vomiting are protective gastrointestinal reflexes triggered by food poisoning, viral gastroenteritis, motion sickness, or dietary indiscretion. Home Care: Rest the stomach: do not eat solid foods for a couple of hours after vomiting. Once vomiting pauses, take tiny sips of clear fluids (water, ORS, thin rice water) every 10 minutes. If fluids are tolerated, progress gradually to bland foods: bananas, rice, applesauce, toast (BRAT diet). Avoid fatty, greasy, or heavily spiced foods. Warning Signs: Inability to keep any fluids down for 24 hours, vomiting blood, green-yellow bile, or signs of severe dehydration requires immediate clinic care.

topic: Food poisoning, stale food sickness, bacterial foodborne illness
source_name: WHO - Food safety fact sheet
content: Food poisoning occurs from consuming food contaminated with infectious bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli, Staph aureus) or bacterial toxins, causing sudden nausea, explosive vomiting, watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and low fever within 2 to 24 hours. Home Care: Focus completely on preventing dehydration: sip ORS, electrolyte solution, tender coconut water, and plain salted rice kanji. Rest in bed. Do not take anti-diarrheal medicines (like loperamide) without medical advice, as stopping diarrhea traps bacterial toxins inside the intestines. Wash hands thoroughly. Warning Signs: Bloody diarrhea, high fever over 38.5C, severe abdominal rigidity, or inability to retain fluids requires immediate clinic care.

topic: Anal fissure, sharp tearing pain during defecation, streak of blood on toilet paper
source_name: National Health Portal India - Colorectal health
content: An anal fissure is a small tear or cut in the thin, moist lining of the anal canal, typically caused by passing hard, dry stools or severe diarrhea, causing intense sharp burning or cutting pain during and for hours after bowel movements, accompanied by a bright red streak of blood on paper. Home Care: Take warm water sitz baths for 15 minutes after bowel movements to relax the internal anal sphincter muscle and promote blood flow. Soften stools by drinking abundant water and eating fibrous foods (papaya, psyllium husk / isabgol, greens). Never strain. Warning Signs: If severe pain prevents defecation or lasts beyond 2 weeks, visit a doctor for specialized healing ointments.

topic: Lactose intolerance, bloating and diarrhea after milk or dairy
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive disorders
content: Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose (the natural sugar in milk and dairy products) due to deficiency of the digestive enzyme lactase in the small intestine. Symptoms occur 30 minutes to 2 hours after consuming dairy: stomach gurgling, bloating, flatulence, abdominal cramps, and watery diarrhea. Home Care: Moderate or replace dairy with fermented alternatives like curd (dahi / yogurt), which naturally has lower lactose and contains friendly bacteria that break it down. Choose plant-based alternatives like soy milk or lactose-free dairy. Get calcium from leafy greens, ragi, sesame seeds, and small fish. Warning Signs: If severe diarrhea or weight loss persists despite avoiding dairy, visit a physician.

topic: Jaundice awareness, yellow eyes, dark urine, viral hepatitis warning signs
source_name: WHO - Hepatitis fact sheet
content: Jaundice is the yellow discoloration of the sclera (white of the eyes), mucous membranes, and skin caused by elevated levels of bilirubin in the blood, frequently stemming from acute viral hepatitis (Hepatitis A or E spread via contaminated water/food), gallstones, or liver inflammation. Symptoms: Yellow eyes, pale or clay-colored stools, tea-colored urine, loss of appetite, nausea, and fatigue. Protocol: Jaundice requires medical blood testing (liver function tests) at a health centre. Rest adequately. Drink clean, boiled water. Eat easily digestible, low-fat carbohydrate-rich meals (boiled rice, fruits). Avoid alcohol, greasy foods, and unverified herbal concoctions that damage the liver. Warning Signs: Drowsiness, confusion, or bleeding requires emergency hospital admission.

topic: Gallstone colic, right upper abdominal pain after fatty meal, biliary pain
source_name: National Health Portal India - Gallbladder diseases
content: Biliary colic occurs when gallstones temporarily block the cystic duct draining the gallbladder, causing sudden, steady, intense ache in the upper right abdomen or below the breastbone, often radiating to the right shoulder or shoulder blade, usually starting an hour after eating a rich fatty meal. Home Care: Rest quietly and refrain from eating heavy, fried, or fatty foods. Place a warm compress on the upper abdomen. Stay hydrated with plain water. Warning Signs: If the pain becomes severe and unremitting for more than 4 hours, or is accompanied by high fever, chills, yellowing of eyes (jaundice), or severe vomiting, this indicates acute cholecystitis or bile duct blockage requiring emergency hospital care.

topic: Pinworms, enterobiasis, intense nighttime anal itching in children
source_name: WHO - Soil-transmitted helminth infections
content: Pinworms (Enterobius vermicularis) are tiny, white, thread-like parasitic worms that live in the colon. At night, female worms migrate to the anal area to deposit eggs, causing intense itching around the anus, restless sleep, and irritability, common in children. Home Care: Wash hands thoroughly with soap before eating and after using the toilet. Keep children's fingernails clipped very short to prevent eggs from lodging under nails from scratching. Wash all bed linens, nightwear, and towels in hot water and sun-dry thoroughly. Bathe in the morning to wash away eggs laid overnight. All household members should receive deworming medication prescribed by an ASHA worker or doctor simultaneously.

topic: Hiccups, singultus, persistent diaphragm spasms, hiccup remedies
source_name: National Health Portal India - General health
content: Hiccups are involuntary, sudden contractions or spasms of the diaphragm muscle, followed by rapid closure of the vocal cords that produces the characteristic 'hic' sound, commonly triggered by eating too quickly, carbonated drinks, sudden excitement, or swallowing air. Home Care: Stimulate the vagus nerve or increase carbon dioxide levels in the bloodstream: Sip a glass of ice-cold water slowly without stopping. Hold your breath for 10-15 seconds. Breathe slowly into a paper bag (never use plastic). Pull knees up to chest and lean forward for 1 minute. Place half a teaspoon of dry sugar on the back of the tongue. Most hiccups resolve naturally within minutes. Warning Signs: Hiccups persisting continuously for more than 48 hours require medical investigation.

topic: Ankle sprain, twisted ankle, foot ligament strain, R.I.C.E. protocol
source_name: WHO - Rehabilitation in health systems
content: An ankle sprain happens when ligaments supporting the ankle stretch or tear after an awkward twist or roll, causing pain, swelling, tenderness, and bruising. First Aid: Follow the R.I.C.E. protocol: REST: Stop walking on the injured foot. ICE: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a towel for 15-20 minutes every 2-3 hours for the first 48 hours (never apply ice directly to bare skin). COMPRESSION: Wrap with an elastic crepe bandage firmly but not so tight as to cut off blood circulation. ELEVATION: Prop the ankle above heart level on pillows while resting. Warning Signs: Inability to take 4 steps immediately after injury, severe deformity, or bone tenderness suggests a fracture requiring X-ray.

topic: Lower back pain, lumbago, back muscle strain, posture ache
source_name: WHO - Low back pain guidelines
content: Non-specific lower back pain is extremely common, usually caused by muscle strains, poor sitting posture, heavy improper lifting, or lack of core strength. Home Care: Stay gently active; avoid prolonged bed rest (more than 1-2 days of bed rest actually delays recovery). Apply cold packs for the first 48 hours, followed by warm compresses. When lifting objects, bend at the knees and hips, never at the waist. Sleep on a firm mattress with a pillow under the knees. Practice gentle walking and core stretching exercises. Warning Signs: Seek emergency medical care if back pain is accompanied by loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness around genitals/groin (saddle anesthesia), or weakness in both legs.

topic: Neck pain, stiff neck, cervical muscle spasm, screen neck
source_name: National Health Portal India - Musculoskeletal health
content: Neck stiffness and muscle spasms often develop from awkward sleeping positions, poor workstation ergonomics ('tech neck' from looking down at mobile phones), or drafty cold air. Home Care: Apply a warm compress or heating pad to the neck for 15 minutes. Perform gentle range-of-motion exercises: slowly turn the head side to side and tilt ear towards shoulder without forcing. Adjust phone and computer screens to eye level. Use a supportive, medium-firm pillow that keeps the neck aligned with the spine. Warning Signs: Sudden neck stiffness accompanied by high fever, severe headache, and light sensitivity is a sign of meningitis requiring emergency hospital care.

topic: Knee pain, osteoarthritis, joint stiffness, aging joint wear
source_name: WHO - Musculoskeletal health
content: Knee osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint condition where protective cartilage wears away over time, causing knee ache, morning stiffness lasting under 30 minutes, swelling, and cracking sensations during movement. Home Care: Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce mechanical load on knees (each kg lost relieves 4 kg of pressure on knees). Perform low-impact exercises: swimming, cycling, and quadriceps-strengthening leg raises. Apply warm packs before activity and cool packs after. Wear well-cushioned flat walking shoes. Warning Signs: If the knee becomes hot, red, and swollen, or cannot bear any weight, visit a clinic.

topic: Muscle cramps, nocturnal leg cramps, charley horse, calf spasms
source_name: National Health Portal India - Muscle disorders
content: Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary, painful contractions of a muscle, most commonly the calf or foot, triggered by muscle fatigue, dehydration, low potassium or magnesium, or prolonged sitting. Home Care: Gently stretch the cramping muscle immediately: for calf cramps, straighten the leg and pull the toes backward toward the shin. Massage the muscle firmly. Apply a warm towel or take a warm shower to relax tight fibers. Drink water or ORS to replace lost electrolytes. Stretch calves before going to bed. Warning Signs: Frequent recurring cramps with persistent leg swelling, redness, or skin changes require medical evaluation.

topic: Sciatica, shooting leg pain, lumbar radiculopathy, pinched nerve in lower back
source_name: National Health Portal India - Spine conditions
content: Sciatica refers to radiating pain along the path of the sciatic nerve, branching from the lower back through the hip, buttock, and down one leg past the knee, usually caused by a herniated disc compressing a nerve root. Symptoms: Burning, shooting pain, electric shock sensations, or tingling in the leg or foot. Home Care: Apply ice packs for 15 minutes to reduce acute inflammation, transitioning to warm packs after 48 hours. Continue gentle walking within pain limits; avoid sitting in soft low chairs or prolonged bed rest. Sleep with a pillow between knees when lying on the side. Warning Signs: Sudden weakness (foot drop), numbness in groin/saddle area, or loss of bladder/bowel control requires emergency surgical evaluation.

topic: Plantar fasciitis, morning heel pain, sharp bottom foot ache on first step
source_name: National Health Portal India - Foot disorders
content: Plantar fasciitis is inflammation of the thick band of tissue (plantar fascia) supporting the foot arch, causing intense stabbing heel pain during the very first steps out of bed in the morning or after sitting, which gradually eases with gentle movement. Home Care: Roll the arch of your foot over a cold or frozen water bottle for 10 minutes twice daily. Gently stretch calves and toes backward before getting out of bed. Wear supportive footwear with cushioned arches and shock-absorbing heels—never walk barefoot on hard tile or concrete floors. Avoid high-impact running until healed. Warning Signs: Persistent numbness, tingling, or pain that prevents walking requires orthopedic evaluation.

topic: Gout flare-up, acute big toe joint pain, high uric acid, podagra
source_name: WHO - Musculoskeletal health fact sheet
content: Gout is a painful form of inflammatory arthritis caused by high uric acid levels in the blood forming needle-like urate crystals in joints, classically presenting as sudden, excruciating, red, hot, swollen agony in the big toe joint (podagra), often starting at night. Home Care: Rest and elevate the affected foot. Apply cold ice packs wrapped in towels for 20 minutes to soothe inflammation (avoid direct pressure). Drink plenty of water (at least 2.5 to 3 liters daily) to assist kidney clearance of uric acid. Avoid alcohol, red meats, organ meats, shellfish, and high-fructose sweetened beverages. Warning Signs: High fever or suspicion of joint infection (septic arthritis) requires immediate hospital aspiration.

topic: Frozen shoulder, adhesive capsulitis, shoulder stiffness and reduced mobility
source_name: National Health Portal India - Joint disorders
content: Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) is characterized by progressive stiffness, deep ache, and restricted range of motion in the shoulder joint as the connective capsule thickens and tightens, common after immobilization, injury, or in people with diabetes. Home Care: Apply warm compresses to the shoulder for 15 minutes before performing gentle pendulum and finger-ladder wall exercises to preserve mobility. Move the arm within comfortable pain-free limits—do not forcefully jerk the joint. Take warm showers to relax shoulder muscles. Warning Signs: Sudden shoulder pain radiating to the jaw, neck, or left arm with shortness of breath is a cardiac emergency—call 108 immediately.

topic: Tennis elbow, lateral epicondylitis, outer elbow pain from repetitive gripping
source_name: National Health Portal India - Musculoskeletal health
content: Tennis elbow is inflammation or micro-tearing of the forearm tendons attaching to the bony outer bump of the elbow, caused by repetitive wrist extension and gripping motions (tennis, painting, carpentry, heavy kitchen chopping). Symptoms: Burning pain on outer elbow and weak grip strength. Home Care: Rest the arm from the repetitive motion causing strain. Apply an ice pack for 15 minutes 3 times daily. Wear a supportive counterforce forearm strap just below the elbow during necessary daily tasks. Perform gentle wrist flexion stretches. Warning Signs: Inability to bend the elbow, visible joint deformity, or numbness in the fingers requires medical evaluation.

topic: Carpal tunnel syndrome, wrist pain, tingling and numbness in thumb and fingers
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nerve conditions
content: Carpal tunnel syndrome occurs when the median nerve becomes compressed as it travels through the carpal tunnel in the wrist, causing tingling, pins-and-needles, numbness, and burning pain primarily in the thumb, index, and middle fingers, often waking people at night. Home Care: Wear a neutral wrist splint at night to keep the wrist straight and prevent nerve compression during sleep. Take frequent breaks from repetitive typing, vibrating tools, or knitting. Perform gentle wrist and finger gliding stretches. Apply cool packs if the wrist feels swollen. Warning Signs: Persistent dropping of objects, loss of thumb muscle bulk (thenar atrophy), or permanent numbness requires orthopedic referral.

topic: Delayed onset muscle soreness, DOMS, stiff aching muscles after workout
source_name: WHO - Physical activity and muscular health
content: Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS) is harmless, temporary muscular stiffness and soreness that peaks 24 to 48 hours after unaccustomed or intense physical exercise, caused by microscopic micro-tears in muscle fibers and subsequent natural repair. Home Care: Perform light active recovery: gentle walking, light swimming, or easy cycling to boost blood circulation. Take warm baths or showers. Gently stretch the sore muscles. Stay well-hydrated and consume adequate protein and nutritious foods to support tissue rebuilding. DOMS resolves naturally within 3 to 5 days. Warning Signs: Dark brown tea-colored urine (rhabdomyolysis) or severe swelling requires emergency hospital care.

topic: Tension headache, forehead band tightness, stress headache
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders fact sheet
content: Tension headache is the most common headache type, feeling like a tight, pressing band or dull ache across both sides of the forehead, temples, or back of the neck, often linked to stress, poor posture, or eye strain. Home Care: Rest quietly in a dark, quiet room. Apply a warm or cool compress to the forehead and neck. Drink a tall glass of water. Practice slow deep breathing and gently stretch neck and shoulder muscles. Take regular screen breaks (20-20-20 rule). Warning Signs: Seek urgent clinic care if the headache is explosive and sudden, follows head trauma, or is accompanied by stiff neck, fever, or confusion.

topic: Migraine, throbbing one-sided headache, nausea, light sensitivity
source_name: WHO - Headache disorders
content: Migraine is a recurrent headache disorder causing moderate to severe throbbing or pulsating pain, usually on one side of the head, worsened by physical activity and accompanied by nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light and sound. Some experience visual aura (flashing zigzags). Home Care: Lie down in a dark, quiet room with eyes closed. Place an ice pack on the forehead or base of skull. Sip water or electrolyte fluids. Avoid known triggers such as skipped meals, lack of sleep, loud noises, and strong odors. Warning Signs: If you experience slurred speech, facial weakness, numbness, or loss of vision, seek immediate hospital emergency care.

topic: Sinus headache, facial pressure, forehead ache, nasal congestion
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sinusitis
content: Sinus headache is characterized by a dull, throbbing ache and feeling of fullness or pressure behind the eyes, cheekbones, and forehead, usually worsening when bending forward and accompanied by a blocked or runny nose. Home Care: Inhale warm steam from a bowl of hot water for 10 minutes. Place a warm moist towel over the cheeks and nose. Drink warm herbal teas and water to thin mucus. Use saline nasal drops or rinses. Warning Signs: Severe pain with high fever, facial swelling, stiff neck, or changes in vision requires immediate medical evaluation.

topic: Dehydration headache, thirst, dry mouth, hot weather head ache
source_name: WHO - Guidelines on hydration and heat
content: Dehydration headache happens when the body loses vital fluids and electrolytes, causing temporary tissue shrinkage that pulls pain-sensitive nerves in the meninges, leading to a dull or throbbing ache. Home Care: Drink 2 to 3 glasses of cool water, oral rehydration solution (ORS), or coconut water immediately. Rest in a cool shaded room. Avoid sugary sodas, tea, coffee, and alcohol which increase dehydration. Headache typically subsides within 1 to 2 hours after rehydration. Warning Signs: If dizziness persists, urine remains dark brown, or you stop producing sweat, seek medical care.

topic: Dizziness, lightheadedness, feeling faint, presyncope upon standing
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dizziness
content: Postural dizziness or orthostatic lightheadedness occurs when standing up quickly causes a momentary drop in blood pressure, leading to brief lightheadedness, blurred vision, or feeling faint. Home Care: Sit or lie down flat immediately with legs elevated above heart level until feelings pass. Drink a glass of water. When waking or getting up, transition slowly: sit on the bed edge for 1 minute before standing. Ensure adequate salt and fluid intake unless medically restricted. Warning Signs: Sudden dizziness accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, loss of speech, or blackouts requires emergency hospital care.

topic: Vertigo, spinning sensation, room spinning, inner ear imbalance, BPPV
source_name: WHO - Ear and hearing care
content: Vertigo is the false sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning or swaying, often triggered by head position changes (Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo / BPPV) or inner ear inflammation (labyrinthitis). Home Care: Sit down immediately to prevent falls. Avoid sudden head turns or bending down rapidly. Rest in a well-lit room and focus gaze on a fixed point. When getting out of bed, move very slowly. Avoid driving or operating machinery. Warning Signs: Vertigo accompanied by double vision, slurred speech, arm or leg weakness, facial numbness, or inability to walk requires urgent emergency care.

topic: Motion sickness, car sickness, travel nausea, sea sickness
source_name: National Health Portal India - Travel health
content: Motion sickness occurs when conflicting sensory messages from the inner ears, eyes, and joints confuse the brain during travel in cars, buses, trains, or boats, causing nausea, cold sweats, and dizziness. Home Care: Sit in the front passenger seat of cars or over the wing on planes. Focus eyes on the distant horizon. Keep windows cracked open for fresh air. Sip cool water or ginger tea. Avoid reading or looking at phone screens while in motion. Eat light, non-greasy snacks before travel. Warning Signs: Persistent vomiting causing inability to retain fluids requires medical evaluation.

topic: Insomnia, trouble falling asleep, sleeplessness, sleep hygiene
source_name: WHO - Mental health and sleep guidance
