content: Insomnia involves persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking unrefreshed, often driven by stress, irregular schedules, late caffeine, or electronic screens. Home Care: Maintain a consistent sleep schedule: wake up at the same hour every day. Keep the bedroom dark, quiet, and cool. Stop screen time (phones, TV) 60 minutes before bed. Avoid heavy dinners, tea, coffee, and nicotine within 4 hours of bedtime. Practice relaxation, meditation, or light reading. Warning Signs: If chronic sleeplessness severely impairs daily functioning or is linked to severe depression, consult a doctor.

topic: Mild anxiety, nervous feelings, racing thoughts, stress calming
source_name: National Mental Health Programme India - Tele-MANAS
content: Mild situational anxiety is a normal human response to stressors like exams, interviews, or family changes, causing restlessness, rapid heartbeat, dry mouth, and racing thoughts. Home Care: Practice the 4-7-8 breathing technique: inhale slowly through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 7, and exhale through the mouth for 8 seconds. Go for a 20-minute brisk walk outdoors. Limit caffeine intake. Talk through your worries with a trusted family member or friend. Warning Signs: If anxiety causes severe panic attacks, chest tightness, or paralyzing fear, consult a doctor or call Tele-MANAS at 14416.

topic: Tele-MANAS national mental health helpline, emotional distress
source_name: MoHFW India - National Tele Mental Health Programme
content: Tele-MANAS is the Government of India's toll-free, 24/7 mental health helpline (dial 14416 or 1800-891-4416) providing free, confidential counseling by mental health professionals in English, Odia, Hindi, and regional languages. Guidance: Anyone experiencing overwhelming stress, persistent sadness, loneliness, relationship difficulties, exam pressure, or emotional pain can reach out safely. Service is free, confidential, and available day and night across Odisha. Warning Signs: For immediate life-threatening physical danger, always call 112 or 108.

topic: Hypertension lifestyle, high blood pressure management, DASH diet, salt reduction
source_name: WHO - Hypertension fact sheet
content: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is often called a 'silent killer' because it usually produces no noticeable symptoms while progressively straining the heart, brain, and kidneys. Lifestyle Care: Follow the DASH eating plan: eat plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy. Strictly limit dietary sodium to less than 5 grams of salt (about 1 teaspoon) per day across all meals. Avoid salted pickles, papads, and processed snacks. Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking) 5 days a week. Maintain a healthy body weight. Avoid tobacco and limit alcohol. Take prescribed BP medications faithfully without skipping. Warning Signs: Severe headache, chest pain, blurry vision, or shortness of breath requires urgent medical care.

topic: Varicose veins, swollen twisted leg veins, heavy aching legs
source_name: National Health Portal India - Vascular health
content: Varicose veins are enlarged, swollen, twisted veins (usually blue or dark purple) appearing on the calves and thighs, caused by weakened vein valves that allow blood to pool backward under gravity. Symptoms: Aching, heavy legs, ankle swelling, and restless legs after standing. Home Care: Elevate legs above hip level on pillows for 15-20 minutes 3 times a day. Wear graduated compression stockings put on first thing in the morning before getting out of bed. Avoid prolonged uninterrupted standing or sitting—take walking breaks every 45 minutes. Exercise regularly to activate calf muscle pumps. Maintain a healthy weight. Warning Signs: Painful skin ulcers near ankles, bleeding from a vein, or sudden red hot tender swelling in one calf (possible DVT) requires urgent medical care.

topic: Stroke FAST recognition, brain attack emergency signs, 108 ambulance protocol
source_name: WHO - Cardiovascular diseases and stroke
content: A stroke occurs when blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or reduced, depriving brain tissue of oxygen and nutrients. Brain cells begin dying within minutes. Protocol: Remember the F.A.S.T. warning signs: FACE: Ask the person to smile; does one side of the face droop? ARMS: Ask the person to raise both arms; does one arm drift downward or feel weak/numb? SPEECH: Ask the person to repeat a simple sentence; is their speech slurred, strange, or unable to speak? TIME: If you observe ANY of these signs, TIME IS CRITICAL—CALL 108 IMMEDIATELY for an emergency ambulance to a stroke-ready hospital. Do NOT give water, food, or aspirin before hospital CT scan confirmation.

topic: Heart attack warning signs, acute myocardial infarction, 108 emergency protocol
source_name: WHO - Cardiovascular emergencies
content: A heart attack occurs when blood flow to a portion of the heart muscle is severely blocked, typically by a blood clot in a coronary artery. Critical Symptoms: Severe, crushing, squeezing pressure, fullness, or pain in the center of the chest lasting more than a few minutes; pain radiating to the jaw, neck, back, left shoulder, or arm; accompanied by cold sweat, dizziness, shortness of breath, and unexplained nausea. In women and elderly persons with diabetes, chest pain may be subtle, presenting mainly as sudden breathlessness or extreme fatigue. Emergency Protocol: CALL 108 IMMEDIATELY or rush to the nearest emergency department. Have the patient sit comfortably resting; do not let them drive or walk.

topic: Urinary tract infection, UTI, burning urination, frequent urge to pee, dysuria
source_name: WHO - Guidelines on urinary tract infections
content: A UTI occurs when bacteria (usually E. coli) enter the urethra and bladder, causing a burning sensation during urination (dysuria), frequent intense urges to urinate with small output, cloudy or foul-smelling urine, and lower pelvic pain. Home Care: Drink plenty of water (at least 2.5 to 3 liters daily) to flush bacteria out of the urinary tract. Urinate frequently and do not hold urine. Wipe from front to back after using the toilet. Urinate shortly after sexual intercourse. Avoid irritants like perfumed soaps and tight synthetic underwear. Warning Signs: If you develop high fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, or back/flank pain, bacteria may have reached the kidneys (pyelonephritis); seek urgent hospital care.

topic: Dehydration urine color, dark yellow urine, hydration guide
source_name: National Health Portal India - Hydration
content: Urine color is a direct indicator of bodily hydration. Pale straw-yellow or clear urine indicates healthy hydration. Deep amber, honey, or dark yellow urine signals dehydration. Home Care: Drink 2 to 3 glasses of clean water immediately. In hot weather, outdoor manual labor, or during fever, increase fluid intake and drink coconut water, buttermilk, or ORS to maintain electrolyte balance. Warning Signs: If urine is cola-colored, red, or tea-colored despite drinking plenty of fluids, or accompanied by abdominal pain, consult a physician for liver or kidney assessment.

topic: Kidney stones, renal calculi, severe flank pain, pathari, hematuria
source_name: National Health Portal India - Kidney stones
content: Kidney stones are hard mineral and salt deposits (commonly calcium oxalate) that form inside the kidneys, causing excruciating, sharp, cramping pain in the back and flank below the ribs that radiates down to the lower abdomen and groin as stones move down the ureter, often with pink/red bloody urine, nausea, and burning on urination. Home Care: Drink large volumes of water (at least 3 liters daily) to help flush small stones (<5 mm). Drink lemon water (citrate naturally binds calcium to inhibit stone growth). Avoid skipping meals or becoming dehydrated in hot sun. Warning Signs: Inability to pass any urine, high fever with chills, uncontrollable pain, or severe vomiting requires immediate emergency hospital admission.

topic: Benign prostatic hyperplasia, BPH, weak urine stream, nighttime urination in older men
source_name: National Health Portal India - Prostate health
content: BPH is a common, non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland in aging men that pinches the urethra, leading to a weak or hesitant urine stream, straining to urinate, sensation of incomplete bladder emptying, and frequent waking up at night to urinate (nocturia). Home Care: Limit fluid intake in the 2 hours before bedtime to reduce nighttime waking. Avoid caffeine and alcohol which irritate the bladder. Practice double voiding: urinate, wait 30 seconds, and try to urinate again. Stay physically active. Avoid over-the-counter decongestants that tighten the prostate. Warning Signs: Complete inability to pass urine (acute urinary retention) is a medical emergency requiring urgent catheterization at a hospital.

topic: Jock itch, tinea cruris, severe groin itching, fungal rash in thigh creases
source_name: WHO - Fungal skin disease management
content: Jock itch (tinea cruris) is a fungal infection of the groin and inner thighs, thriving in warm, moist, friction-prone skin folds, producing an itchy, burning, red rash with elevated scaly borders. Common in athletes, laborers, and during humid monsoon months. Home Care: Keep the groin clean and thoroughly dry after bathing (dry groin with a separate towel from feet to prevent transferring athlete's foot fungus). Put socks on before underwear. Wear loose-fitting, breathable 100% cotton underwear and shorts. Apply prescribed topical antifungal cream for the full recommended 2-3 weeks. Never apply steroid creams. Warning Signs: If the rash spreads to the scrotum, blisters, or oozes pus, visit a doctor.

topic: Testicular pain emergency, testicular torsion, sudden severe scrotum pain
source_name: National Health Portal India - Men's health emergencies
content: Sudden, severe, sharp pain in one testicle accompanied by swelling, redness of the scrotum, nausea, or abdominal pain can indicate TESTICULAR TORSION (the testicle rotates, twisting the spermatic cord and cutting off its blood supply). This is a surgical EMERGENCY: blood flow must be surgically restored within 6 hours to prevent permanent loss of the testicle. Protocol: Do NOT wait or attempt home remedies; go IMMEDIATELY to the nearest hospital emergency room. For mild gradual ache due to epididymitis, wear a supportive athletic supporter or snug briefs and rest, but always obtain medical examination.

topic: Balanitis, redness and swelling of foreskin and glans penis
source_name: National Health Portal India - Men's health
content: Balanitis is inflammation of the head of the penis (glans) and the foreskin, commonly caused by poor hygiene, trapped moisture, soap irritation, or Candida yeast infection. Symptoms include redness, soreness, itching, foul-smelling smegma under the foreskin, and pain when retracting the foreskin. Home Care: Gently pull back the foreskin daily during bathing and wash the glans with plain warm water (avoid harsh scented soaps or bubble baths). Dry completely before pulling the foreskin back into normal position. Wear loose cotton underwear. Apply prescribed antifungal or mild soothing cream. Warning Signs: If you cannot pull the foreskin back forward over the glans (paraphimosis), go to emergency care immediately.

topic: Pregnancy danger signs, emergency obstetric signs, call 108 ambulance Odisha
source_name: WHO - Maternal health: danger signs in pregnancy
content: Certain symptoms during pregnancy indicate life-threatening complications for the mother or fetus requiring IMMEDIATE emergency hospital care (call 108 or Janani Express): Any vaginal bleeding or spotting; severe persistent headache with blurred vision, spots before eyes, or swelling of face and hands (preeclampsia/eclampsia); convulsions or seizures; high fever; severe continuous abdominal pain; sudden gush or leakage of fluid from vagina (premature rupture of membranes); reduced or absent fetal movements in the third trimester; or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Do not wait for routine antenatal clinic days; seek emergency hospital care immediately.

topic: Morning sickness, nausea and vomiting in early pregnancy, hyperemesis care
source_name: WHO - Antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience
content: Morning sickness (nausea and vomiting) is very common in the first trimester of pregnancy due to rising pregnancy hormones like hCG and progesterone. Home Care: Eat small, frequent meals every 2-3 hours; avoid having an empty stomach. Keep dry crackers, roasted chana, or plain biscuits by your bedside and eat a couple before getting out of bed in the morning. Sip ginger tea, lemon water, or cold water throughout the day. Avoid greasy, highly spiced, or strong-smelling foods. Get plenty of rest. Warning Signs: If you cannot keep any liquids or food down for 24 hours, lose weight, feel severely dizzy, or urine turns dark and scanty (hyperemesis gravidarum), see a doctor immediately for IV fluids.

topic: Anemia in pregnancy, Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) red tablets, Odisha guidelines
source_name: MoHFW India - Anemia Mukt Bharat Guidelines
content: Nutritional iron deficiency anemia is widespread during pregnancy and increases risks of maternal exhaustion, low birth weight, and postpartum hemorrhage. Protocol: Under the Government of India's Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines, pregnant women must take 1 Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) red tablet daily for at least 180 days starting from the second trimester (after 12-14 weeks), continuing for 180 days postpartum. Take IFA with water or lemon water after food; vitamin C enhances iron absorption. Never take IFA with tea, coffee, or milk as calcium and tannins block iron absorption. Eat iron-rich foods: green leafy vegetables, jaggery, drumstick leaves, lentils, and eggs.

topic: Exclusive breastfeeding in the first 6 months, colostrum feeding, infant nutrition
source_name: WHO - Infant and young child feeding
content: Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of birth. The thick yellowish first milk, COLOSTRUM, is packed with antibodies and acts as the baby's first natural immunization; never discard it. Practice EXCLUSIVE BREASTFEEDING for the first 6 full months of life: give the baby ONLY breast milk—no plain water, no gripe water, no honey, no animal milk, and no infant formula, even in hot summer weather (breast milk is over 80% water and provides complete hydration and nutrition). Exclusive breastfeeding protects infants against life-threatening diarrhea and respiratory infections. Introduce soft complementary foods along with continued breastfeeding at 6 months.

topic: Diaper rash, red irritated infant bottom, nappy dermatitis care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Infant skin care
content: Diaper rash is irritation and inflammation of an infant's bottom caused by prolonged contact with wet or soiled diapers, friction, and lack of air circulation. Home Care: Change diapers immediately when wet or soiled. Clean the baby's bottom gently with warm water and soft cotton cloth; avoid alcohol-based or perfumed wipes. Pat the skin gently until completely dry—never rub. Allow the baby to have diaper-free time for several hours daily so fresh air reaches the skin. Apply a thick protective barrier layer of plain petroleum jelly or zinc oxide cream at every diaper change. Warning Signs: If the rash develops bright red satellite pimples with white pus (Candida yeast infection), visit an ASHA worker or doctor for antifungal cream.

topic: Infantile colic, inconsolable crying in healthy baby, rule of threes
source_name: National Health Portal India - Child health
content: Colic is repeated episodes of intense, inconsolable crying in an otherwise healthy, well-fed infant, often occurring in the late afternoon or evening, characterized by clenched fists, red face, and knees drawn up to the tummy ('rule of threes': crying >3 hours a day, >3 days a week, for >3 weeks). Home Care: Burp the infant thoroughly during and after every feed. Hold the baby upright against your chest or gently rock them in your arms. Try gentle rhythmic motion or soothing white noise (gentle shushing). Massage the baby's tummy gently in clockwise circles or gently cycle their legs. Avoid feeding cow's milk. Remember that colic is temporary and naturally resolves by 3 to 4 months of age. Warning Signs: Fever, vomiting, bloody stools, or poor weight gain requires medical evaluation.

topic: Teething pain in babies, drooling, sore gums, baby chewing on objects
source_name: National Health Portal India - Infant dental health
content: Teething occurs when primary teeth begin emerging through the infant's gums (usually around 6 to 12 months), causing increased drooling, tender swollen gums, irritability, sleep disruption, and a desire to chew on firm objects. Home Care: Gently massage the baby's gums with a clean finger. Give the baby a firm, solid rubber teething ring chilled in the refrigerator (never in the freezer, as frozen rings can injure delicate gums). Offer a cool, clean, damp washcloth to chew on. Wipe drool from the baby's chin and neck frequently to prevent saliva rash. Avoid teething necklaces, amber beads, or numbing gels containing benzocaine (which can cause methemoglobinemia). Warning Signs: High fever, diarrhea, or vomiting is NOT caused by teething and requires medical checkup.

topic: Cradle cap, infantile seborrheic dermatitis, greasy yellowish scalp flakes in newborns
source_name: National Health Portal India - Infant care
content: Cradle cap is a harmless, non-itchy condition in infants causing thick, greasy, yellowish or brown crusty scales on the scalp, driven by maternal hormones stimulating the baby's oil glands. Home Care: Cradle cap is benign and not caused by poor hygiene. Wash the baby's hair daily with a gentle baby shampoo. Massage a few drops of pure coconut oil or mineral oil into the baby's scalp 15 minutes before bathing to loosen the crusts, then gently brush with a soft baby brush or comb during shampooing. Rinse thoroughly. Never vigorously pick or scrape scales with fingernails. The condition resolves naturally over several months. Warning Signs: If the scalp becomes bright red, swollen, oozes pus, or spreads to the face, consult a doctor.

topic: Childhood fever home care, lukewarm sponging, paracetamol guidelines, febrile fit
source_name: WHO - Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI)
content: Fever is the body's natural immune defense fighting an infection. Home Care: Dress the child in light, breathable cotton clothing and keep the room well-ventilated. Give plenty of fluids: breast milk, water, ORS, or soups to prevent dehydration. If the child is uncomfortable or body temperature is high (>38.5C / 101.3F), sponge the forehead, neck, and limbs with LUKEWARM tap water (never use cold ice water or alcohol, which causes severe shivering and spikes core temperature). Paracetamol syrup may be administered strictly according to body weight under doctor/ASHA guidance; NEVER give aspirin to children due to Reye's syndrome risk. Warning Signs: Inability to drink, extreme lethargy, stiff neck, persistent vomiting, or seizures requires immediate hospital admission.

topic: Measles warning signs, rubeola virus, koplik spots, red rash and high fever in children
source_name: WHO - Measles fact sheet
content: Measles is a highly contagious airborne viral disease in unvaccinated children. Symptoms begin with high fever, runny nose, red watery eyes (conjunctivitis), cough, and tiny white spots with red centers inside the mouth (Koplik spots), followed 3-5 days later by a blotchy red rash spreading from the face and hairline downward across the body. Protocol: Measles can cause severe complications like pneumonia, blindness, and brain swelling (encephalitis). Ensure the child receives 2 doses of Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine at 9 months and 16-24 months under the Universal Immunization Programme. Keep sick children isolated. Administer 2 doses of Vitamin A syrup under health worker supervision. Warning Signs: Rapid breathing, chest indrawing, stridor, or convulsions requires immediate hospital emergency care.

topic: Dengue fever, aedes mosquito, high fever, joint pain, platelet warning signs
source_name: WHO - Dengue and severe dengue fact sheet
content: Dengue is a viral infection transmitted by day-biting Aedes mosquitoes. Symptoms: Sudden high fever, severe retro-orbital eye pain, bone and joint aches ('breakbone fever'), skin rash, and nausea. Home Care: Rest completely in bed under a mosquito net to prevent infecting others. Hydrate vigorously with ORS, coconut water, fruit juices, and soups to prevent hemoconcentration. Paracetamol can be taken for fever; NEVER take aspirin, ibuprofen, or diclofenac as they increase bleeding risks. Warning Signs: Seek emergency hospital care immediately if you notice severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding from gums/nose, black stools, extreme restlessness, or sudden drop in body temperature with clammy skin.

topic: Malaria, anopheles mosquito, cyclical chills, high fever, sweating paroxysms
source_name: WHO - Malaria fact sheet
content: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through bites of female Anopheles mosquitoes. Symptoms: Cyclical attacks (paroxysms) of intense cold shivering and chills, followed by spiking high fever, and concluding with profuse drenching sweating and exhaustion. Protocol: In Odisha, malaria is widespread; test immediately at any CHC, PHC, or with an ASHA worker using Rapid Diagnostic Kits (RDK) or blood smear. Complete the full prescribed course of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT). Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets (LLIN). Clear stagnant water collections. Warning Signs: Confusion, convulsions, inability to sit, or jaundice indicates cerebral/severe malaria requiring immediate emergency hospital care.

topic: Rabies prevention, dog bite first aid, animal scratch protocol
source_name: WHO - Rabies fact sheet
content: Rabies is a 100% fatal but 100% preventable viral disease transmitted through the saliva of infected mammals (dogs, cats, monkeys, bats) via bites, scratches, or contact with broken skin. Emergency First Aid: IMMEDIATELY wash the bite or scratch wound thoroughly under running tap water with soap for at least 15 FULL MINUTES. Apply povidone-iodine or antiseptic. Do NOT apply chili powder, lime, oil, or turmeric to the wound. Do NOT bandage or suture the wound tightly. Go IMMEDIATELY to the nearest Government Hospital for Anti-Rabies Vaccine (ARV) and Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG). Starting vaccination on Day 0 is crucial.

topic: Typhoid fever, enteric fever, salmonella typhi, step-ladder fever
source_name: WHO - Typhoid fact sheet
content: Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi spread through contaminated food and drinking water. Symptoms: Sustained high fever rising in a step-ladder pattern, headache, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhea, weakness, and dry cough. Prevention & Care: Drink only boiled or certified purified water. Wash hands thoroughly before eating. Eat freshly cooked, hot food; peel fruits yourself. Avoid raw roadside street foods. Typhoid requires prescription antibiotics following blood/Widal testing. Warning Signs: Severe persistent abdominal pain, vomiting blood, or confusion indicates intestinal perforation requiring urgent surgery.

topic: Chikungunya, viral fever, severe incapacitating joint pain
source_name: WHO - Chikungunya fact sheet
content: Chikungunya is a viral disease spread by Aedes mosquitoes characterized by sudden fever and debilitating, severe joint pain (polyarthralgia), commonly in wrists, hands, and ankles, often accompanied by rash. Home Care: Rest completely. Stay well-hydrated with fluids and ORS. Apply cold compresses to swollen, tender joints to ease stiffness. Paracetamol may be used for fever under health worker guidance; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs until dengue is ruled out. Joint pain may persist for weeks or months. Warning Signs: Inability to drink fluids, severe drowsiness, or bleeding requires immediate hospital care.

topic: Cholera, rice-water stools, explosive watery diarrhea, rapid dehydration
source_name: WHO - Cholera fact sheet
content: Cholera is an acute bacterial diarrheal infection caused by ingestion of food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae. Hallmark symptom: Sudden onset of profuse, painless, watery diarrhea resembling cloudy 'rice-water', accompanied by rapid vomiting and leg cramps. Severe cases can cause lethal dehydration and circulatory collapse within hours if untreated. Emergency Protocol: IMMEDIATELY begin drinking Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) in continuous large volumes and rush to the nearest Community Health Centre or District Hospital. Intravenous (IV) fluids and antibiotics save lives. In communities, boil all drinking water and chlorinate water sources.

topic: Leptospirosis, flood water fever, mud water exposure, rat urine infection
source_name: WHO - Leptospirosis guidance
content: Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease caused by Leptospira interrogans shed in the urine of infected animals (especially rats) that contaminates flood waters, soil, and mud, entering through skin cuts or mucous membranes during monsoons or agricultural work. Symptoms: High fever, severe headache, intense calf muscle pain, chills, and red suffused eyes without discharge. Prevention & Care: Avoid wading barefoot in flood waters or stagnant muddy puddles; wear rubber gumboots. Wash limbs with soap and water after field work. Take prophylactic doxycycline if advised by health authorities during flood relief. Warning Signs: Yellow jaundice, dark cola urine, reduced urination, or bleeding (Weil's disease) requires immediate hospital admission.

topic: Scrub typhus, mite-borne fever, chigger bite, black eschar mark
source_name: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) India - Scrub typhus guidelines
content: Scrub typhus is an acute infectious bacterial disease caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi transmitted by the bite of larval trombiculid mites ('chiggers') found in dense scrub vegetation and agricultural fields. Hallmark sign: A characteristic painless, cigarette-burn-like black scab with a red halo called an 'eschar' at the bite site (often in groin, armpits, or neck), accompanied by high fever, severe headache, muscle aches, and swollen lymph nodes. Protocol: Scrub typhus responds rapidly to specific antibiotics (like doxycycline) if started early; report immediately to a CHC or PHC. Avoid sitting directly on grassy ground; wear long pants tucked into socks in fields.

topic: Lymphatic filariasis, elephantiasis, swollen leg, mosquito-borne parasitic worm, MDA
source_name: WHO - Lymphatic filariasis fact sheet
content: Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis) is caused by microscopic filarial worms transmitted through repeated bites of Culex mosquitoes that damage the lymphatic vessels, leading to chronic abnormal swelling (lymphedema) of the legs, arms, or scrotum (hydrocele), and thickened, pebbled skin. Prevention & Home Care: Take the annual Mass Drug Administration (MDA) preventive tablets (DEC and Albendazole) distributed by health workers. For established swollen limbs: Practice meticulous limb hygiene: wash the affected leg daily with clean water and mild soap, dry completely between toes, elevate the limb during sleep, perform regular gentle ankle exercises, and wear comfortable footwear to prevent secondary bacterial attacks. Hydrocele can be corrected by free government surgery.

topic: Leprosy, Hansen's disease, pale numb skin patch, free MDT treatment Odisha
source_name: WHO - Leprosy (Hansen's disease) fact sheet
content: Leprosy (Hansen's disease) is a chronic, non-fatal, curable infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae. Early Signs: Single or few pale, reddish, or hypopigmented flat skin patches that show COMPLETE LOSS OF SENSATION (numb to light touch, pinprick, or heat/cold) with loss of sweating and hair over the patch, or thickened peripheral nerves. Protocol: Leprosy is completely curable and NOT a curse. The Government of Odisha provides Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) completely FREE at all PHCs and CHCs. Early treatment within weeks prevents all nerve damage, claw hands, foot drop, and disability. MDT stops transmission immediately after the very first dose.

topic: Minor burns, thermal scalds, boiling water burns, first-degree burn first aid
source_name: WHO - Burns fact sheet
content: Minor first-degree burns affect only the outer skin layer, causing redness, swelling, and pain without large open blisters. First Aid: IMMEDIATELY cool the burn under gentle, cool running tap water for 15 to 20 minutes (do NOT use freezing ice or ice water, as extreme cold causes frostbite damage to burned tissue). Do NOT apply toothpaste, butter, raw egg, ghee, or mud, which introduce bacterial infections. Cover loosely with a clean, dry, sterile cloth. Warning Signs: If burns cover large areas, face, hands, groin, or result in charred white/black skin (third-degree), go immediately to the hospital burn unit.

topic: Snake bite emergency, venomous snakebite first aid, anti-snake venom
source_name: WHO - Snakebite envenoming fact sheet
content: Snakebites from venomous snakes (Cobras, Kraits, Vipers) are life-threatening medical emergencies. Protocol: Call 108 or arrange immediate transport to a Community Health Centre with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV). Keep the victim calm and strictly IMMOBILIZE the bitten limb below heart level with a splint. Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing before swelling begins. DO NOT cut the wound with blades. DO NOT attempt to suck out venom. DO NOT tie a tight tourniquet (which causes gangrene). DO NOT apply herbal pastes or electrical shocks. Administering ASV at a hospital is the ONLY effective cure.

topic: Choking first aid, airway obstruction, Heimlich maneuver, adult and child
source_name: WHO - Emergency trauma care
content: Choking occurs when a foreign object lodges in the throat or windpipe, blocking the flow of air. If the person can cough forcefully, encourage them to keep coughing. If the person CANNOT speak, cry, cough, or breathe (universal choking sign: hands clutching throat): Act immediately. Stand behind the person, wrap arms around waist, make a fist with one hand just above the navel, grasp the fist with the other hand, and give quick, upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) until the object is expelled. For unconscious choking victims, call 108 and begin chest compressions immediately.

topic: Heat exhaustion, extreme summer heat, Odisha loo, heat cramps
source_name: NDMA India - National guidelines on heat wave management
content: Heat exhaustion results from prolonged exposure to high temperatures and inadequate fluid/salt replacement. Symptoms: Heavy sweating, paleness, muscle cramps, tiredness, weakness, dizziness, headache, and nausea. First Aid: Move the person immediately to a cool, shaded, or air-conditioned room. Loosen or remove tight clothing. Apply cool, wet towels to the neck, forehead, and armpits. Give cool water, ORS, or salted lemon water in small sips. Fan the person. Warning Signs: If body temperature exceeds 40C (104F), sweating ceases, or the person becomes confused, unconscious, or delirious, this is HEAT STROKE—call 108 immediately.

topic: Minor cuts, scrapes, abrasions, wound cleaning, antiseptic dressing
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid cuts
content: Minor cuts and scrapes break the skin surface with minimal bleeding. First Aid: Wash hands with soap. Apply direct gentle pressure with a clean cloth for 2-3 minutes to stop bleeding. Clean the wound under gentle running tap water to wash away dirt and debris. Clean around the wound with mild soap. Apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly or antiseptic ointment to keep the surface moist. Cover with a sterile adhesive bandage. Change the bandage daily. Warning Signs: If the cut is deep, gaping, caused by rusty objects, or shows signs of redness, warmth, and pus, visit a clinic for stitches or a tetanus toxoid (TT) booster.

topic: Hypoglycemia in diabetes, low blood sugar warning signs, rule of 15 emergency care
source_name: WHO - Diabetes fact sheet
content: Hypoglycemia (blood glucose dropping below 70 mg/dL) is an acute danger in people taking diabetes medications or insulin who delay meals or exercise heavily. Symptoms: Trembling, rapid heartbeat, cold clammy sweating, intense hunger, dizziness, anxiety, blurred vision, and confusion. Emergency Protocol (Rule of 15): IMMEDIATELY consume 15 grams of fast-acting simple carbohydrates: 3 teaspoons of sugar or honey dissolved in water, half a cup of fruit juice, or 4 glucose tablets. Wait 15 minutes and check blood sugar if a meter is available. If still low or symptoms persist, take another 15 grams of sugar. Once recovered, eat a proper meal. Warning Signs: If the person becomes unconscious or unable to swallow, do NOT force liquids; call 108 immediately.

topic: Type 2 diabetes lifestyle management, blood sugar control, diet and walking
source_name: WHO - Diabetes management guidelines
content: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder where the body cannot effectively use insulin. Lifestyle Care: Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking) daily, which increases muscle insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose naturally. Follow a plate method diet: fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables (greens, beans, cucumber), one quarter with complex whole grains (brown rice, whole wheat, millets like ragi), and one quarter with protein (dal, lentils, eggs, fish). Completely avoid white refined sugar, sweetened tea, and sodas. Inspect feet daily for cuts or blisters. Have HbA1c checked every 3 to 6 months. Warning Signs: Fruity smelling breath, extreme thirst with confusion, or non-healing foot ulcers requires immediate hospital care.

topic: Fall prevention in older adults, elderly home safety, balance and lighting
source_name: WHO - Step safely: strategies for preventing and managing falls across the life-course
content: Falls are a leading cause of bone fractures (especially hip fractures), head injuries, and loss of independence among elderly individuals. Home Care & Prevention: Ensure adequate lighting in bedrooms, stairways, and corridors with night lamps. Remove loose rugs, floor mats, clutter, and electrical cords. Install sturdy grab bars beside the toilet and in the shower area, and use non-slip rubber bath mats. Keep frequently used kitchen and household items at waist level to avoid climbing on stools. Check vision and hearing annually. Wear non-skid flat footwear with firm heel support inside the home. Practice gentle balance exercises like walking or yoga. Warning Signs: Any fall resulting in inability to stand, severe hip pain, or head strike requires immediate hospital X-ray and evaluation.

topic: Bee and wasp stings, insect envenomation, stinger removal, local swelling
source_name: WHO - Management of venomous stings and bites
content: Bee and wasp stings inject venom that causes immediate sharp burning pain, redness, and localized swelling at the sting site. First Aid: Scrape the sting site immediately with a fingernail, dull knife, or credit card edge to remove the venom sac (do not squeeze the stinger with tweezers, which pumps more venom into the skin). Wash the area with soap and water. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 10-15 minutes to reduce pain and swelling. Apply calamine lotion. Elevate the stung arm or leg if swollen. Warning Signs: If within minutes the person develops difficulty breathing, wheezing, swelling of the throat or lips, generalized hives, or dizziness (anaphylaxis), call 108 or inject an EpiPen immediately.

topic: Six steps of proper handwashing, infection prevention, soap and water technique
source_name: WHO - Hand hygiene guidelines
content: Proper handwashing with soap and clean running water is the single most effective, low-cost public health intervention preventing diarrhea and respiratory infections. Steps (20-30 seconds): 1. Wet hands with clean water and apply soap. 2. Rub palms together to create lather. 3. Rub the back of each hand with the opposite palm with fingers interlaced. 4. Interlace fingers and rub palms together. 5. Rub the backs of fingers against opposing palms with fingers interlocked. 6. Rotational rubbing of each thumb clasped in the opposite palm. 7. Rub rotational tips of fingers in each palm. Rinse thoroughly and dry with a clean single-use towel or air dry. Critical times: Before preparing or eating food, after using the toilet, after cleaning a child's bottom, and after coughing or sneezing.

topic: Chilblains, swollen painful red itchy toes and fingers in winter, pernio
source_name: National Health Portal India - Winter health
content: Chilblains (pernio) are painful, itchy, red or purple swellings on the extremities (toes, fingers, earlobes) caused by sudden rewarming after cold, damp exposure, constricting small blood vessels. Home Care: Keep extremities warm and dry with warm wool socks and gloves. Warm cold feet and hands GRADUALLY (never place cold feet directly in front of hot heaters or boiling water, which worsens vascular spasms). Exercise indoors to stimulate circulation. Avoid smoking. Warning Signs: If skin cracks, forms open ulcers, or signs of infection appear, visit a doctor.

topic: Keratosis pilaris, rough chicken skin bumps on upper arms and thighs
source_name: National Health Portal India - Common skin conditions
content: Keratosis pilaris is a harmless genetic skin condition where dead skin cells plug hair follicles, causing dry, rough, tiny sandpaper-like bumps resembling 'goosebumps' on the back of upper arms and thighs. Home Care: It is completely harmless and non-infectious. Moisturize daily with thick creams containing urea or lactic acid immediately after bathing. Use mild soap-free cleansers and avoid harsh scrubbing with loofahs which aggravates irritation. Take short lukewarm showers. Warning Signs: Does not require emergency care; consult a dermatologist if severely inflamed.

topic: Pityriasis versicolor, tinea versicolor, discolored light or dark patches on chest and back
source_name: WHO - Fungal skin disease management
content: Pityriasis versicolor is a common, non-contagious superficial fungal infection caused by Malassezia yeast overgrowth, producing patches of discolored skin (lighter or darker than surrounding skin) with fine scaling on the chest, back, and upper arms in hot, humid weather. Home Care: Wash skin with antidandruff shampoo containing selenium sulfide or ketoconazole, lathering onto affected areas for 10 minutes before rinsing, twice weekly. Keep skin cool and dry. Wear loose cotton shirts. Full skin color may take months to normalize after the fungus is cleared.

topic: Pityriasis rosea, herald patch, oval pink scaly rash in Christmas tree pattern
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin rashes
content: Pityriasis rosea is a benign, self-limiting skin rash that begins with a single larger oval scaly red spot ('herald patch') on the chest or back, followed 1 to 2 weeks later by smaller oval pink spots distributed along skin cleavage lines ('Christmas tree pattern'). Home Care: The condition is harmless, non-contagious, and resolves on its own over 6 to 10 weeks. Use lukewarm baths and mild moisturizers to relieve dryness. Apply calamine lotion for itching. Avoid hot showers and harsh soaps. Warning Signs: Consult a doctor if the rash lasts over 3 months or affects the palms and soles (to rule out secondary syphilis).

topic: Dyshidrotic eczema, pompholyx, intensely itchy tiny clear blisters on sides of fingers and palms
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eczema guidelines
content: Dyshidrotic eczema (pompholyx) is a distinct form of eczema causing clusters of intensely itchy, deep-seated, tiny clear blisters ('tapioca pudding appearance') along the edges of fingers, palms, and soles, often triggered by stress, sweating, metal allergies (nickel), or frequent handwashing. Home Care: Soak hands in cool water compresses for 15 minutes twice daily to dry blisters. Apply thick petroleum jelly immediately afterward. Wear cotton gloves under rubber gloves during wet chores. Avoid harsh detergents and nickel jewelry. Warning Signs: If blisters burst with yellow pus or hands become red, hot, and painful, seek medical care for secondary bacterial infection.

topic: Sebaceous cyst, epidermoid cyst, painless moveable lump under skin with central punctum
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin cysts
content: An epidermoid cyst is a slow-growing, benign sac beneath the skin filled with cheesy keratin protein, feeling like a smooth, round, painless marble that moves easily under the skin, often with a tiny black central pore. Home Care: Leave undisturbed; cysts are non-cancerous and harmless unless inflamed. Apply a warm moist compress for 10 minutes if tender. NEVER squeeze, pop, or attempt to lance a cyst at home, as this introduces severe bacterial infection and leaves scar tissue. If removal is desired, have a surgeon excise the entire cyst wall safely.

topic: Lipoma, soft painless fatty lump under skin
source_name: National Health Portal India - Benign growths
content: A lipoma is a slow-growing, completely benign tumor of fat tissue located between the skin and underlying muscle layer. It feels soft, doughy, moves readily under slight finger pressure, and is typically painless. Home Care: Lipomas are harmless and non-cancerous. No home treatment is required. Do not massage or press aggressively. Medical removal is purely elective if it presses on a nerve or for cosmetic reasons. Warning Signs: If a lump grows rapidly, becomes firm and immovable, or causes persistent pain, seek medical evaluation to rule out other conditions.

topic: Subungual hematoma, blood blister under crushed fingernail or toenail
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail trauma first aid
content: A subungual hematoma is a pool of blood beneath a fingernail or toenail following direct blunt trauma, such as slamming a finger in a door or dropping a heavy object on a toe, causing throbbing pain and dark purple-black discoloration under the nail. Home Care: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth immediately for 15 minutes. Elevate the hand or foot above heart level to reduce throbbing and swelling. If the injury is small (<25% of nail area) and pain eases, the nail will gradually grow out with the dark mark over several months. Warning Signs: If severe throbbing pain is unbearable, or blood covers more than half the nail, visit a clinic where a doctor can perform quick painless trephination (tiny hole to release pressure).

topic: Brittle nails, peeling splitting fingernails, onychoschizia
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail care
content: Brittle nails (onychoschizia) involve fingernails that split, chip, peel, or break easily, commonly caused by repeated wetting and drying of hands, harsh cleaning chemicals, nail polish removers, or nutritional deficiencies (iron, biotin). Home Care: Wear protective rubber gloves lined with cotton when washing dishes or doing laundry. Keep nails trimmed short and rounded to prevent snagging. Apply petroleum jelly, coconut oil, or moisturizer to cuticles and nails daily, especially after washing hands. Limit acetone nail polish removers. Eat balanced iron-rich foods. Warning Signs: Nails that turn spoon-shaped (koilonychia) indicate severe iron deficiency anemia requiring blood testing.

topic: Angular cheilitis, painful cracking and sores at corners of mouth, perleche
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral care
content: Angular cheilitis is inflammation and deep painful cracking at one or both corners of the mouth, caused by saliva accumulating in skin folds that creates a warm, moist breeding ground for Candida yeast or Staph bacteria. Home Care: Apply petroleum jelly or zinc oxide ointment to mouth corners to create a water-resistant barrier against saliva. Avoid licking the corners of your mouth. Clean and sanitize dentures daily. Ensure adequate dietary B-vitamins and iron. Apply doctor-prescribed antifungal or antibacterial ointment. Warning Signs: If lesions fail to heal after 2 weeks, consult a physician.

topic: Caterpillar dermatitis, stinging caterpillar rash, itchy hives from hairy caterpillars
source_name: WHO - Environmental health and envenomation
content: Caterpillar dermatitis occurs when fine, brittle, venomous hairs (setae) from hairy caterpillars lodge in the skin after direct contact or airborne dispersion from trees, releasing toxins that trigger immediate intense stinging, burning, itchy hives, and red welts. First Aid: IMMEDIATELY apply adhesive cellophane tape (Scotch tape) to the skin and peel it off repeatedly to pull out embedded toxic hairs. Wash the area thoroughly with soap and water without scrubbing roughly. Apply cold ice compresses and calamine lotion. Avoid scratching. Warning Signs: If hairs enter the eyes, or if facial swelling and breathlessness develop, seek emergency hospital care.

topic: Spider bite first aid, non-venomous spider marks, localized redness and swelling
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid bites
content: Most common domestic spider bites in India are from non-venomous spiders, producing minor localized symptoms: two tiny puncture marks, mild redness, swelling, and itching similar to a bee or mosquito sting. First Aid: Wash the bite area gently with soap and water. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a clean cloth for 10-15 minutes to reduce swelling. Apply calamine lotion. Keep the bitten area clean and elevated. Do not scratch. Warning Signs: If the bite develops a dark black necrotic center, spreading red streaks, severe muscle cramps, abdominal rigidity, or fever, seek urgent hospital medical care.

topic: Heat edema, swollen hands and feet in hot summer weather
source_name: National Health Portal India - Heat illness
content: Heat edema is harmless, mild swelling of the hands, ankles, and feet that occurs when blood vessels dilate in response to high ambient temperatures, causing fluid to pool in dependent extremities under gravity. Home Care: Elevate feet on pillows above hip level while resting. Move to a cool, shaded, well-ventilated room or use a fan. Stay adequately hydrated with cool plain water. Avoid tight footwear, tight rings, and restrictive clothing. Avoid high-salt foods. Do not take over-the-counter water pills (diuretics) as they worsen dehydration. Swelling resolves naturally as the body acclimates to heat. Warning Signs: Swelling in only one leg with calf pain, or swelling accompanied by shortness of breath, requires urgent medical evaluation.

topic: Solar lentigo, age spots, liver spots, harmless sun-induced brown spots
source_name: WHO - Ultraviolet radiation health risks
content: Solar lentigines (age spots or liver spots) are harmless, flat, oval brown or black spots appearing on chronically sun-exposed areas (face, hands, shoulders, forearms) due to localized ultraviolet-induced melanin production, common in older adults. Home Care: Age spots are completely benign and do not turn into skin cancer. No medical treatment is needed. Protect skin from further ultraviolet exposure by applying sunscreen daily and wearing long-sleeved clothing. Warning Signs: Consult a dermatologist if a spot changes size, develops irregular jagged borders, displays multiple uneven colors, bleeds, or itches persistently (ABCDE melanoma rules).

topic: Lichen planus, purple itchy flat-topped polygonal skin bumps
source_name: National Health Portal India - Inflammatory skin diseases
content: Lichen planus is a non-contagious inflammatory condition affecting the skin and mucous membranes, classically presenting as shiny, flat-topped, intensely itchy, purple or reddish polygonal bumps on the wrists, ankles, and lower back, often with a fine network of white lines (Wickham's striae). Home Care: Apply cool damp compresses to soothe itching. Take lukewarm baths and apply plain emollient moisturizers. Avoid scratching to prevent the Koebner phenomenon (new lesions forming along scratch lines). Wear soft cotton clothing. Consult a physician for prescription topical anti-inflammatory creams.

topic: Subconjunctival hemorrhage, broken blood vessel in eye, harmless red eye patch
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye health
content: A subconjunctival hemorrhage is a broken fragile capillary beneath the clear conjunctiva, creating a bright red, painless blood patch on the white of the eye, often triggered by violent coughing, sneezing, straining, or rubbing eyes. Home Care: The condition looks alarming but is harmless and does not damage vision. No drops are required; the pooled blood naturally reabsorbs over 10 to 14 days, like a skin bruise turning from red to yellowish-green. Avoid rubbing the eye. Warning Signs: Seek immediate medical care if accompanied by eye pain, changes in vision, discharge, or following severe blunt trauma to the eye.

topic: Eye twitching, myokymia, involuntary eyelid fluttering, eyelid spasm
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye health
content: Eyelid myokymia is a harmless, involuntary, gentle twitching or fluttering of the lower or upper eyelid muscle, commonly triggered by high stress, fatigue, lack of sleep, excessive caffeine intake (strong tea/coffee), or eye strain. Home Care: Get adequate nightly rest and prioritize 7-8 hours of sleep. Reduce tea, coffee, and energy drinks. Take frequent screen breaks. Apply a warm compress to the eye for 5 minutes. Practice relaxation and deep breathing. Eyelid twitches typically resolve on their own within days. Warning Signs: If the twitching spreads to the cheek or mouth, forces the entire eye shut, or persists longer than 3 weeks, consult a neurologist.

topic: Arc eye, welder's flash, photokeratitis, ultraviolet corneal burn
source_name: WHO - Occupational health and eye safety
content: Photokeratitis (welder's flash or arc eye) is a painful corneal burn caused by unprotected exposure to ultraviolet radiation from welding torches, tanning lamps, or intense sun reflection off water or snow. Symptoms develop 6 to 12 hours later: severe gritty eye pain, profuse tearing, bloodshot eyes, extreme light sensitivity, and swollen eyelids. First Aid: Rest in a completely darkened room. Keep eyes closed. Apply cool damp washcloths over closed eyes. Remove contact lenses immediately. Wear dark sunglasses. DO NOT rub eyes. The corneal epithelium naturally regenerates within 24 to 48 hours. Warning Signs: Severe persistent pain or loss of vision requires emergency ophthalmology evaluation for antibiotic eye ointment.

topic: Pinguecula and pterygium, surfer's eye, yellowish fleshy growth on eye white
source_name: WHO - Blindness and visual impairment
content: A pinguecula is a yellowish raised bump, and a pterygium is a fleshy triangular growth of conjunctival tissue spreading from the inner corner toward the cornea, caused by long-term exposure to outdoor ultraviolet sunlight, wind, and airborne dust. Home Care: Protect eyes outdoors by wearing wrap-around UV-blocking sunglasses and wide-brimmed hats. Use lubricating artificial tear drops to soothe dryness and redness. Avoid rubbing the eyes. Warning Signs: If a pterygium grows across the cornea toward the pupil, threatening vision, or causes persistent inflammation, consult an ophthalmologist for surgical excision.

topic: Eye floaters and flashes warning signs, posterior vitreous detachment triage
source_name: WHO - Prevention of blindness
content: Eye floaters are microscopic clumps within the vitreous gel casting shadows on the retina, seen as tiny gray specks, cobwebs, or threads drifting across vision. Most are harmless aging changes. Warning Signs: Seek IMMEDIATE emergency ophthalmic care if you notice: A sudden explosion of numerous new floaters; bright flashing lights in the peripheral vision like lightning streaks; or a dark shadow/curtain pulling across any part of your vision. These are danger signs of retinal tear or retinal detachment requiring emergency laser repair to prevent permanent blindness.

topic: Night blindness, nyctalopia, difficulty seeing in dim light, Vitamin A deficiency
source_name: WHO - Vitamin A deficiency in children
content: Night blindness (nyctalopia) is impaired visual adaptation to dim light or darkness. In children and pregnant women in developing regions, it is classically caused by dietary Vitamin A deficiency, which damages rhodopsin pigment in retinal rod cells. Protocol: Eat Vitamin A-rich foods: drumstick leaves, spinach, papaya, mango, carrots, pumpkin, eggs, and milk. Ensure children receive all bi-annual doses of Vitamin A syrup (100,000 to 200,000 IU) distributed at Anganwadi centers under the National Prophylaxis Programme. Warning Signs: If night blindness progresses to dry wrinkled eye whites (Bitot's spots) or corneal clouding (xerophthalmia), seek emergency hospital care to prevent permanent blindness.

topic: Black eye, periorbital hematoma, bruised swollen eyelid from blunt facial injury
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye trauma
content: A black eye is bruising and swelling of the tissues around the eye socket caused by ruptured capillaries following blunt facial impact. First Aid: Immediately apply an ice pack or bag of frozen vegetables wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes every hour for the first 24 hours to reduce swelling and bleeding (never press an ice pack with heavy force against the eyeball). Keep head elevated on pillows. After 48 hours, switch to warm compresses. Warning Signs: Seek emergency medical care if you experience double vision, inability to move the eye upward, bloody fluid inside the eyeball (hyphema), loss of vision, or clear fluid leaking from the nose.

topic: Chemical splash in eye emergency, acid or alkali burn first aid
source_name: WHO - Emergency eye trauma protocols
content: Chemical splashes in the eye (household bleach, lime/chuna, drain cleaner, battery acid, fertilizers) are urgent ocular emergencies. Alkali chemicals (like whitewash chuna and lye) are especially hazardous as they rapidly penetrate deep corneal tissues. EMERGENCY FIRST AID: IMMEDIATELY FLUSH THE EYE WITH CLEAN RUNNING WATER CONTINUOUSLY FOR AT LEAST 15 TO 20 FULL MINUTES. Hold eyelids wide open with clean fingers and roll the eye in all directions under a gentle stream of tap water or saline. Do NOT search for neutralizing agents. Rush IMMEDIATELY to the nearest eye hospital or emergency department while continuing to rinse if possible.

topic: Peritonsillar abscess, quinsy, severe one-sided throat pain, difficulty opening mouth
source_name: National Health Portal India - Throat emergencies
content: A peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) is a serious collection of pus behind one of the tonsils following severe untreated bacterial tonsillitis. Symptoms: Severe one-sided throat pain, difficulty and pain when opening the mouth (trismus), muffled 'hot potato' voice, drooling saliva, fever, and deviation of the uvula to the opposite side. This is an ENT EMERGENCY: home remedies are unsafe. Go immediately to a Community Health Centre or District Hospital for intravenous antibiotics and needle drainage of the abscess. Warning Signs: Inability to breathe or swallow requires emergency 108 hospital transfer.

topic: Strep throat, group A streptococcal pharyngitis, sudden fever and white pus on tonsils
source_name: WHO - Prevention of rheumatic fever and heart disease
content: Strep throat is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, presenting with abrupt high fever, severe painful swallowing, bright red swollen tonsils coated with white or yellow patches of pus, tender swollen lymph nodes in the neck, and absence of a cough (cough suggests a viral cold). Protocol: Strep throat requires professional medical evaluation and prescription antibiotics (such as penicillin or amoxicillin) for 10 full days to prevent serious complications like rheumatic fever and heart valve damage. Home Care: Gargle warm salt water, drink warm broths, and rest. Take the full antibiotic course without stopping early.

topic: Wisdom tooth eruption pain, pericoronitis, swollen red gum over back molar
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral health
content: Pericoronitis is inflammation and infection of the gum flap (operculum) overlying a partially erupted wisdom tooth (third molar), caused by food particles and dental plaque becoming trapped beneath the gum flap. Symptoms: Throbbing pain in the back of the jaw, swollen tender gum flap, bad taste in mouth, and pain when chewing. Home Care: Rinse mouth with warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in a warm glass of water) 4 times daily, especially after eating, swishing gently near the back molar. Use a soft toothbrush to gently clean the area. Apply an ice pack to the cheek. Warning Signs: Inability to open the mouth (trismus), swelling spreading down the neck, or fever requires urgent dental antibiotic care.

topic: Xerostomia, chronic dry mouth, reduced saliva, difficulty swallowing dry food
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dental health
content: Xerostomia is the persistent sensation of dry mouth caused by reduced saliva secretion, commonly triggered by medications (antihistamines, BP drugs, antidepressants), dehydration, mouth-breathing during sleep, or diabetes. Saliva is vital for neutralizing acids and preventing cavities. Home Care: Sip water frequently throughout the day. Chew sugar-free gum to mechanically stimulate salivary flow. Avoid caffeinated tea, coffee, alcohol, and tobacco which dry oral tissues. Use a room humidifier at night. Practice meticulous dental hygiene and brush with fluoride toothpaste after meals. Warning Signs: Severe tooth decay, fungal oral thrush, or painful dry eyes and joints (Sjögren's syndrome) requires physician evaluation.

topic: Oral leukoplakia warning signs, thick white precancerous patch in mouth, gutka and bidi risk
source_name: National Cancer Control Programme India - Oral cancer prevention
content: Oral leukoplakia is a firmly attached, thick, rough white or grayish patch on the inside of the cheeks, tongue, or gums that CANNOT be wiped or scraped away, overwhelmingly caused by chronic tobacco use (smoking bidi/cigarettes or chewing gutka, khaini, paan with betel nut). While some patches are benign, leukoplakia is a PRE-CANCEROUS lesion that can transform into oral squamous cell carcinoma. Protocol: STOP all tobacco, gutka, paan, and alcohol immediately. Visit a dentist or government hospital for clinical biopsy and examination. Early detection completely prevents mouth cancer. Warning Signs: Any mouth ulcer or lump lasting more than 3 weeks requires urgent medical checkup.

topic: Temporomandibular joint dysfunction, TMJ pain, jaw clicking and jaw lock
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dental disorders
content: TMJ dysfunction involves pain, clicking, popping sounds, and restricted movement of the jaw joints and chewing muscles, often linked to teeth grinding (bruxism), stress clenching, arthritis, or jaw misalignment. Home Care: Eat soft foods (khichdi, curd, soups); avoid hard, chewy, or crunchy foods. Avoid extreme jaw movements: do not chew gum, open mouth widely while yawning, or bite nails. Apply warm moist compresses to the side of the face for 15 minutes to relax jaw muscles. Practice gentle jaw relaxation exercises. Wear a dental nightguard if you grind teeth. Warning Signs: Jaw completely locked open or shut, or severe ear pain radiating down the neck, requires dental evaluation.

topic: Burning mouth syndrome, glossodynia, scalded tongue sensation without visible sores
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral health
content: Burning mouth syndrome is a chronic, painful burning or scalding sensation affecting the tongue, roof of the mouth, and lips, without any visible sores, redness, or medical abnormalities, often linked to nerve sensitivity, hormonal changes during menopause, nutritional deficiencies (vitamin B12, iron, zinc), or stress. Home Care: Sip cold water or melt ice chips on the tongue to numb burning. Avoid spicy, acidic, crunchy, or citrus foods, hot beverages, and alcohol. Use mild, unflavored toothpaste without sodium lauryl sulfate. Avoid mint and cinnamon flavors. Check blood levels of vitamin B12, iron, and blood glucose with a doctor.

topic: Exercise-induced bronchospasm, coughing and chest tightness during sports or running
source_name: WHO - Chronic respiratory diseases
content: Exercise-induced bronchospasm is temporary airway narrowing triggered by physical exertion, particularly when breathing cold, dry air during sports or running, causing shortness of breath, wheezing, coughing, and chest tightness within 5-15 minutes of strenuous exercise. Home Care: Warm up thoroughly with 10-15 minutes of light jogging and stretching before intense activity. Breathe through the nose rather than the mouth to warm and humidify inhaled air. Wear a scarf or mask over the mouth and nose when exercising outdoors in cold weather. Cool down gradually. Always carry prescribed reliever inhalers to use 15 minutes before sports if prescribed by a doctor.

topic: Hyperventilation syndrome, rapid shallow breathing, tingling fingers from panic
source_name: WHO - Emergency clinical protocols
content: Hyperventilation occurs during acute panic or severe anxiety when rapid, deep breathing blows off excessive carbon dioxide (hypocapnia), causing lightheadedness, chest tightness, palpitations, and characteristic tingling and numbness around the mouth, hands, and feet (carpopedal spasms). Home Care: Calm the person and provide reassurance. Guide them to slow their breathing rate: breathe in slowly through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 2, and breathe out through pursed lips for 6 seconds. Have them breathe with a cupped hand over the mouth and nose to re-inhale carbon dioxide. Sit comfortably. Warning Signs: If rapid breathing is accompanied by severe chest pain, fever, or blue lips, seek emergency hospital care.

topic: Pleurisy, pleuritic chest pain, sharp stabbing pain on deep breathing or coughing
source_name: WHO - Clinical guidelines for respiratory illness
content: Pleurisy is inflammation of the double-layered membranes (pleura) lining the lungs and chest cavity, commonly resulting from viral respiratory infections, pneumonia, or autoimmune disease. Hallmark symptom: Sharp, stabbing chest pain that distinctly worsens with deep inhalation, coughing, or sneezing, and eases when holding breath or breathing shallowly. Home Care: Rest in bed lying on the painful side (splinting the chest), which can reduce pleural friction and ease pain. Drink warm fluids. Pleurisy requires medical examination and a chest X-ray to determine the underlying cause and treat any infection. Warning Signs: High fever, coughing up blood, or severe breathlessness requires immediate hospital care.

topic: Irritable bowel syndrome, IBS, alternating diarrhea and constipation, stress gut
source_name: WHO - Noncommunicable diseases and gut health
content: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurring abdominal cramping, bloating, and altered bowel habits (alternating diarrhea, constipation, or both), often relieved temporarily by defecation and aggravated by emotional stress. Home Care: Eat meals at regular hours. Increase soluble fiber gradually (oats, psyllium / isabgol, flaxseeds). Drink plenty of water. Keep a food diary to identify and avoid individual trigger foods (excess caffeine, beans, artificial sweeteners, greasy foods). Practice stress-reduction techniques like regular walking, yoga, and meditation. Warning Signs: IBS does NOT cause rectal bleeding, nocturnal diarrhea, unexplained weight loss, or anemia; these 'red flags' require colonoscopy evaluation.

topic: Amoebiasis, entamoeba histolytica, amoebic dysentery, mucus and blood in stool
source_name: WHO - Neglected tropical diseases: amoebiasis
content: Amoebiasis is an intestinal parasitic infection caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, spread through ingestion of food or water contaminated with cysts. Symptoms: Gradual onset of crampy lower abdominal pain, frequent loose stools containing visible bloody mucus (amoebic dysentery), tenesmus (painful urge to pass stool with little output), and mild fever. Protocol: Amoebic dysentery requires stool testing and specific prescription anti-protozoal medications (like metronidazole). Hydrate continuously with ORS. Boil all drinking water; wash raw vegetables thoroughly. Warning Signs: High fever with severe right upper abdominal pain can indicate amoebic liver abscess requiring urgent hospital ultrasound.

topic: Fatty liver disease lifestyle, NAFLD, non-alcoholic hepatic steatosis management
source_name: WHO - Noncommunicable diseases and metabolic health
content: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is the accumulation of excess fat in liver cells in individuals who drink little or no alcohol, closely tied to obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and high triglycerides. It typically causes no symptoms in early stages. Lifestyle Reversal: Weight reduction of 7-10% through gradual, healthy lifestyle modification reverses liver fat deposits. Adopt a Mediterranean or whole-food diet: eliminate sweetened beverages, soft drinks, refined sugar, and refined flours. Eat leafy vegetables, lentils, whole grains, and healthy fats. Exercise for at least 150 minutes weekly (brisk walking). Avoid alcohol completely. Have liver enzymes monitored annually.

topic: Appendicitis red flags, right lower quadrant abdominal pain, surgical emergency
source_name: WHO - Emergency surgical care guidelines
content: Appendicitis is acute inflammation of the vermiform appendix. It begins with dull, aching pain around the navel (belly button) that shifts over several hours to sharp, intense, localized agony in the RIGHT LOWER ABDOMEN (McBurney's point), worsened by walking, coughing, or bumping, accompanied by loss of appetite, low fever, and vomiting. Protocol: This is a SURGICAL EMERGENCY: a ruptured appendix causes life-threatening peritonitis. Call 108 or go IMMEDIATELY to a surgical hospital. DO NOT eat or drink anything (in case emergency surgery is needed). DO NOT take laxatives, pain pills, or apply a hot heating pad to the abdomen.

topic: Vitamin D deficiency, bone ache, muscle weakness, sunlight exposure guidelines
source_name: WHO - Guidelines on Vitamin D and bone health
content: Vitamin D is essential for intestinal calcium absorption, immune health, and bone mineralization. Deficiency causes diffuse bone aches, lower back pain, muscle weakness, and fatigue, leading to osteomalacia in adults and rickets in children. Home Care: Get 15 to 20 minutes of midday sunlight exposure on face, arms, and legs 3 to 4 times weekly without sunscreen (sunlight converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to pre-vitamin D3). Consume dietary sources: fortified milk, egg yolks, and oily fish. Individuals with proven severe deficiency (<20 ng/mL) require weekly therapeutic oral vitamin D3 (60,000 IU) prescribed by a doctor for 8 weeks.

topic: Vitamin B12 deficiency, tingling numbness in feet, smooth beefy red tongue, anemia
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nutritional deficiency
content: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is vital for red blood cell synthesis and neurological nerve sheath maintenance, found almost exclusively in animal foods and dairy. Deficiency is common in strict vegetarians and the elderly, causing pins-and-needles (paresthesia) in feet, unsteady walking, fatigue, memory fog, and a smooth, sore, beefy red tongue (glossitis). Home Care: Consume dairy products: curd (dahi), milk, paneer, and eggs. Strict vegans must take regular oral vitamin B12 supplements. Severe neurological deficiency requires prescription intramuscular cyanocobalamin injections. Warning Signs: Unsteady gait, frequent falls, or severe mental confusion requires immediate physician evaluation.

topic: Iron deficiency anemia diet, low hemoglobin, fatigue, pale conjunctiva
source_name: MoHFW India - Anemia Mukt Bharat
content: Iron deficiency anemia occurs when the body lacks sufficient iron to produce hemoglobin, leading to fatigue, weakness, pale inner eyelids and tongue, brittle spoon nails (koilonychia), shortness of breath on exertion, and cravings for chalk or clay (pica). Home Care: Eat iron-rich foods: drumstick leaves, spinach, fenugreek, beetroot, jaggery (gur), sprouted green gram (moong), lentils, and eggs. Pair iron foods with Vitamin C (lemon juice, amla, guava) to multiply non-heme iron absorption fourfold. Avoid drinking tea, coffee, or milk with meals as polyphenols and calcium inhibit iron uptake. Take prescribed iron supplements with water after meals.

topic: Osteoporosis prevention, brittle bones in postmenopausal women, calcium and walking
source_name: WHO - Assessment of osteoporosis
content: Osteoporosis is silent thinning and micro-architectural weakening of bone tissue, making bones fragile and prone to fracture from minor falls (especially hip, wrist, and spine), highly prevalent in postmenopausal women due to falling estrogen levels. Home Care: Consume 1,000 to 1,200 mg of calcium daily from dairy (milk, curd), ragi (finger millet), sesame seeds, green leafy vegetables, and small fish. Ensure adequate Vitamin D from sunlight or supplements. Engage in regular weight-bearing and resistance exercises (brisk walking, climbing stairs) 30 minutes daily to stimulate bone density. Avoid smoking and alcohol. Prevent home trip hazards.

topic: Deep vein thrombosis warning signs, DVT, unilateral painful swollen calf, flight risk
source_name: WHO - Thrombosis prevention and cardiovascular health
content: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) is a blood clot forming within deep veins, usually of the calf or thigh, triggered by prolonged immobility (long bus/train/plane travel, bed rest after surgery, plaster casts) or hypercoagulable states. Hallmark Signs: UNILATERAL (one-sided) calf swelling, deep throbbing calf pain or cramping, warmth, and skin redness. Protocol: This is a MEDICAL EMERGENCY: if the clot dislodges, it can travel to the lungs causing a fatal Pulmonary Embolism (PE). Call 108 or go immediately to the hospital. DO NOT massage or squeeze the painful calf (massaging breaks the clot loose into the bloodstream). Keep the leg resting and elevated.

topic: Raynaud's phenomenon, white blue red color changes in cold fingers
source_name: National Health Portal India - Vascular disorders
content: Raynaud's phenomenon is an exaggerated vascular spasm of digital blood vessels in response to cold temperatures or emotional stress, causing fingers and toes to turn numb, waxy white, then blue (cyanosis from lack of oxygen), and finally red, throbbing, and tingling upon rewarming. Home Care: Keep the whole body warm, especially hands, feet, and head. Wear insulated mittens and thick socks in cold weather. Rewarm fingers GRADUALLY in lukewarm water or inside armpits. Avoid sudden cold drafts or holding icy drinks directly. Never smoke, as nicotine constricts peripheral vessels severely. Practice stress management. Warning Signs: Skin ulcers, black tissue, or sores on fingertips requires rheumatology evaluation.

topic: Peripheral neuropathy in diabetes, numb burning feet, foot ulcer prevention
source_name: International Diabetes Federation - Diabetic foot care
content: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is nerve damage resulting from chronically high blood glucose levels, classically affecting the longest nerves first ('stocking-glove distribution'), causing numbness, loss of protective pain sensation, burning pain, and pins-and-needles in the feet. Home Care: Inspect feet daily using a mirror for any cuts, blisters, cracks, or red spots. Wash feet daily with lukewarm water and dry thoroughly between toes. Apply moisturizer to feet, but NEVER between toes. Never walk barefoot—always wear well-fitting shoes and soft clean socks. Cut toenails straight across. Have feet clinically examined by a doctor at least once a year. Warning Signs: Any non-healing ulcer, black toe, or foul odor requires immediate hospital care to prevent amputation.

topic: Restless legs syndrome, RLS, irresistible urge to move legs at night
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sleep disorders
content: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) is a neurological disorder causing an overwhelming, uncomfortable, crawling, pulling, or creeping sensation deep inside the legs, accompanied by an irresistible urge to move them, occurring almost exclusively in the evening or night when sitting or lying down, relieved temporarily by walking or stretching. Home Care: Engage in moderate daily exercise like walking or cycling (avoid intense late-night workouts). Take a warm bath and massage leg muscles before bed. Apply heating pads or cool ice packs to the calves. Cut out caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine. Check ferritin (iron) levels with a doctor, as iron deficiency is a major reversible cause.

topic: Bell's palsy recognition, sudden one-sided facial weakness, eyelid drooping
source_name: National Health Portal India - Neurological conditions
content: Bell's palsy is sudden, temporary weakness or paralysis of the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII), causing one entire side of the face to droop, inability to close the eye on that side, loss of forehead wrinkles, drooling from the mouth corner, and change in taste. It develops rapidly over 24-48 hours, often linked to viral reactivation. Protocol: Bell's palsy requires URGENT medical evaluation within 72 hours to start oral corticosteroid therapy that significantly boosts complete recovery. Home Care: Protect the eye that cannot blink: use artificial tears every 2 hours and tape the eyelid closed with paper tape or wear an eye patch during sleep to prevent corneal drying and ulcers.

topic: Sleep apnea warning signs, loud chronic snoring, choking gasps during sleep, daytime fatigue
source_name: WHO - Chronic respiratory diseases and sleep
content: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) occurs when upper airway throat muscles intermittently relax and collapse during sleep, completely blocking the airway for 10-30 seconds hundreds of times a night. Hallmark Signs: Very loud chronic snoring, witnessed pauses in breathing followed by loud gasping or choking sounds, dry mouth upon waking, morning headaches, and extreme daytime sleepiness. Lifestyle Care: Weight loss is the most effective intervention (reducing neck fat reduces airway collapse). Sleep on your side (lateral position) using pillows rather than on your back. Completely avoid alcohol and sedatives before bed. Avoid smoking. Warning Signs: Falling asleep while driving or operating machinery requires clinical sleep study (polysomnography) and CPAP therapy.

topic: Early signs of dementia, Alzheimer's vs normal aging memory lapses
source_name: WHO - Dementia fact sheet
content: Normal aging involves occasional memory slips (like temporarily misplacing keys and finding them later). Dementia (such as Alzheimer's disease) is a progressive brain disorder causing memory loss that DISRUPTS DAILY LIFE: forgetting recently learned information, asking the same questions repeatedly, getting lost in familiar neighborhoods, difficulty managing money or cooking familiar recipes, misplacing items in bizarre places (e.g., wallet in refrigerator), and dramatic changes in mood or withdrawal from social hobbies. Protocol: If a family member shows these progressive signs, consult a neurologist or psychiatrist at a District Hospital for cognitive screening and supportive care.

topic: Electrical shock first aid, domestic electric shock, power line accident
source_name: WHO - Emergency trauma care
content: Domestic electrical shocks (from exposed wiring, wet appliances, or plugs) can cause severe internal tissue burns, muscle spasms, cardiac arrhythmias, and cardiac arrest. EMERGENCY FIRST AID: 1. DO NOT TOUCH THE VICTIM DIRECTLY WITH BARE HANDS while they are still in contact with the electrical source (you will be electrocuted too). 2. IMMEDIATELY turn off the main circuit breaker / switch off the power source. 3. If the switch cannot be reached, stand on dry wood, rubber mat, or plastic and push the victim away using a dry non-conductive object (dry wooden broom handle, dry bamboo pole, or dry rolled newspaper). 4. Check breathing; if not breathing, call 108 and begin CPR immediately. All electrical shock victims must be evaluated in a hospital for cardiac monitoring.

topic: Chemical skin burns, acid and lime burns, immediate irrigation protocol
source_name: WHO - Burns fact sheet
content: Chemical burns occur when strong acids (sulfuric, muriatic acid) or strong alkalis (whitewash lime, caustic soda, lye, drain cleaner) destroy skin tissue. Alkali burns are especially destructive and penetrate deeply. FIRST AID: 1. Remove contaminated clothing, shoes, and jewelry immediately while protecting yourself with gloves. 2. Brush dry chemical powders off the skin with a dry cloth BEFORE rinsing. 3. IMMEDIATELY FLUSH THE AFFECTED SKIN UNDER COLD, GENTLE RUNNING TAP WATER FOR AT LEAST 20 CONTINUOUS MINUTES. Do not apply neutralizing substances (like vinegar on alkali or soda on acid), as neutralization reactions release intense heat that deepens thermal burns. Cover loosely with sterile cloth and rush to the hospital.

topic: Fishbone stuck in throat, sharp throat sensation after eating fish
source_name: National Health Portal India - Foreign body in throat
content: Small, sharp fishbones frequently lodge in the tonsils, base of tongue, or vallecula while eating fish, causing sharp, localized prickling pain every time you swallow. First Aid: DO NOT attempt to force the bone down by swallowing large dry balls of rice, dry chapati, or bananas, as forcing dry boluses can push the bone deeper into esophageal tissues or tear the mucosal lining. Cough gently to see if the bone dislodges. Sip a little olive oil or warm water. If pain, scratching sensation, or difficulty swallowing persists, visit an ENT specialist or Community Health Centre where a doctor can inspect the throat with a headlight and remove the bone safely with forceps in seconds.

topic: Foreign object swallowed, swallowed coin or small battery in children
source_name: WHO - Pediatric emergency guidelines
content: Young children frequently swallow small objects like coins, marbles, safety pins, or button batteries. Protocol: BUTTON BATTERIES ARE A CRITICAL MEDICAL EMERGENCY: when lodged in the esophagus, button batteries create an electrical current that generates alkaline hydroxide, burning a hole through the esophagus within 2 hours. Go to the nearest emergency hospital IMMEDIATELY; do NOT induce vomiting. If a smooth coin or marble was swallowed and the child is breathing, coughing, and swallowing normally, it usually passes harmlessly through the gut over 3-5 days. Warning Signs: Choking, drooling, inability to swallow, chest pain, or vomiting requires emergency endoscopy.

topic: Splinter removal, wooden sliver or bamboo thorn under skin first aid
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid splinters
content: A splinter is a fragment of wood, bamboo, glass, or metal embedded beneath the superficial skin layers, causing localized tenderness, pricking pain, and risk of bacterial or fungal infection.
