First Aid: Wash your hands and clean the area gently with soap and warm water. Sterilize a pair of tweezers with rubbing alcohol. If the end of the splinter protrudes above the skin surface, grasp it firmly with the tweezers and pull it straight out at the same angle it entered. Do not squeeze forcefully. Clean the wound again, apply antiseptic, and cover with a small adhesive bandage. Warning Signs: If the splinter is deep under a nail, glass, near the eye, or if you haven't had a Tetanus Toxoid (TT) vaccine in 10 years, visit a clinic.

topic: Scorpion sting first aid, red and black scorpion sting, severe pain relief
source_name: WHO - Management of venomous stings and bites
content: Scorpion stings (common in rural Odisha from Indian red scorpions or black rock scorpions) inject venom causing immediate, excruciating burning pain, numbness, sweating, and localized swelling at the sting site. First Aid: Wash the sting site with soap and water. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a clean towel for 10-15 minutes to reduce pain and slow venom spread. Keep the stung limb immobilized and resting. Do NOT cut the wound or try to suck venom. Do NOT tie tight tourniquets. Administer paracetamol for pain if advised. Warning Signs: Red scorpion venom contains neurotoxins and cardiotoxins that can cause profuse sweating, vomiting, breathlessness, irregular heartbeat, or high BP (pulmonary edema); transport to a hospital equipped with prazosin immediately.

topic: Leech bite first aid, removing river leeches, bleeding from leech attachment
source_name: National Health Portal India - Environmental first aid
content: Aquatic or terrestrial leeches attach to bare skin in rivers, ponds, and wet paddy fields, releasing hirudin (a potent anticoagulant) and local anesthetics so their bite is painless. Symptoms include a small Y-shaped painless bite that bleeds persistently for hours after the leech drops off. First Aid: To remove an attached leech safely: slide a fingernail, flat credit card, or edge of paper under the small suction mouth at the front end to break the suction seal; the leech will detach easily. DO NOT burn with matches, salt, or pull violently, as this causes the leech to regurgitate bacteria into the wound. Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and water. Apply firm pressure with a clean sterile gauze for 15 minutes to stop bleeding. Apply antiseptic.

topic: Fainting first aid, syncope, sudden temporary loss of consciousness
source_name: WHO - Emergency first aid guidelines
content: Fainting (syncope) is a brief, temporary loss of consciousness caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain, triggered by dehydration, prolonged standing in hot sun, emotional shock, pain, or skipping meals. Recovery is usually rapid. First Aid: Lay the person flat on their back immediately on the ground. ELEVATE THEIR LEGS 30 cm (12 inches) above heart level to assist venous blood return to the brain. Loosen tight collars, belts, and restrictive clothing. Ensure plenty of fresh air (fan the person, clear away crowding onlookers). Do NOT splash cold water into their face or give liquids while unconscious. If they wake, keep them lying down for 10 minutes before slowly sitting up. Warning Signs: If unconsciousness lasts over 1 minute, follows chest pain, or is accompanied by convulsions, call 108 immediately.

topic: Near-drowning first aid, water submersion rescue, rescue breathing
source_name: WHO - Drowning fact sheet
content: Near-drowning occurs when submersion in water causes suffocation and lack of oxygen. Every second counts. Emergency Protocol: 1. Remove the victim from water safely while protecting yourself. 2. Call 108 immediately. 3. Check for responsiveness and breathing. 4. If the person is NOT breathing: begin CPR immediately. For drowning victims, START WITH 5 RESCUE BREATHS: pinch the nose, seal your mouth over theirs, and blow until the chest rises. Follow with cycles of 30 chest compressions (2 inches deep at 100-120 per minute) and 2 rescue breaths. DO NOT attempt to drain swallowed water from the stomach by pressing the abdomen; doing so causes vomiting and lung aspiration. Continue CPR until emergency help arrives.

topic: Polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS, irregular periods, facial hair, weight gain lifestyle
source_name: WHO - Polycystic ovary syndrome fact sheet
content: PCOS is a common endocrine disorder characterized by hormonal imbalance, irregular or absent menstrual cycles, elevated male hormones (androgens) causing excess facial/body hair (hirsutism) and acne, and multiple small follicles on the ovaries. It is closely linked to insulin resistance. Lifestyle Management: Weight reduction of even 5% through consistent exercise and dietary changes significantly restores normal ovulation and regular periods. Adopt a low-glycemic diet: replace white rice and refined flour with whole grains, millets (ragi), lentils, vegetables, and lean protein. Eliminate sugary sodas, sweets, and pastries. Exercise for at least 30-45 minutes daily. Consult a gynecologist for cycle-regulating medical therapy.

topic: Premenstrual syndrome, PMS, irritability, breast tenderness, bloating before period
source_name: National Health Portal India - Women's health
content: Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS) encompasses physical and emotional symptoms that occur in the 1 to 2 weeks before menstruation (luteal phase) and resolve within days of period onset, including mood swings, irritability, sadness, abdominal bloating, breast tenderness, headaches, and food cravings. Home Care: Engage in regular aerobic exercise (brisk walking, swimming) which releases endorphins and reduces fluid retention. Reduce salt, refined sugar, and caffeine during the 2 weeks before periods. Eat complex carbohydrates and smaller frequent meals. Maintain consistent sleep hours. Practice stress-relief techniques like meditation. Warning Signs: If emotional distress is severe, causing depressive despair or suicidal thoughts (PMDD), seek psychiatric/gynecological evaluation.

topic: Bacterial vaginosis, thin grayish vaginal discharge with fishy odor
source_name: WHO - Guidelines for the management of vaginal discharge
content: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common condition caused by an overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria (Gardnerella) outnumbering protective hydrogen-peroxide-producing Lactobacillus bacteria in the vagina, producing a thin, watery, grayish-white vaginal discharge with a characteristic strong 'fishy' odor that becomes more noticeable after sexual intercourse. Home Care: BV is an imbalance, not a sexually transmitted disease. Practice gentle hygiene: wash the external vulva with plain warm water only. NEVER douche (douching washes away healthy protective bacteria and worsens BV). Avoid scented soaps, bubble baths, and feminine hygiene deodorants. Wear breathable cotton underwear. BV requires prescription oral or topical antibiotic therapy from a health centre.

topic: Menopause symptoms, hot flashes, night sweats, mood fluctuations, perimenopause
source_name: WHO - Menopause fact sheet
content: Menopause is the natural biological transition marking the end of menstrual cycles (diagnosed after 12 consecutive months without a period, typically between ages 45 and 55), caused by declining ovarian estrogen production. Symptoms include sudden intense heat spreading over face and chest ('hot flashes'), drenching night sweats, sleep disturbances, mood swings, and vaginal dryness. Home Care: Dress in removable layers of lightweight breathable cotton clothing. Keep bedrooms cool and use a bedside fan. Avoid hot flash triggers: hot tea/coffee, spicy foods, alcohol, and stress. Practice slow deep abdominal breathing when a hot flash starts. Use water-based vaginal moisturizers for comfort. Walk regularly for bone health.

topic: Mastitis, breast engorgement, painful red swollen breast, fever in nursing mothers
source_name: WHO - Mastitis: causes and management
content: Mastitis is inflammation or bacterial infection of breast tissue in lactating mothers, commonly resulting from a plugged milk duct or cracked nipple allowing bacteria to enter, causing a firm, red, tender, wedge-shaped swollen area on one breast accompanied by high fever, flu-like chills, and severe pain. Home Care: CONTINUE BREASTFEEDING FREQUENTLY from the affected breast (breast milk is safe for the baby and completely emptying the breast is the most critical step to clear the plugged duct). Apply warm, moist compresses to the breast for 10 minutes before nursing to encourage milk let-down. Massage gently from the hard lump toward the nipple while the baby nurses. Rest in bed and drink plenty of fluids. Warning Signs: If fever and redness do not improve within 24 hours, visit a doctor for breastfeeding-safe antibiotics.

topic: Cracked sore nipples during breastfeeding, latch correction, lanolin care
source_name: WHO - Infant and young child feeding counselling
content: Sore, cracked, or bleeding nipples during nursing are overwhelmingly caused by SHALLOW OR IMPROPER ATTACHMENT (latch) of the infant, where the baby suckles only on the nipple tip rather than taking a large mouthful of the lower areola. Home Care: Correct the baby's latch: wait until the baby opens their mouth wide like a yawn, then bring the baby swiftly to the breast (not the breast to the baby) so the nipple is deep against the soft palate. Express a few drops of hindmilk after feeding and rub it gently onto the nipples (breast milk has natural antibacterial and healing properties); allow to air dry. Apply medical-grade purified lanolin or pure coconut oil. Do not wash breasts with soap before nursing. Contact an ASHA worker for hands-on latch guidance.

topic: Postpartum blues vs postpartum depression, sadness after childbirth, maternal mental health
source_name: WHO - Maternal mental health
content: The 'baby blues' affects up to 80% of new mothers in the first 2 weeks after childbirth due to dramatic hormonal drops and sleep deprivation, causing mild mood swings, crying spells, anxiety, and fatigue that resolve naturally with rest and family support. Postpartum Depression (PPD) is a serious medical illness that lasts beyond 2 weeks, characterized by persistent deep sadness, inability to feel joy or bond with the baby, overwhelming guilt, intense anxiety, panic attacks, or frightening thoughts of self-harm. Protocol: PPD is NOT a personal failure. Talk openly to your family, ASHA worker, or doctor. Free counseling is available via Tele-MANAS at 14416. Professional counseling and safe medical therapies are highly effective.

topic: Cold hands and feet, poor peripheral circulation, warm clothing care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Seasonal health
content: Cold extremities frequently occur when the body naturally shunts blood to core organs in chilly weather, or due to low physical activity, mild anemia, or stress. Home Care: Dress in warm layers; wear insulated socks, comfortable footwear, and gloves. Engage in 10-15 minutes of brisk indoor walking, jogging in place, or hand exercises to stimulate blood flow. Drink warm fluids like hot water or soups. Avoid smoking, as nicotine rapidly constricts peripheral blood vessels. Avoid tight shoes or socks with tight elastic bands that impede venous return. Warning Signs: If fingers turn waxy white or blue with severe pain (Raynaud's), or if accompanied by non-healing sores on toes, visit a clinic.

topic: Burning sensation in feet, hot burning soles at night, peripheral nerve health
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nerve conditions
content: A burning or stinging sensation on the soles of the feet, particularly noticeable at night in bed, is frequently linked to early diabetic peripheral neuropathy, Vitamin B12 or B6 deficiency, alcohol excess, or prolonged standing in tight synthetic footwear. Home Care: Wash feet in cool (not freezing) water for 10 minutes before bed. Wear breathable, cushioned cotton socks and open-toed footwear. Check blood glucose and Vitamin B12 levels with a doctor. Avoid alcohol. Maintain a balanced diet rich in leafy greens, dairy, and whole grains. Warning Signs: If burning is accompanied by numbness (loss of sensation to pinpricks), weakness in feet, or foot ulcers, seek immediate medical evaluation.

topic: Bitter taste in mouth, sour acid taste upon waking, morning oral hygiene
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral and digestive health
content: A persistent bitter, sour, or metallic taste in the mouth upon waking is most commonly caused by nighttime gastroesophageal acid reflux (GERD), dry mouth from sleeping with an open mouth, bacterial tongue coating, or certain medications. Home Care: Clean the tongue gently with a tongue cleaner or soft toothbrush to remove accumulated anaerobic bacteria. Rinse mouth thoroughly with warm water. Avoid heavy, oily, or spicy dinners within 3 hours of sleeping. Elevate the head of the bed slightly on pillows. Drink a glass of water upon waking. Stay well-hydrated throughout the day. Warning Signs: If accompanied by yellowing of the eyes (jaundice), abdominal pain, or loss of appetite, visit a doctor for liver assessment.

topic: White coated tongue, tongue biofilm, thick white layer on tongue surface
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral health
content: A white tongue occurs when dead cells, food debris, and oral bacteria become trapped between enlarged, inflamed papillae on the surface of the tongue, often due to dehydration, poor oral hygiene, mouth breathing, smoking, or excessive soft foods. Home Care: Gently brush or scrape the tongue from back to front using a tongue scraper or soft-bristled toothbrush twice daily. Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of water daily. Chew crunchy, fibrous foods (apples, carrots) which naturally clean the tongue surface. Rinse mouth after eating. Quit smoking. Warning Signs: If white patches cannot be scraped away (leukoplakia), or leave raw bleeding red sores when wiped (oral candidiasis/thrush), seek dental examination.

topic: Sensitive teeth to cold or sweet foods, dentin hypersensitivity, tooth enamel wear
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dental care
content: Tooth sensitivity is a sharp, brief pain triggered when consuming hot, cold, sweet, or acidic foods, caused by worn enamel or receding gums exposing the porous microscopic dentinal tubules leading directly to the tooth nerve. Home Care: Brush gently twice daily using a soft-bristled toothbrush and desensitizing toothpaste containing potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride (dab a little toothpaste directly onto the sensitive spot before bed). Do not brush aggressively or scrub teeth horizontally. Limit acidic foods, citrus fruits, and carbonated sodas which dissolve enamel. Use lukewarm water for brushing. Warning Signs: Persistent throbbing pain that lingers after hot food indicates deep tooth pulp inflammation requiring dental treatment.

topic: Cheek biting sore, accidental inner cheek bite ulcer, traumatic mouth wound
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral first aid
content: Accidentally biting the inside of the cheek or lip while chewing, talking, or during sleep creates a painful, swollen laceration or traumatic mouth ulcer with a white center and red border. Home Care: Rinse immediately with cool water. Place an ice cube wrapped in clean cloth against the cheek to reduce swelling and bleeding. Rinse with warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in warm water) 3 times daily to keep the wound clean and speed natural healing. Eat soft, bland foods; chew carefully on the opposite side of the mouth. Avoid spicy, acidic, or salty foods that sting. Traumatic sores heal naturally within 5 to 7 days. Warning Signs: If the sore fails to heal after 2 weeks, see a dentist.

topic: Morning throat clearing, throat phlegm on waking, sleep post-nasal drip
source_name: National Health Portal India - Respiratory care
content: Waking up with the urge to clear thick phlegm from the throat is typically caused by nighttime post-nasal drip (from mild allergies or sinus congestion) or silent gastroesophageal acid reflux irritating the vocal cords while lying flat. Home Care: Drink a tall glass of warm water or lemon-honey water upon waking to loosen mucus. Sleep with the head of the bed slightly elevated. Flush the nose with saline spray before sleeping. Avoid heavy or oily dinners within 3 hours of bed. Inhale warm steam for 5 minutes. Avoid clearing the throat aggressively, which irritates vocal cords; swallow water instead. Warning Signs: If throat clearing produces blood, or is accompanied by persistent hoarseness over 2 weeks, consult an ENT doctor.

topic: Dark under-eye circles, periorbital hyperpigmentation, tired puffy eyes
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye care
content: Dark circles under the eyes are caused by thin lower eyelid skin revealing underlying dark blood vessels, fluid retention, lack of sleep, eye strain, nasal congestion (allergic shiners), or genetics. Home Care: Ensure 7 to 8 hours of consistent, restful sleep nightly. Sleep with head slightly elevated on an extra pillow to prevent fluid pooling under the eyes. Apply a cool damp washcloth, chilled cucumber slices, or cold tea bags over closed eyes for 10 minutes to constrict dilated capillaries. Stay well-hydrated. Treat underlying nasal allergies. Wear sunglasses outdoors. Dark circles are harmless and do not indicate internal organ disease. Warning Signs: Sudden swelling of only one eye with redness or fever requires medical evaluation.

topic: Stomach growling, borborygmi, loud belly gurgling sounds, empty stomach noises
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive health
content: Stomach growling (borborygmi) is the normal rumbling sound produced by the muscular contractions of the stomach and small intestine (peristalsis) moving food, gas, and digestive fluids along the gastrointestinal tract, especially audible on an empty stomach when air echoes. Home Care: Stomach growling is completely normal and healthy. If hungry, eat a light balanced snack or meal. Chew food slowly and avoid gulping air. Drink water between meals. Avoid carbonated drinks, chewing gum, and excess beans if gurgling is accompanied by gas. Gurgling indicates an active digestive system. Warning Signs: If loud gurgling is accompanied by severe persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, or absence of bowel movements, seek clinic evaluation.

topic: Traveler's diarrhea, loose stools during journey, food and water safety on travel
source_name: WHO - Travel health and waterborne disease
content: Traveler's diarrhea is an acute intestinal infection acquired by consuming contaminated food or water during travel, most commonly caused by enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) or viral pathogens. Symptoms: Abrupt onset of watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, and mild fever. Home Care: Prevent dehydration immediately by drinking Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS), bottled boiled water, or tender coconut water. Eat bland, easily digestible foods (bananas, boiled rice, toast, plain crackers). Follow the travel safety rule: 'Boil it, cook it, peel it, or forget it'. Drink only sealed bottled or boiled water; avoid ice cubes and raw street salads. Warning Signs: Stools containing blood, high fever over 38.5C, or severe dehydration requires clinic antibiotic care.

topic: Tailbone pain, coccydynia, aching lower tailbone when sitting on hard chairs
source_name: National Health Portal India - Spine health
content: Coccydynia is localized pain and tenderness at the tailbone (coccyx) at the very base of the spine, aggravated by prolonged sitting, leaning backward in a chair, or rising from a sitting position, often triggered by a fall on the buttocks, childbirth, or repetitive hard chair sitting. Home Care: Use a wedge-shaped or doughnut-shaped coccyx cushion with a rear cut-out to eliminate direct pressure on the tailbone while sitting. Lean slightly forward when sitting to shift body weight onto the ischial tuberosities (sit bones) rather than the tailbone. Apply ice packs for 15 minutes to reduce acute pain, or warm packs for chronic ache. Avoid soft low couches where the tailbone sinks in. Warning Signs: Unexplained numbness, tingling, or bowel dysfunction requires spine evaluation.

topic: Clicking knee, knee crepitus, cracking popping sounds without pain
source_name: National Health Portal India - Joint health
content: Painless knee clicking, popping, or crunching sounds (crepitus) are very common and typically caused by harmless tiny nitrogen gas bubbles popping in the synovial fluid or tendons and ligaments gently snapping over bony prominences during bending or squatting. Home Care: If there is NO PAIN, swelling, or locking, knee clicking is completely harmless and does not indicate arthritis. Maintain strong quadriceps and hamstring muscles through regular walking, cycling, and gentle straight leg raises. Warm up muscles before sports. Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce joint load. Warning Signs: If knee clicking is accompanied by sharp pain, joint swelling, tenderness, or knee 'giving way' or locking in place, consult an orthopedic doctor for meniscus examination.

topic: Texting thumb, de Quervain's tenosynovitis, pain at base of thumb and wrist
source_name: National Health Portal India - Hand and wrist disorders
content: De Quervain's tenosynovitis is painful inflammation of the tendons controlling thumb movement as they pass through a narrow tunnel along the thumb side of the wrist, commonly caused by repetitive thumb motion from smartphone texting, gaming, or lifting infants with thumbs extended. Symptoms: Pain, swelling, and tenderness at the base of the thumb and wrist, worsened when making a fist or twisting the wrist. Home Care: Rest the affected thumb; take frequent breaks from phone texting and typing. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15 minutes 3 times daily. Wear a thumb spica splint to immobilize the thumb and wrist. Perform gentle thumb stretches. Warning Signs: Severe persistent pain that prevents grasping objects requires orthopedic evaluation.

topic: Shin splints, medial tibial stress syndrome, exercise-induced shin pain
source_name: National Health Portal India - Sports injuries
content: Shin splints involve throbbing, aching pain along the inner edge of the shinbone (tibia) resulting from repetitive stress and micro-tears in the muscles, tendons, and bone tissue, common in runners, military recruits, or dancers who suddenly increase training intensity. Home Care: Rest the legs; avoid high-impact running or jumping until pain resolves. Switch to low-impact cross-training like swimming or cycling. Apply ice packs wrapped in towels for 15-20 minutes 3 times daily to reduce inflammation. Wear well-cushioned running shoes with proper arch support. Avoid running on hard concrete surfaces. Stretch calves and Achilles tendons before and after exercise. Warning Signs: Severe pinpoint bone tenderness or pain at rest suggests a tibial stress fracture requiring X-ray.

topic: Achilles tendonitis, tender painful heel cord, calf stiffness in morning
source_name: National Health Portal India - Musculoskeletal conditions
content: Achilles tendonitis is overuse inflammation of the large Achilles tendon connecting the calf muscles to the heel bone, common in runners or people who suddenly increase physical activity, presenting with burning pain, stiffness, and tenderness along the back of the heel cord, particularly upon taking first steps in the morning. Home Care: Rest the tendon; stop running, sprinting, or jumping. Apply an ice pack for 15-20 minutes after activity. Perform gentle eccentric calf stretches (lowering heel slowly off a step) when pain is mild. Wear supportive footwear with a slightly elevated heel to reduce tension on the tendon. Avoid walking barefoot. Warning Signs: A sudden loud pop or snap in the heel followed by severe sharp pain and inability to stand on tiptoes indicates an Achilles tendon rupture requiring emergency hospital care.

topic: Paper cut first aid, painful small finger slice, superficial skin cut
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid cuts
content: A paper cut is a superficial cut on the fingertip that causes disproportionately sharp, intense pain because fingertips have an exceptionally dense concentration of sensitive pain receptors and the cut is rarely deep enough to bleed heavily and seal with a clot. First Aid: Wash the cut immediately under cool running tap water with mild soap to remove paper dust and bacteria. Apply gentle pressure with clean tissue for 1 minute to stop minor bleeding. Apply a dab of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment to keep the exposed nerve endings moist and sealed from air. Cover with a small sterile adhesive bandage. Change the bandage if wet. Paper cuts heal naturally within 2 to 3 days. Warning Signs: If the finger becomes red, hot, swollen, and throbs with pus, seek clinic care.

topic: Oil splatter burn on hand, kitchen hot cooking oil burn first aid
source_name: WHO - Burns fact sheet
content: Hot oil droplets splashing onto the skin during cooking reach temperatures above 180C, causing immediate sharp stinging and small blistered burns. FIRST AID: IMMEDIATELY place the burned hand or fingers under cool, gentle running tap water for 15 to 20 FULL MINUTES (never use freezing ice or ice cubes, which cause frostbite tissue damage). Do NOT apply raw eggs, flour, ghee, butter, or toothpaste, which trap heat and cause severe bacterial wound infections. Clean gently with mild soap and water. Apply a thin layer of pure aloe vera gel or petroleum jelly. Cover loosely with a clean, dry, non-stick sterile gauze. Do not pop blisters. Warning Signs: If burns cover large areas, face, or skin turns white/numb, visit a hospital burn unit.

topic: Acanthosis nigricans, velvety dark thickened skin on neck and armpits, insulin resistance
source_name: National Health Portal India - Metabolic health
content: Acanthosis nigricans is a skin condition characterized by thick, dark, velvety, hyperpigmented patches in skin folds, most commonly around the back and sides of the neck, armpits, and groin. It is NOT caused by poor hygiene and cannot be scrubbed away. It is an important cutaneous marker of high circulating insulin levels and insulin resistance, closely associated with prediabetes, obesity, and type 2 diabetes. Home Care: Do not scrub or exfoliate aggressively with harsh sponges, which thickens skin further. The most effective treatment is addressing the underlying insulin resistance: reduce dietary refined carbohydrates and sugars, engage in daily aerobic exercise (walking), and achieve gradual weight loss. Have fasting blood glucose and HbA1c tested with a doctor.

topic: Thigh chafing, chub rub, painful red friction rash on inner thighs
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin care
content: Thigh chafing occurs when inner thighs rub against each other or against rough clothing seams during hot, humid weather, walking, or running, causing raw, red, stinging, and burning skin irritation. Home Care: Clean the chafed area gently with mild soap and cool water and pat dry. Apply a generous layer of petroleum jelly, zinc oxide barrier cream, or pure coconut oil to soothe raw skin and prevent further friction. Wear breathable, snug cotton bike shorts or anti-chafing thigh bands under dresses or trousers. In hot weather, keep skin clean and dry. Avoid wearing rough, stiff denim during long walks. Warning Signs: If chafed skin develops open bleeding fissures or oozes yellow pus, visit a clinic for antibiotic cream.

topic: Hangnail care, peeling painful skin flap beside fingernail cuticle
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail care
content: A hangnail is a small, torn strip of dead skin along the side edge of a fingernail (it is not part of the nail itself), caused by dry skin, winter cold, frequent handwashing, or nail-biting. It is painful because it tears adjacent nerve-rich live tissue. Home Care: Soften the skin by soaking the finger in warm water for 5 minutes. Use clean, alcohol-sterilized cuticle nippers or small nail scissors to carefully clip the hangnail flush at its base. DO NOT rip, pull, or bite off the hangnail with teeth, as ripping tears living skin and frequently leads to bacterial paronychia infections. Apply petroleum jelly or antibacterial ointment and cover with a small adhesive bandage until healed.

topic: Neonatal jaundice, physiological newborn jaundice vs danger signs
source_name: WHO - Newborn health and infant care
content: Physiological jaundice is mild yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes in newborns (appearing on days 2 to 4 of life) caused by the immature neonatal liver processing fetal red blood cells, resolving naturally as the baby feeds frequently. Home Care: Ensure frequent breastfeeding (every 2 to 3 hours, at least 8 to 12 times a day); adequate hydration stimulates frequent bowel movements that clear bilirubin through stools. Do not give plain water or sunlight baking. Warning Signs: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of birth, yellowing spreading below the navel to knees and feet, pale chalky stools, dark yellow urine, poor feeding, extreme lethargy, or high-pitched crying requires immediate hospital evaluation for phototherapy to prevent kernicterus.

topic: Umbilical cord stump care, newborn navel hygiene, omphalitis warning signs
source_name: WHO - Care of the umbilical cord
content: The umbilical cord stump gradually dries, turns black, and falls off naturally within 7 to 21 days after birth. Home Care: Practice clean, dry cord care: keep the stump clean, completely dry, and exposed to air. Fold the front of the diaper down below the cord stump to avoid urine contamination. Clean only with boiled and cooled water if soiled and pat dry with clean cotton. DO NOT apply cow dung, mud, ash, oils, turmeric, or powders to the cord stump (traditional applications are the leading cause of lethal neonatal tetanus and sepsis). Wash hands before touching the baby. Warning Signs: If the skin around the navel becomes red, swollen, hot, bleeds continuously, or oozes foul-smelling yellow pus (omphalitis), rush the baby to a hospital immediately.

topic: Infant regurgitation, baby spitting up milk vs projectile vomiting
source_name: WHO - Infant and young child health
content: Spitting up (gastroesophageal reflux) is normal, effortless regurgitation of small amounts of breast milk or formula after feeds in healthy infants, caused by an immature lower esophageal sphincter muscle. Home Care: Burp the baby gently midway through and after every feed. Keep the baby upright against your shoulder for 20 to 30 minutes after feeding. Avoid bouncing or active play immediately after meals. Feed smaller amounts slightly more frequently. As long as the baby is happy, gaining weight normally, and not choking, spitting up is harmless and resolves naturally by 9-12 months. Warning Signs: Forceful, projectile vomiting of entire feeds, vomit that is green-yellow (bile-stained) or contains blood, or poor weight gain requires urgent pediatric examination.

topic: Febrile seizures in children, fever fits first aid, parental guidance
source_name: WHO - Pocket book of hospital care for children
content: A febrile seizure is a convulsion in a child aged 6 months to 5 years triggered by a rapid spike in body temperature during viral infections. The child becomes unconscious, stiffens, and twitches rhythmically for 1-3 minutes. FIRST AID: 1. Stay calm. 2. Place the child gently on their side in the recovery position on a soft surface to prevent choking on saliva or vomit. 3. DO NOT hold the child down or restrain movements. 4. DO NOT put anything into the child's mouth (no fingers, spoons, water, or onions; children do not swallow their tongue). 5. Time the seizure. 6. Once twitching stops, sponge gently with lukewarm water. 7. All first-time seizures require immediate doctor examination. Warning Signs: If a seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes or child does not wake up, call 108 immediately.

topic: Hand, foot, and mouth disease, HFMD, coxsackievirus blisters in toddlers
source_name: WHO - Hand, foot and mouth disease
content: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common, self-limiting viral infection caused by enteroviruses (Coxsackievirus) in young children under 5, causing mild fever, sore throat, small painful blisters inside the mouth and tongue, and a non-itchy red rash with small blisters on palms, soles, and buttocks. Home Care: HFMD resolves naturally on its own in 7 to 10 days. Keep the child well-hydrated with cool fluids, tender coconut water, cold milk, or curd; avoid spicy, salty, or acidic foods that sting mouth sores. Give paracetamol under health worker guidance for fever. Wash hands frequently with soap. Keep child home from daycare until blisters dry. Warning Signs: Persistent high fever, refusal to drink any fluids (dehydration), extreme drowsiness, or jerking movements requires hospital care.

topic: Bedwetting, nocturnal enuresis in children, reassurance and bladder training
source_name: National Health Portal India - Child health
content: Nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting) is involuntary urination during nighttime sleep in children older than 5 years who are fully toilet trained during the day, commonly caused by a small nocturnal functional bladder capacity, deep sleep, or delayed nighttime vasopressin secretion. It is NOT willful misbehavior or laziness. Home Care: Never punish, blame, or shame the child; emotional support and reassurance are essential. Ensure regular fluid intake during the day, but restrict large fluid drinks in the 2 hours before bed. Have the child urinate before starting bedtime routine and again immediately before getting into bed. Ensure easy, well-lit access to the toilet. Protect the mattress with a waterproof sheet. Celebrate dry mornings. Warning Signs: Sudden new bedwetting after 6 months of dryness, painful urination, or daytime wetting requires clinic urine testing.

topic: Growing pains in children, nighttime calf and thigh aches
source_name: National Health Portal India - Pediatric conditions
content: Growing pains are harmless, non-inflammatory, throbbing or cramping muscular aches felt deep in both legs (usually calves, thighs, or behind knees) in children aged 3 to 12 years, occurring typically in the late evening or waking the child from sleep after physically active days, completely disappearing by morning. Home Care: Growing pains are completely benign. Gently massage the child's sore leg muscles. Apply a warm heating pad or warm towel to the legs for 15 minutes. A warm bath before bed relaxes muscles. Help the child do gentle calf and hamstring stretches. The child runs, plays, and walks completely normally during the day. Warning Signs: If pain is only in ONE leg, causes a morning limp, joint swelling, redness, fever, or daytime pain, consult a doctor to rule out bone conditions.

topic: Croup, viral laryngotracheobronchitis, barking seal cough and stridor in toddlers
source_name: WHO - Pocket book of hospital care for children
content: Croup is an acute viral swelling of the larynx and trachea in infants and toddlers (6 months to 3 years), causing a distinctive, harsh, loud 'barking seal' cough, hoarse voice, and a high-pitched whistling noise when inhaling (stridor), classically worsening at night. Home Care: Keep the child calm in your arms (crying increases airway swelling). Take the child into a steamy bathroom (run hot shower water with door closed) for 10-15 minutes, or sit with them in cool night air by an open window; moist or cool air soothes swollen vocal cords. Keep the child well-hydrated with fluids. Warning Signs: Seek IMMEDIATE hospital emergency care if the child has stridor at rest, struggles to breathe, ribs pull in sharply (retractions), skin or lips turn blue, or child drools and cannot swallow.

topic: Whooping cough, pertussis, 100-day cough, intense coughing paroxysms
source_name: WHO - Pertussis fact sheet
content: Pertussis (whooping cough) is a highly contagious respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis bacteria, characterized by severe, exhausting coughing fits followed by a high-pitched 'whoop' intake of breath, often triggering vomiting after the coughing spell. It is dangerous in young unimmunized infants. Protocol: Preventable through the Pentavalent / DPT vaccine under the Universal Immunization Programme (at 6, 10, 14 weeks and boosters at 16-24 months and 5 years). Pertussis requires prescription antibiotics to clear bacteria and protect household contacts. Home Care: Rest, offer small frequent sips of water, and use a cool mist humidifier. Warning Signs: In young infants under 6 months, pertussis may present without a whoop as pauses in breathing (apnea) and turning blue; seek emergency hospital admission.

topic: Complementary feeding after 6 months, introduction of semi-solid foods, baby nutrition
source_name: WHO - Infant and young child feeding guidelines
content: At exactly 6 completed months of age, breast milk alone no longer fulfills an infant's growing nutritional and iron needs, although breastfeeding should continue for 2 years or beyond. Protocol: Introduce clean, freshly prepared, nutrient-dense complementary foods: thick mashed khichdi (rice + dal + ghee), mashed ripe banana, mashed papaya, cooked mashed carrots, soft ragi porridge, and boiled egg yolk. Begin with 2 to 3 tablespoons 2 times a day, gradually increasing texture, diversity, and frequency to 3-4 meals daily by 9-12 months. Do NOT add extra salt or refined sugar before 1 year of age. Never give honey before 1 year due to infant botulism risk. Always wash hands before preparing food.

topic: Dehydration in older adults, reduced thirst sensation, senior fluid intake
source_name: WHO - Integrated care for older people (ICOPE)
content: Elderly individuals have a diminished physiological thirst sensation and reduced renal concentrating ability, making them highly vulnerable to rapid dehydration even before feeling thirsty, which triggers acute confusion, urinary infections, kidney injury, and falls. Home Care: Establish a scheduled fluid routine: do not wait for thirst. Encourage 6 to 8 glasses of fluids daily (water, buttermilk / chaas, thin dal soup, tender coconut water, herbal tea) distributed steadily from morning through evening. Keep a filled water bottle near the elder's favorite chair. Monitor urine color (should be pale yellow). Warning Signs: Dry sunken eyes, sudden mental confusion, dry tongue, dizziness upon standing, or no urination for 8 hours requires prompt medical clinic hydration.

topic: Walking stick cane sizing, assistive mobility device safety for seniors
source_name: WHO - Assistive technology for mobility
content: Using an improperly sized cane or walking stick causes poor posture, shoulder strain, and increases fall risks rather than preventing them. Cane Sizing: Stand upright wearing normal walking shoes with arms hanging naturally at the sides: the top handle of the cane should reach the CREASE OF THE WRIST. When holding the cane, the elbow should be comfortably bent at a 15-to-20-degree angle. Walking Technique: Always hold the cane in the hand OPPOSITE the weaker or painful leg. Move the cane forward simultaneously with the weaker leg, distributing weight onto the cane, then step forward with the good leg. Ensure the rubber tip (ferrule) has good grip tread and replace it if worn smooth.

topic: Age-related macular degeneration, AMD, blurry central vision, straight lines look wavy
source_name: WHO - Blindness and visual impairment
content: Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) is gradual deterioration of the macula (the central portion of the retina responsible for sharp, straight-ahead vision) in adults over 55. Symptoms: Blurriness or a dark blind spot in the center of vision, colors looking faded, and straight lines appearing wavy or distorted (e.g., doorframes or telephone poles). Peripheral vision remains intact. Home Care: Protect eyes from ultraviolet light by wearing UV-blocking sunglasses. Stop smoking (smoking multiplies AMD risk twofold). Eat dark leafy green vegetables (spinach) rich in lutein and zeaxanthin. Have regular dilated eye exams. Warning Signs: Sudden rapid distortion or dark blind spot in central vision (wet AMD) requires emergency ophthalmology referral for anti-VEGF therapy to prevent permanent vision loss.

topic: Denture care, false teeth cleaning, preventing denture stomatitis
source_name: National Health Portal India - Oral health in the elderly
content: Improper denture hygiene allows food debris and Candida yeast to accumulate underneath the acrylic plate, leading to painful red inflammation of the palate and gums (denture stomatitis) and mouth odor. Home Care: Remove and rinse dentures under running water after every meal. Brush dentures daily with a soft toothbrush or dedicated denture brush using mild hand soap or denture paste (do NOT use abrasive regular toothpaste, which scratches acrylic). REMOVE DENTURES EVERY NIGHT AT BEDTIME and soak in a glass of clean plain water (never sleep with dentures in place; gums need overnight rest to stay healthy). Rinse mouth thoroughly with warm water. Warning Signs: Painful white patches, bleeding gums, or cracked sores at mouth corners requires dental care.

topic: Urinary incontinence in women, stress incontinence, pelvic floor Kegel exercises
source_name: National Health Portal India - Women's urinary health
content: Urinary incontinence is involuntary leakage of urine. Stress incontinence involves leakage during coughing, sneezing, laughing, or lifting, caused by weakened pelvic floor muscles following childbirth or menopause. Urge incontinence involves a sudden, uncontrollable urge to urinate. Home Care: Perform KEGEL EXERCISES daily: squeeze the pelvic floor muscles (as if stopping the flow of urine mid-stream), hold for 5 seconds, relax for 5 seconds, repeating 10-15 times, 3 sessions daily. Avoid bladder irritants: excess tea, coffee, carbonated sodas, and artificial sweeteners. Maintain a healthy body weight. Maintain regular bowel habits to avoid straining. Warning Signs: Burning pain, cloudy foul-smelling urine, or blood in urine indicates a urinary tract infection requiring clinic testing.

topic: Pesticide ingestion emergency, organophosphate poisoning, accidental swallow
source_name: WHO - Clinical management of pesticide poisoning
content: Agricultural pesticides (organophosphates, carbamates) are extremely toxic chemicals used in rural farming. Accidental swallowing or severe skin absorption causes acute cholinergic toxicity: pinpoint pupils, profuse sweating, excessive salivation (drooling), vomiting, diarrhea, wheezing, and slow heartbeat. CRITICAL EMERGENCY PROTOCOL: CALL 108 OR RUSH TO THE NEAREST HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING (inducing vomiting causes lethal aspiration of petroleum solvents into the lungs and chemical pneumonia). Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin with soap and water if spilled externally. Bring the original chemical container or bottle label to the hospital so doctors can administer the specific antidote (Atropine and Pralidoxime).

topic: Kerosene ingestion emergency, petroleum product swallowed, DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING
source_name: WHO - Guidelines for poison control
content: Accidental ingestion of kerosene, diesel, petrol, or kerosene lamp oil is a common domestic emergency in young children when fuel is stored in unmarked soft drink bottles. CRITICAL EMERGENCY RULE: NEVER INDUCE VOMITING and do NOT give raw eggs, milk, or salt water. When vomited, volatile kerosene fumes are easily inhaled into the lungs (aspiration), rapidly causing severe chemical pneumonitis, lung destruction, and asphyxiation within hours. Keep the child upright and calm. Rush IMMEDIATELY to the nearest hospital emergency room. If kerosene spilled on skin or clothes, remove clothes and wash skin with soap and water.

topic: Carbon monoxide poisoning, room heater hazard, charcoal angithi in closed room
source_name: WHO - Indoor air quality guidelines
content: Burning charcoal (angithi), coal, wood, or unvented gas heaters inside closed, poorly ventilated bedrooms during cold winter nights produces odorless, colorless, lethal CARBON MONOXIDE (CO) gas. CO binds to hemoglobin 200 times more strongly than oxygen, silently suffocating occupants during sleep. Symptoms: Dull headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, confusion, and loss of consciousness ('silent killer'). Emergency Protocol: 1. Immediately evacuate everyone into fresh outdoor air. 2. Call 108. 3. Turn off or extinguish the burning heater. Prevention: NEVER burn charcoal or unvented coal heaters inside closed bedrooms; always keep windows cracked open for cross-ventilation.

topic: Tick bite removal, tick attached to skin, Lyme and Crimean-Congo prevention
source_name: WHO - Vector-borne diseases
content: Ticks attach to skin in forest areas, livestock sheds, and tall grass, embedding their mouthparts to feed on blood. Ticks can transmit infectious pathogens (spotted fever, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever). FIRST AID FOR TICK REMOVAL: Use fine-tipped tweezers to grasp the tick as close to the skin surface as possible. Pull upward with steady, even pressure—DO NOT jerk, twist, or squeeze the tick body (twisting can cause mouthparts to break off in the skin). DO NOT burn with matches, smother with petroleum jelly, or apply nail polish. After removing, clean the bite area thoroughly with rubbing alcohol or soap and water. Warning Signs: If a red expanding bullseye rash or fever develops in the next 3 weeks, visit a doctor.

topic: Monsoon drinking water safety, chlorination tablets, water boiling guidelines
source_name: WHO - Water quality and health
content: During the monsoon season in Odisha, heavy rains frequently flood wells, tube wells, and open water bodies, causing widespread fecal contamination with cholera, typhoid, and viral hepatitis A/E pathogens. Protocol for Safe Water: 1. BOIL DRINKING WATER: Bring water to a ROLLING BOIL for at least 1 FULL MINUTE (this kills 100% of bacteria, viruses, and parasites); allow to cool naturally in a covered clean vessel. 2. CHLORINE TABLETS (Halazone / Chlorine): Dissolve 1 chlorine tablet (0.5 g) per 20 liters of clear water; stir well and wait 30 minutes before drinking. Store purified water in clean, narrow-mouthed covered containers with a tap; never dip bare hands into drinking water.

topic: Water trapped in ear after bath or swimming, plugged ear feeling
source_name: National Health Portal India - Ear health
content: Water entering the external ear canal during bathing or swimming can get trapped behind surface tension or a small wax barrier, causing a muffled sensation, sloshing sound, or tickling. Home Care: Tilt your head sideways toward the affected ear and gently pull your earlobe in different directions (downward and backward) to straighten the ear canal and allow gravity to drain the water. Create a gentle vacuum by cupping your palm firmly over the ear and releasing. Use a hairdryer on the lowest cool setting held 30 cm away from the ear for a few minutes. DO NOT insert cotton swabs, pins, or rolled cloth into the canal. Warning Signs: If pain, foul odor, or yellowish discharge develops after water exposure, visit a doctor for swimmer's ear.

topic: Earlobe tearing from heavy earrings, split earlobe care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Minor surgical conditions
content: Wearing heavy earrings or accidental pulling can gradually stretch or completely tear the soft earlobe piercing hole, causing a slit or split lobe. Home Care: Clean any fresh tear with soap and water and apply gentle pressure with clean gauze to stop bleeding. Avoid wearing earrings in the torn or stretched lobe to prevent complete bifurcation. Torn earlobes do not heal together naturally because skin grows over the edges of the split; a simple 15-minute minor outpatient surgical repair (lobuloplasty) under local anesthesia at a health centre can repair the split cleanly. Warning Signs: Redness, swelling, heat, or pus around the tear indicates a bacterial infection requiring antibiotic treatment.

topic: Red eyes from chlorine in swimming pool, chemical eye irritation
source_name: National Health Portal India - Eye safety
content: Chlorine and chloramines in swimming pool water strip away the eye's natural protective tear film, causing temporary redness, stinging, burning, and blurred vision after swimming. Home Care: Rinse eyes gently with cool, clean tap water or saline immediately after exiting the pool. Apply lubricating artificial tear drops to restore the tear film. Place a cool, damp washcloth over closed eyelids for 10 minutes. Wear snug-fitting swimming goggles when in pool water to prevent direct chemical contact. Avoid rubbing eyes. The redness typically resolves naturally within a few hours. Warning Signs: If severe pain, light sensitivity, or thick discharge persists the next day, consult an eye specialist.

topic: Nasal crusting and dry nose in winter, dry nasal mucosa
source_name: National Health Portal India - ENT health
content: Cold winter air and dry indoor drafts evaporate moisture from the nasal passages, causing dry, stinging nasal mucosa, hard crusts, and minor bleeding when blowing the nose. Home Care: Apply a tiny dab of plain petroleum jelly or coconut oil just inside the rim of each nostril using a clean cotton swab twice daily. Inhale warm steam for 5 minutes. Use a sterile saline nasal spray or drops to keep nasal membranes moist. Use a room humidifier or place a bowl of water near the bed. Avoid picking nasal crusts, which tears delicate capillaries and triggers nosebleeds. Drink adequate water throughout the day. Warning Signs: Persistent deep nasal sores or foul-smelling nasal crusting requires ENT evaluation.

topic: Sneezing fits when sweeping dust, dust mite allergic sneezing bouts
source_name: National Health Portal India - Allergy prevention
content: Sweeping dry household dust stirs up microscopic dust mite droppings and mold spores into the air, triggering acute allergic rhinitis with consecutive sneezing fits, watery eyes, and runny nose. Home Care: Avoid dry broom sweeping; use damp mopping to trap dust particles instead of dispersing them into the breathing zone. Wear a comfortable cloth mask while cleaning. Wash bedsheets, pillow covers, and curtains regularly in hot water and sun-dry thoroughly. Air out mattresses in direct hot sunlight for several hours. Rinse the nose with saline spray after cleaning to flush out inhaled allergens. Warning Signs: If dust exposure triggers chest tightness, wheezing, or difficulty breathing, evaluate for allergic asthma.

topic: Squatting vs sitting toilet posture, constipation and defecation mechanics
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive wellness
content: Defecation mechanics are heavily influenced by toilet posture. On a Western seated toilet, the puborectalis muscle remains partially cinched around the rectum at a 90-degree angle, requiring more straining. An Indian squatting posture (or using a footstool on a Western toilet to elevate knees above hips to a 35-degree angle) straightens the anorectal canal completely, allowing smooth, effortless bowel evacuation without straining. Home Care: Place a 6-to-8 inch footstool in front of the toilet to lift your knees above your hips. Lean slightly forward with elbows on knees. Never strain or hold breath; exhale gently while passing stool. Avoid spending more than 5 minutes on the toilet. Drink plenty of water and eat fibrous foods.

topic: Anal burning after spicy food, capsaicin rectal irritation
source_name: National Health Portal India - Gastrointestinal health
content: Capsaicin (the compound that gives red chilies and hot peppers their spicy heat) is not fully broken down by human digestive enzymes and passes through the entire gut intact, activating heat-sensitive TRPV1 pain receptors in the sensitive perianal skin during defecation, causing burning or stinging. Home Care: Wash the anal area gently with cool water after bowel movements instead of wiping with dry paper. Pat dry gently. Apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly, coconut oil, or zinc oxide cream to the perianal skin to create a soothing barrier. Drink a glass of cold milk, salted buttermilk (chaas), or eat curd (dahi), which contains casein that binds capsaicin. Moderate hot chili consumption. Warning Signs: If rectal bleeding, persistent throbbing, or fever occurs, visit a clinic.

topic: Nocturnal anal itching, pruritus ani, sweat and fungal hygiene
source_name: National Health Portal India - Colorectal care
content: Pruritus ani is an intense urge to scratch around the anal area, often worsening at night in bed, caused by trapped perspiration, Candida fungal overgrowth, residual stool moisture, or pinworms in children. Home Care: Clean the perianal area gently with plain water after bowel movements and pat completely dry with a soft towel or hairdryer on cool setting. Wear loose-fitting, breathable 100% cotton underwear and change daily. Avoid scented toilet wipes, harsh soaps, and synthetic tight underwear. Apply plain zinc oxide cream. Resist scratching, as scratching creates micro-tears and secondary bacterial infections. In children, check for thread-like pinworms at night. Warning Signs: If severe redness, cracks, or bleeding persists beyond a week, consult a clinic.

topic: Water brash, sudden mouth filling with sour saliva, acid reflux symptom
source_name: National Health Portal India - Digestive health
content: Water brash is the sudden, reflex filling of the mouth with excessive watery, slightly sour or salty saliva, triggered when stomach acid regurgitates into the lower esophagus and activates salivary gland reflexes in an attempt to dilute and neutralize the acid. Home Care: Swallow the saliva or spit it out and drink half a glass of warm water to rinse the esophagus. Sit upright and avoid lying down flat. Avoid eating heavy, oily, or highly spiced meals. Avoid tea, coffee, chocolate, and carbonated beverages. Eat smaller, frequent meals. Elevate the head of the bed by 6 inches during sleep. If water brash occurs regularly, consult a physician for antacid or proton pump inhibitor evaluation.

topic: Curvy road motion sickness in Odisha ghats, bus travel nausea remedies
source_name: National Health Portal India - Travel health
content: Traveling through winding ghat roads (such as Kalinga Ghat or Similipal) frequently induces severe motion sickness due to rapid vestibular acceleration signals conflicting with visual cues. Home Care: Sit near the front of the bus or in the front passenger seat of a car where motion is minimized. Focus your gaze far ahead on the distant road or horizon—do NOT read books or look down at mobile screens. Keep the vehicle window cracked open for a steady stream of fresh cool air. Chew on crystallized ginger or sip ginger tea before departure. Eat a light, non-greasy snack 1 hour before travel (do not travel on an entirely empty or overly full stomach). Sip cool water in small amounts. Wear acupressure wristbands.

topic: Shaky hands from skipping meals, hunger shakiness, physiological hypoglycemia
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nutrition and metabolic health
content: Skipping meals or fasting for prolonged hours causes blood glucose levels to drop, prompting the body to release adrenaline (epinephrine) to liberate stored glycogen from the liver, which causes shaky hands, rapid heartbeats, irritability ('hangry'), sweating, and mild dizziness. Home Care: Eat or drink a balanced source of carbohydrates immediately: a banana, a glass of milk, a small handful of nuts with fruit, or a proper meal with rice and dal. Sit down and rest for 10-15 minutes until blood sugar stabilizes. Establish regular meal hours and avoid going more than 4 to 5 hours without nutritious food during the day. Carry a healthy snack when traveling. Warning Signs: If shakiness occurs despite eating, or is accompanied by confusion or fainting, consult a doctor to evaluate for endocrine conditions.

topic: Shoulder knot pain, myofascial trigger point, upper back muscle knot from desk work
source_name: National Health Portal India - Musculoskeletal health
content: A muscle knot (myofascial trigger point) in the trapezius or rhomboid muscle between the spine and shoulder blade is a localized band of tight, contracted muscle fibers caused by prolonged computer desk sitting, forward-head posture, stress, or carrying a heavy one-sided shoulder bag. Home Care: Apply a warm heating pad or warm towel to the shoulder for 15-20 minutes. Place a tennis ball between your shoulder blade and a wall, leaning gently against it to apply targeted self-massage pressure to the knot for 60 seconds while taking slow breaths. Perform gentle neck and shoulder rolls. Adjust desk ergonomics: monitor at eye level, elbows supported. Take 2-minute movement breaks every hour.

topic: Heavy aching legs in the evening, occupational leg fatigue from standing
source_name: National Health Portal India - Occupational health
content: Standing or sitting for prolonged hours at work (shopkeepers, teachers, traffic police, desk workers) causes gravity to pool venous blood and lymph fluid in the calves and ankles, leading to a heavy, dull ache, tiredness, and mild evening foot puffiness. Home Care: Lie down with legs elevated on 2 pillows above heart level for 20 minutes upon returning home. Take a warm foot bath. While standing at work, do periodic heel-to-toe rocking exercises to activate the calf muscle venous pump. Take short walking breaks every 45 minutes. Wear supportive, cushioned flat shoes with arch support. Wear graduated compression socks during working hours. Stay adequately hydrated throughout the day.

topic: Toe cramp, sudden painful toe curl spasm, foot muscle cramp
source_name: National Health Portal India - Foot health
content: A sudden toe cramp happens when the small intrinsic muscles of the foot or tendons in the toes suddenly contract into a painful, locked spasm (often curling the toes downward), triggered by muscle fatigue, dehydration, tight narrow shoes, or electrolyte shifts. Home Care: Stand up immediately and put weight on the foot on a flat, firm floor. Gently use your hands to pull the cramped toes backward and upward toward your shin to stretch the contracted muscle. Massage the arch of the foot and base of the toes firmly. Apply a warm towel or warm water. Drink a glass of water or electrolyte fluid. Wear shoes with a wide toe box that allows toes to spread naturally. Stretch your feet before going to sleep.

topic: Glass sliver or glass shard in foot, fine glass fragment first aid
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid trauma
content: Stepping on a broken glass fragment or bottle shard can embed tiny, transparent, painful glass slivers in the sole of the foot or hand, causing sharp pain every time pressure is applied. First Aid: Wash the area gently with soap and warm water without pressing down hard (pressing can push the glass deeper into muscle tissue). Sterilize fine-tipped tweezers with rubbing alcohol. Under bright lighting, inspect the sliver; if the end protrudes above the skin, grasp it firmly with the tweezers and pull it straight out along the path of entry. Do not dig deeply with needles. Wash the wound again, apply antiseptic, and dress with a sterile bandage. Warning Signs: If the glass is deeply embedded, near a joint, cannot be gripped, or feels numb, visit a clinic for safe removal.

topic: Cracked rough elbows and knees, hyperkeratosis of extensor skin
source_name: National Health Portal India - Skin care
content: Skin on the elbows and knees is naturally thicker, contains fewer oil glands, and is subjected to constant bending and friction, making it prone to developing rough, dark, dry, and scaly calloused skin. Home Care: Apply a thick, intensive moisturizer containing urea, lactic acid, or pure petroleum jelly immediately after bathing while the skin is damp. Use a mild soap-free cleanser. Gently buff the area with a washcloth during warm baths (avoid rough pumice scrubbing which causes reactive skin thickening). Avoid resting elbows on rough, hard desk surfaces. Wear soft cotton sleeves. Drink plenty of water. The roughness softens and normalizes over a few weeks of consistent daily moisturizing.

topic: Leukonychia, harmless white spots or dots on fingernails
source_name: National Health Portal India - Nail health
content: Small, isolated white spots or lines across the fingernail plate (punctate leukonychia) are extremely common and almost universally caused by minor, forgotten micro-trauma to the nail matrix at the base of the cuticle (such as tapping nails, bumping fingers, or aggressive manicures). They are NOT caused by calcium deficiency or vitamin shortage. Home Care: White spots are completely harmless and require no treatment, medication, or supplements. As the fingernail grows forward, the white spot simply moves outward toward the fingertip and will be clipped off naturally over 4 to 6 months. Protect nails from trauma and keep cuticles moisturized. Warning Signs: If the entire nail turns milky white (total leukonychia), consult a physician to check liver and kidney function.

topic: Bruised fingernail from hammer blow, crushed fingertip trauma
source_name: National Health Portal India - First aid trauma
content: Accidentally striking a fingertip with a hammer or slamming it in a car door crushes small capillaries beneath the nail, leading to a subungual hematoma with throbbing pain, localized swelling, and purple-black discoloration under the nail plate. First Aid: Immediately apply an ice pack wrapped in a clean cloth for 15-20 minutes to reduce pain and internal bleeding. Keep the hand elevated above the level of the heart to minimize throbbing. Check the fingertip for open cuts. If the pooled blood covers less than a quarter of the nail and the bone is not tender, the nail will heal naturally and grow out. Warning Signs: If the fingertip is visibly deformed, unable to straighten, or throbbing pain is agonizing, visit a clinic for an X-ray to check for a distal phalanx fracture.

topic: Swallowed fishbone sensation without visible bone, throat mucosal scratch
source_name: National Health Portal India - ENT conditions
content: Frequently, a sharp fishbone scratches the delicate mucous membrane of the throat as it goes down into the stomach, leaving an abrasion that continues to feel exactly like a bone is still stuck even though the bone has already passed safely into the digestive tract. Home Care: Sip warm water, olive oil, or eat a small piece of soft banana. Gargle with warm salt water to soothe the scratched mucosal lining. The scratch sensation naturally fades within 24 to 48 hours. DO NOT force dry lumps of rice or dry bread down, which can worsen tissue scratches. Warning Signs: If you have true difficulty swallowing, drooling, inability to swallow liquids, fever, or pain radiating to the chest, visit an ENT specialist immediately for endoscopic examination.

topic: Blister beetle dermatitis, potu rash, Nairobi fly burn in Odisha
source_name: WHO - Environmental health and toxicology
content: Blister beetles (Paederus beetles / 'potu') are common in Odisha during monsoon and post-monsoon months near bright lights. When a beetle crawls on the skin, crushing or slapping it releases 'pederin', a potent blistering toxin that causes a linear, fiery red chemical burn with multiple fluid-filled blisters appearing 12 to 24 hours later ('kissing lesions' where skin touches). FIRST AID: If a beetle is on your skin, DO NOT CRUSH OR SLAP IT—blow it away gently or let it walk onto a piece of paper. If crushed against skin, wash the area immediately and thoroughly with soap and water. Apply cold wet compresses and calamine lotion. Do not burst blisters. Lesions heal over 10-14 days. Warning Signs: If toxin enters the eyes (Nairobi eye), seek emergency ophthalmic irrigation.

topic: Vitamin C deficiency, scurvy signs, bleeding swollen gums, easy bruising
source_name: WHO - Micronutrient deficiencies: Vitamin C
content: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is vital for collagen synthesis, capillary integrity, and wound healing. Severe deficiency causes scurvy: swollen bleeding gums, loose teeth, tiny pinpoint skin hemorrhages (petechiae), corkscrew body hairs, slow-healing wounds, and severe fatigue. Home Care: Consume fresh Vitamin C-rich fruits and vegetables daily: Indian gooseberry (amla - one of the richest natural sources), guavas, lemons, oranges, tomatoes, drumstick leaves, and capsicum. Heat destroys Vitamin C, so eat fruits raw or lightly steamed. Scurvy responds rapidly to daily dietary Vitamin C or oral ascorbic acid tablets. Warning Signs: Extensive skin bruising or severe joint bleeding requires medical evaluation.

topic: Iodine deficiency, simple goiter, neck thyroid swelling prevention
source_name: MoHFW India - National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme
content: Iodine is an essential trace mineral required by the thyroid gland to produce thyroid hormones controlling metabolism and fetal brain development. Deficiency causes compensatory enlargement of the thyroid gland (goiter, visible swelling at the base of the neck), lethargy, and cretinism in children. Protocol: Use IODIZED SALT (marked with the smiling sun logo) for all household cooking as mandated under the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme. Store iodized salt in a covered plastic or glass jar away from moisture and direct sunlight. Add salt toward the end of cooking to preserve iodine. Warning Signs: Rapidly enlarging neck mass, hoarseness of voice, or difficulty swallowing requires thyroid clinic evaluation.

topic: Dietary fiber guidelines, 30g daily fiber, digestive motility and heart health
source_name: WHO - Healthy diet fact sheet
content: Dietary fiber (both soluble and insoluble) is essential for normal bowel motility, feeding beneficial gut microbiome bacteria, preventing constipation, and lowering blood cholesterol and glucose spikes. Recommended intake is at least 25 to 30 grams daily for adults. Home Care: Increase fiber gradually to prevent temporary bloating: eat whole wheat flour (atta with bran), brown rice, millets (ragi, bajra), lentils (dal), chickpeas, beans, green leafy vegetables, papayas, and apples with skin. Drink plenty of water (at least 8 to 10 glasses daily) alongside high-fiber foods to ensure smooth, soft stools. Soluble fiber (oats, psyllium / isabgol) binds bile acids to lower LDL cholesterol naturally.

topic: Salt reduction guidelines, WHO 5 grams daily sodium limit, high blood pressure prevention
source_name: WHO - Salt reduction fact sheet
content: Excess dietary salt (sodium) is a leading cause of hypertension, strokes, and cardiovascular deaths globally. The World Health Organization recommends consuming LESS THAN 5 GRAMS OF SALT (about 1 level teaspoon) per day across all meals for adults. Home Care: Do not add extra table salt to already cooked food. Reduce consumption of high-sodium foods: papads, salted pickles (achaar), namkeen snacks, instant noodles, and packaged chips. Flavor food with natural spices, herbs, garlic, ginger, and lemon juice instead of extra salt. Gradually reducing salt allows taste buds to adapt within 2 to 3 weeks.

topic: Sugar reduction, free sugars limit, preventing childhood obesity and cavities
source_name: WHO - Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children
content: Free sugars (added sugars in food and beverages plus sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, and fruit juices) increase risks of dental cavities, unhealthy weight gain, fatty liver, and type 2 diabetes. WHO recommends keeping free sugars below 5% to 10% of total daily energy intake (less than 6 teaspoons of sugar daily for adults). Home Care: Drink plain clean water instead of sugary carbonated sodas, sweetened fruit drinks, or commercial energy drinks. Limit sugar added to daily tea and coffee. Replace sweets and bakery pastries with whole fresh seasonal fruits (bananas, guavas, oranges). Check food labels for hidden sugars (sucrose, high-fructose corn syrup, dextrose).

topic: Daily physical activity guidelines, 150 minutes weekly aerobic exercise
source_name: WHO - Physical activity fact sheet
content: Regular physical activity is vital for cardiovascular health, mental well-being, weight maintenance, and reducing risks of hypertension, diabetes, and colon cancer. WHO recommends that all adults engage in at least 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise (e.g., 30 minutes of brisk walking 5 days a week) or 75 minutes of vigorous exercise weekly. Home Care: Incorporate brisk walking, cycling, swimming, gardening, or household chores into daily routines. Perform muscle-strengthening exercises involving major muscle groups twice weekly. Break up long periods of sitting by standing or walking for 2 minutes every hour. Start slowly and build duration gradually.

topic: Menstrual hygiene management, sanitary pad safety and disposal in Odisha
source_name: MoHFW India - Menstrual Hygiene Scheme guidelines
content: Proper menstrual hygiene prevents pelvic inflammatory infections, cervical irritation, and reproductive tract infections. Protocol: Change sanitary pads or clean cloth napkins every 4 to 6 hours, regardless of how light the flow is, to prevent bacterial multiplication. If using reusable cloth, wash thoroughly with soap and clean water and dry in DIRECT HOT SUNSHINE (sunlight is a natural disinfectant); never dry cloths in dark, damp bathroom corners. Wash the genital area with plain water from front to back. Dispose of used pads wrapped in newspaper in designated waste bins—never flush pads down the toilet or burn them in open pits.

topic: Heavy menstrual bleeding, menorrhagia, soaking more than one pad an hour warning
source_name: WHO - Sexual and reproductive health
content: Menorrhagia is abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding (bleeding lasting more than 7 days, or needing to change one or more sanitary pads every hour for several consecutive hours, or passing large blood clots larger than a coin), commonly caused by uterine fibroids, adenomyosis, polyps, or hormonal imbalances. Home Care: Rest during heavy days. Stay well-hydrated. Consume iron-rich foods (green leafy vegetables, jaggery, lentils, eggs) to compensate for menstrual blood loss. Take daily Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) tablets under doctor guidance. Warning Signs: Dizziness upon standing, pale skin, extreme fatigue, or sudden flooding requires emergency gynecological evaluation.

topic: Irregular menstrual cycles, oligomenorrhea, missed period lifestyle factors
source_name: National Health Portal India - Women's health
content: A normal menstrual cycle ranges from 21 to 35 days. Cycles that vary widely, occur less frequently than every 35 days, or stop intermittently can be caused by significant psychological stress, sudden weight loss or gain, extreme physical over-exercising, thyroid dysfunction, or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Home Care: In sexually active women, the first step for a missed period is always taking a home urine pregnancy test. Maintain a balanced diet with adequate calories and healthy fats. Practice stress reduction techniques (yoga, walking, meditation). Maintain a consistent sleep schedule. Avoid crash dieting. Warning Signs: If periods stop for more than 3 consecutive months (amenorrhea), or are accompanied by severe pelvic pain or excess facial hair, consult a gynecologist.

topic: Endometriosis awareness, severe chronic pelvic pain, painful intercourse, dyspareunia
source_name: WHO - Endometriosis fact sheet
content: Endometriosis is a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus (endometrium) grows outside the uterus on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, and pelvic peritoneum, causing chronic inflammation, scarring, and adhesions. Symptoms: Severe, debilitating period pain that does not respond to common pain relief, deep pelvic pain during or after sexual intercourse (dyspareunia), painful bowel movements during menstruation, and difficulty conceiving. Home Care: Apply a warm heating pad to the lower abdomen and lower back. Engage in gentle low-impact walking and pelvic stretches. Maintain a nutritious anti-inflammatory diet. Consult a gynecologist for clinical ultrasound and specialized medical management.

topic: Pelvic inflammatory disease, PID warning signs, lower abdominal pain and fever
source_name: WHO - Sexually transmitted infections
content: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is an infection of the female upper reproductive organs (uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries), commonly resulting from untreated sexually transmitted bacteria (chlamydia, gonorrhea) ascending from the vagina. Symptoms: Dull, persistent ache in the lower abdomen and pelvis, unusual heavy foul-smelling vaginal discharge, bleeding between periods or after sex, painful urination, and fever with chills. Protocol: PID is a SERIOUS condition that can cause permanent tubal scarring and infertility if untreated; visit a Community Health Centre or gynecologist immediately for prescription antibiotic therapy. Ensure your sexual partner is treated simultaneously to prevent re-infection. Complete all antibiotics.

topic: Atrophic vaginitis, vaginal dryness after menopause, painful intimacy
source_name: National Health Portal India - Menopausal health
content: Atrophic vaginitis (genitourinary syndrome of menopause) is thinning, drying, and inflammation of the vaginal walls caused by declining natural estrogen levels after menopause, causing vaginal dryness, itching, burning during urination, and discomfort or pain during intercourse. Home Care: Use water-based or silicone-based over-the-counter vaginal lubricants during intercourse to eliminate friction. Apply non-hormonal vaginal moisturizers regularly 2 to 3 times weekly to restore tissue hydration. Avoid perfumed soaps, bubble baths, and douches that irritate dry mucosa. Wear loose breathable cotton underwear. Consult a gynecologist for prescription low-dose topical vaginal estrogen cream, which safely restores tissue thickness.

topic: Varicocele, bag of worms scrotum swelling, dull testicular ache
source_name: National Health Portal India - Men's reproductive health
content: A varicocele is an abnormal enlargement and pooling of blood in the pampiniform plexus of veins inside the scrotum (most commonly on the left side, due to renal vein drainage angle), often described as feeling like a soft 'bag of worms' above the testicle, accompanied by a dull, dragging scrotal ache that worsens with prolonged standing or heavy lifting. Home Care: Wear a supportive athletic supporter or snug cotton briefs to support scrotal weight and ease venous tension. Avoid prolonged standing when possible. Apply cool compresses if uncomfortable. Varicoceles are benign; however, they can affect sperm quality and fertility. Warning Signs: Sudden rapid scrotal enlargement, sharp severe pain, or a firm testicular lump requires urgent urological evaluation.

topic: Hydrocele in men, painless fluid swelling around testicle, surgical cure
source_name: National Health Portal India - Urological conditions
content: A hydrocele is an accumulation of clear serous fluid within the tunica vaginalis sheath surrounding a testicle, causing painless, gradual swelling of one or both sides of the scrotum. The scrotum feels smooth, heavy, and transilluminates brightly when a light torch is held against it in a dark room. Home Care: Small hydroceles in adults that cause no discomfort do not require urgent treatment. Wear supportive underwear to relieve heaviness. NEVER attempt to drain a hydrocele with a needle at home, which introduces life-threatening bacterial infections. Government District Hospitals in Odisha provide safe, definitive minor surgical repair (hydrocelectomy) completely free. Warning Signs: Sudden painful swelling or redness requires emergency checkup to rule out torsion.

topic: Male pattern hair loss, androgenetic alopecia, receding hairline care
source_name: National Health Portal India - Dermatology
content: Male pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia) is a progressive, genetically determined thinning of scalp hair driven by dihydrotestosterone (DHT) sensitivity, classically starting with a receding hairline at the temples and thinning at the crown (vertex). Home Care: Male pattern baldness is a cosmetic condition and does not affect physical health. Handle hair gently: avoid aggressive towel-drying, tight pulling, and harsh chemical treatments. Wash scalp with gentle shampoo. Maintain a nutritious balanced diet with adequate protein, iron, and zinc. Certified medical treatments like topical minoxidil or oral finasteride can slow progression and promote regrowth under a dermatologist's supervision.

topic: Ascariasis, large roundworm infection in children, abdominal pain and poor appetite
source_name: WHO - Soil-transmitted helminthiases
content: Ascariasis is an intestinal infection caused by the large parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides, spread when food or hands contaminated with soil containing microscopic worm eggs are ingested. Symptoms include vague belly pain, bloating, nausea, poor appetite, malnutrition, and occasionally live worms passed in stool or vomited. Protocol: All children aged 1 to 19 years in Odisha should receive bi-annual deworming with single-dose Albendazole (400 mg) distributed free at schools and Anganwadi centers on National Deworming Day. Home Care: Wash hands thoroughly with soap before eating and after using the toilet. Wash and peel all raw fruits and vegetables. Wear shoes outdoors to prevent soil contamination. Warning Signs: Severe vomiting, belly swelling, or complete bowel obstruction requires emergency hospital care.

topic: Giardiasis, water-borne parasite, foul sulfur burps, greasy floating diarrhea
source_name: WHO - Waterborne parasites
content: Giardiasis is an intestinal infection caused by the microscopic protozoan parasite Giardia duodenalis, acquired by drinking contaminated stream, river, or well water, causing foul-smelling greasy diarrhea that floats, intense abdominal bloating, stomach cramps, nausea, and characteristic sulfur-tasting ('rotten egg') burps. Protocol: Giardiasis requires stool examination and specific prescription anti-protozoal medications (like metronidazole or tinidazole). Hydrate with clean, safe water and ORS. Boil all drinking water for at least 1 full minute to kill chlorine-resistant Giardia cysts. Wash hands thoroughly. Avoid dairy temporarily if secondary lactose intolerance occurs.

topic: Japanese encephalitis, JE virus, Culex mosquito, monsoon brain fever warning
source_name: WHO - Japanese encephalitis fact sheet
content: Japanese encephalitis (JE) is a serious viral brain infection transmitted by night-biting Culex mosquitoes breeding in flooded rice paddies and stagnant rural water bodies, with pigs and wading birds acting as amplifying hosts. Symptoms: Sudden high fever, severe headache, stiff neck, vomiting, mental confusion, tremors, convulsions, and coma. Protocol: Vaccination against Japanese Encephalitis is provided under the Universal Immunization Programme in endemic districts of Odisha. Prevention: Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets (LLIN), wear full-sleeved clothing during evening hours, install window mesh screens, and relocate pig shelters away from residential homes.
